claim_boundary: Every taxonomy subtheme has a synthesis record. Family evidence currently comes from the analyst-reviewed D2/D3 seed and does not represent the full corpus.

records.subtheme_name: How bodies make voiced and unvoiced sound
records.question: Which parts of the signal come from the source and which from the moving vocal tract?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech reaches a microphone as changing air pressure after vocal-fold vibration, mouth shape, room reflections, and electronics have already mixed together. The subtheme asks: Which parts of the signal come from the source and which from the moving vocal tract?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with periodic vocal-fold source, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Not every speech segment is periodic: frication, stops, breath, and irregular phonation cannot be reduced to one stable pitch.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make periodic vocal-fold source, vocal-tract filtering, articulatory coordination explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Build a finite-element model with dual sources and vary tract geometry to connect physical parameters to observed bandwidth and resonance.
subtheme_boundary: Not every speech segment is periodic: frication, stops, breath, and irregular phonation cannot be reduced to one stable pitch.
A filter-only explanation misses changes caused directly by source irregularity, radiation, or recording conditions.
A label such as a phoneme is not itself a physical movement or a complete account of coarticulation.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Analysis of Avian Biphonic Vocalization Using Computational Modelling: The paper models a dual avian sound source and upper vocal tract to explain how physical geometry produces biphonic spectral structure.; Vocal-tract model with two directions: Static design for a dummy head and dynamic design for a speaking machine: Physical static and dynamic vocal-tract models expose how geometry and articulation shape sound.; Reconstruction of the Complete Vocal Tract Contour Through Acoustic to Articulatory Inversion Using Real-Time MRI Data: The paper infers coordinated vocal-tract movement from acoustic evidence; it is about the physical source/filter relationship, not ordinary word recognition.; Enhancing Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Multi-Target Pretraining for Low-Resource Settings: Multi-target pretraining uses linguistic and articulatory labels to make acoustic-to-articulatory inversion useful under scarce paired data and lower inference cost.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Build a finite-element model with dual sources and vary tract geometry to connect physical parameters to observed bandwidth and resonance.
Show the two ends of the design space: a fixed one-vowel dummy head and a cam-driven model whose blocks change shape in real time.
Train acoustic-to-articulatory models against complete vocal-tract contours from real-time MRI and compare individual and joint articulator prediction.

Pretrain the inversion model against three related targets—phoneme labels, articulatory features, and critical articulator labels—so it receives useful structure without carrying the external extractor at deployment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Analysis of Avian Biphonic Vocalization Using Computational Modelling
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a finite-element model with dual sources and vary tract geometry to connect physical parameters to observed bandwidth and resonance.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A reconstructed syrinx and upper tract are represented in COMSOL; source placement and geometric parameters are changed, then simulated vocalizations are compared with recordings of real birds.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: COMSOL frequency-domain pressure-acoustics simulations vary tracheal length, glottis radius, and beak angle; simulated resonance peaks are compared with house-sparrow and domestic-canary vocalizations. The reported comparison is spectral/formant frequency and SPL behavior, not a human-listener denominator.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports experimentally validated biphonic simulations and systematic effects of tract geometry on resonance modulation and syllable bandwidth.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports experimentally validated biphonic simulations and systematic effects of tract geometry on resonance modulation and syllable bandwidth.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The model concerns avian vocalization rather than human speech; micro-CT reconstruction, source assumptions, and validation recordings constrain the result. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Vocal-tract model with two directions: Static design for a dummy head and dynamic design for a speaking machine
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Show the two ends of the design space: a fixed one-vowel dummy head and a cam-driven model whose blocks change shape in real time.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The static model fixes one tract configuration and radiates a repeatable vowel; the dynamic model uses blocks and cams to change simulated articulators and tract shape.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Physical models of the human vocal tract have been developed for many purposes, including education in acoustics and phonetics, speech and language pathology, and speech science/technology.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper demonstrates both models and argues that static and dynamic versions serve different education, phonetics, pathology, and technology purposes.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper demonstrates both models and argues that static and dynamic versions serve different education, phonetics, pathology, and technology purposes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: This is a two-page demonstration with no shared quantitative evaluation or claim of human-speech equivalence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Reconstruction of the Complete Vocal Tract Contour Through Acoustic to Articulatory Inversion Using Real-Time MRI Data
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train acoustic-to-articulatory models against complete vocal-tract contours from real-time MRI and compare individual and joint articulator prediction.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper reconstructs the complete vocal-tract contour from acoustic input using real-time MRI data and bidirectional recurrent models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The average RMSE precision on the test set is 1.65 mm to be compared with the pixel size which is 1.62 mm.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports average contour RMSE near the MRI pixel size on its test set.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports average contour RMSE near the MRI pixel size on its test set.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speakers, MRI protocol, segmentation, speech styles, and model assumptions limit generalization; contour accuracy is not a complete articulatory theory.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Enhancing Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Multi-Target Pretraining for Low-Resource Settings
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Pretrain the inversion model against three related targets—phoneme labels, articulatory features, and critical articulator labels—so it receives useful structure without carrying the external extractor at deployment.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model maps acoustic features to articulatory trajectories. During pretraining it predicts phonemic, broad articulatory, and critical-articulator targets; it is then fine-tuned with different amounts of paired data and compared with a baseline and SSL-feature systems on seen and unseen speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate our approach against both baseline and SSL-based models across various data conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports consistent AAI improvement, including low-resource gains; the strongest reported unseen-speaker configuration reaches CC 0.8612 and RMSE 1.1023, while inference avoids the external SSL extractor.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports consistent AAI improvement, including low-resource gains; the strongest reported unseen-speaker configuration reaches CC 0.8612 and RMSE 1.1023, while inference avoids the external SSL extractor.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The articulatory targets, speakers, language, and feature choices define the tested boundary; predicted movement is not equivalent to direct imaging. Reported gains and speed claims are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Articulatory modeling of the S-shaped F2 trajectories observed in Öhman's spectrographic analysis of VCV syllables
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate the same VCV sequences with an articulatory model, separate vowel transitions from consonant influence, and compare the resulting trajectories and locus equations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study uses the Maeda articulatory model to reproduce Öhman's S-shaped F2 trajectories and reassesses conventional locus-equation interpretations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The computational articulatory model generates 75 VCV syllables over five vowels and four consonant configurations, computes F1–F3 trajectories with a transmission-line model, and compares synthetic F2/F3 transition clusters with aggregated Öhman observations. The evaluation is geometric/formant trajectory agreement, not a listener or recognition study.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports synthetic trajectories resembling the observed sequences and structured effects of articulatory planning.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports synthetic trajectories resembling the observed sequences and structured effects of articulatory planning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Model geometry, trajectory planning, corpus, and synthetic-to-observed comparison limit claims; matching a trajectory does not identify a unique human motor plan.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Evaluation of a model for sound radiation from the vocal tract wall
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent each tract section as a damped spring-mass system and fit wall parameters to real speaker voicebars.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The simulated radiation from tube sections is compared with six speakers producing /b,d,g/ in vowel contexts, with parameters optimized to real spectra.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study evaluated a simulation model for sound radiation from the vocal tract wall in the context of articulatory speech synthesis.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 2.26–3.82 dB RMSE from 0–800 Hz and concludes the simple model can reproduce the spectra closely.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 2.26–3.82 dB RMSE from 0–800 Hz and concludes the simple model can reproduce the spectra closely.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The six speakers, selected consonants/vowels, frequency range, and fitted parameters bound the claim; other speech sounds and independent physical validation remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Influence of wall coverings of 3D-printed vocal tract models on measured transfer functions
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Dampen or mechanically constrain the replica and test whether the expected resonances become cleaner and more repeatable.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Ten axisymmetric 3D-printed vowel tubes are measured with reciprocity; sound-absorbing fabric and sand embedding are compared as artifact-reduction methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this empirical study, two methods to reduce these artifacts were compared, namely wrapping the models with sound-absorbing fabric and embedding the models in sand.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Both coverings reduce spurious poles and zeros and improve repeatability of the measured transfer functions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Both coverings reduce spurious poles and zeros and improve repeatability of the measured transfer functions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Printed geometries, ten vowels, materials, reciprocity setup, and repeatability metric bound the claim; improved measurement does not prove the replica matches a human tract.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speech Reduction in French: The Relationship Between Vowel Space and Articulation Dynamics
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Model spatial vowel distinctiveness and temporal rate together and test whether their interaction predicts non-lexicalized reductions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: French spontaneous speech is measured with pVSA, VDI, articulation rate, and temporally compressed speech zones.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The study extracts 113,296 French oral vowels from eight hours of Corpus of Interactional Data, retains 112,346 after duration filtering, and identifies 6,373 in reduced sequences. Lobanov-normalized formants support pVSA, vowel-distinctiveness, and reduction-rate analyses across speakers and conversational contexts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Smaller vowel space predicts more reduction only when articulation rate is included; rate is the strongest predictor and VDI is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Smaller vowel space predicts more reduction only when articulation rate is included; rate is the strongest predictor and VDI is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The French speakers, spontaneous tasks, reduction definition, and acoustic measures bound the result; other languages and conversational settings remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Equivalence and differences: Formant patterns of labialization and pharyngealization in Tashlhiyt
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare adjacent-vowel formants across both articulations, vowel qualities, and speakers, then identify which formants preserve their difference.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Thirty-five Tashlhiyt speakers produce VCV logatomes with /i, a, u/ and labialized or pharyngealized consonants; F1 and F2 patterns are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The analysis of VCV logatomes containing /i, a, u/ produced by 35 Tashlhiyt speakers revealed that both secondary articulations show equivalent patterns related to F2, which are strongest in /i/, followed by /a/, whereas differences between labialization and pharyngealization depend mainly on F1 and vowel quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Both articulations show similar F2 effects, strongest for /i/ and then /a/, while differences depend on F1 and vowel quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Both articulations show similar F2 effects, strongest for /i/ and then /a/, while differences depend on F1 and vowel quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The language, speakers, logatomes, adjacent vowels, and formant measures bound the result; formants alone cannot identify every articulatory gesture.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Phonetic Posteriorgram-Based Phoneme Selection for Vocal Cord Disorder Classification in Continuous Mandarin Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use phonetic posteriorgrams to identify informative phoneme segments, then classify vocal-cord disorders from the selected evidence.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes phonetic-posteriorgram-based phoneme selection for vocal-cord-disorder classification in continuous Mandarin speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Results show a 15% accuracy improvement over a baseline model that ignores phonetic context and a prior study on the same patients using single-word utterances and sustained vowels.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports classification results for the selected phonetic evidence on continuous Mandarin speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports classification results for the selected phonetic evidence on continuous Mandarin speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Cohort, disorder labels, language, transcript quality, phoneme selection, and recording conditions limit clinical generalization; classification is not diagnosis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Study of vocal fold vibration using M-mode ultrasound: a proof of concept
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use M-mode ultrasound along the larynx and compare its fundamental-frequency estimate with simultaneous voice analysis.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Spatio-temporal maps of the fundamental and second harmonic are compared with median f0 from recordings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To validate our method, 108 recordings (MUS and voice) from 12 healthy subjects were acquired.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports close agreement and reveals temporal drift; four high-pitched recordings expose aliasing.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports close agreement and reveals temporal drift; four high-pitched recordings expose aliasing.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The 500-Hz rate, probe placement, healthy participants, and excluded aliased cases limit clinical and high-pitch claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Hybrid Expert Knowledge and Self-Supervised Learning for Diagnostic Modeling of Adductor Spasmodic and Primary Myotonic Dysphonia
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine expert-designed voice measures with representations learned directly from the waveform.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A CNN receives handcrafted features and self-supervised waveform representations and predicts ADSD versus pMTD on a newly collected patient dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This marks the first application of deep learning techniques to ADSD and pMTD diagnostic modeling, achieving a classification accuracy of 83.3% on our newly constructed dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 83.3% classification accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 83.3% classification accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is tied to the constructed dataset, its patient mix, and the two diagnoses; clinical deployment, calibration, and external validation remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: PERCEPT-US: A Multimodal American English Child Speech Corpus Specialized for Articulatory Feedback
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a multimodal American English child-speech corpus specialized for articulatory feedback, with synchronized speech and articulatory information.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: PERCEPT-US provides a multimodal child speech corpus designed for articulatory feedback.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present PERCEPT-US, a multimodal corpus of audio and ultrasound data from 126 American English-speaking children ages 8 to 17.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports corpus resources and articulatory-feedback-oriented evaluation for American English child speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports corpus resources and articulatory-feedback-oriented evaluation for American English child speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speakers, ages, tasks, sensor alignment, labels, and corpus size limit generalization; a resource does not itself establish learning or clinical benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Creaky Voice Facilitates More Efficient Phonological Processing of Mandarin Tone 3
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Test whether creaky voice changes the time and accuracy of Tone 3 processing, separating phonological benefit from general listening difficulty.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies how creaky voice facilitates more efficient phonological processing of Mandarin Tone 3.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: While most studies explore creaky voice in tone recognition behaviorally, its neural processing remains unclear.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports behavioral evidence that creaky voice can facilitate Tone 3 processing in the tested Mandarin stimuli.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports behavioral evidence that creaky voice can facilitate Tone 3 processing in the tested Mandarin stimuli.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Listeners, stimuli, tone context, creak manipulation, and task bound the claim; a processing benefit is not a universal production or perception rule.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Acoustic similarities, articulatory uniqueness: Speech production mechanisms in individuals with congenital lip paralysis
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare acoustic similarity with articulatory measurements in individuals with congenital lip paralysis to identify compensatory production mechanisms.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies acoustic similarities and articulatory uniqueness in speech production by individuals with congenital lip paralysis.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The articulatory/acoustic comparison uses 590 tokens from 97 French disyllabic target words produced by three women with Moebius syndrome and three controls. Forced-aligned duration, F1–F3 at vowel midpoint, and tongue/lip sensor x/y/z positions are compared between accented and unaccented vowels using Bayesian regressions with vowel, state, interaction, and by-speaker intercepts. Four chains of 4,000 iterations and 95% HDIs with a standardized [-0.1,0.1] ROPE define clear differences versus tendencies.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports acoustic and articulatory findings for the affected speakers and comparison conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports acoustic and articulatory findings for the affected speakers and comparison conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Cohort, anatomy, language, tasks, imaging or motion measures, and acoustic metrics limit clinical generalization; similarity is not a diagnosis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Articulatory variations in Apical Vowels in Southwestern Mandarin
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure articulatory variation in apical vowels and relate it to acoustic outcomes across Southwestern Mandarin speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper analyzes articulatory variations in apical vowels in Southwestern Mandarin.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Data were collected from seven speakers in their twenties, focusing apical vowels, the high vowel [i], and their er-suffixed forms.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports articulatory variation and its acoustic relationships for the studied apical vowels.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports articulatory variation and its acoustic relationships for the studied apical vowels.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speakers, dialect region, imaging or measurement method, vowel context, and sample size limit generalization; variation is not pathology.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: French schwa is not acoustically distinct  from its two lexical neighbors /ø/ and /œ/
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare schwa and its lexical neighbors in natural contexts while separating acoustic overlap from lexical and phonological distribution.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper argues that French schwa is not acoustically distinct from its two lexical neighbors /ø/ and /œ/.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: French schwa, or mute-e, is one of the most studied topics in French phonology, yet its exact phonetic quality remains debated.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports acoustic overlap between French schwa and the neighboring vowels in the tested materials.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports acoustic overlap between French schwa and the neighboring vowels in the tested materials.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speakers, dialect, context, corpus, measurements, and lexical analysis bound the claim; acoustic overlap is not proof that all grammatical distinctions disappear.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speaker-specific Patterns of Phonetic Covariation in Korean Word-medial Stops and the Role of Phonological and Morphological Contexts
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure several phonetic dimensions jointly within each speaker and test whether their covariation preserves category contrasts across phonological and morphological contexts.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Seoul Korean word-medial stops are analyzed through speaker-specific distributions and covariation patterns across contexts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Korean word-medial stops provide a compelling test case, as these stops are subject to extensive contextual variability.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports systematic speaker-specific covariation that keeps stop categories distinct despite contextual variability, supporting a phonetic-uniformity account.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports systematic speaker-specific covariation that keeps stop categories distinct despite contextual variability, supporting a phonetic-uniformity account.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The language, stop system, contexts, speaker sample, and chosen phonetic measures bound the result; other languages and interactional settings require separate evidence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Supralaryngeal Kinematics of Implosives in Central Vietnamese: An EMA Study
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Track lip-aperture trajectories with electromagnetic articulography and compare Vietnamese implosives against voiced and voiceless controls in another language.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: EMA measures movement amplitude, velocity, and plateau timing during Central Vietnamese bilabial implosives; Taiwanese Southern Min controls the voicing explanation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Results indicate that implosives exhibited a higher peak velocity away from closure, whereas their voiceless plosive counterparts were found to have a longer gestural plateau.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Implosives show greater peak velocity away from closure, while voiceless plosives have a longer gestural plateau; the voiced-plosive control does not reproduce the rapid movement.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Implosives show greater peak velocity away from closure, while voiceless plosives have a longer gestural plateau; the voiced-plosive control does not reproduce the rapid movement.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The languages, speakers, consonant inventory, EMA measures, and statistical model bound the result; laryngeal airflow itself was not directly measured.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Temporal organization of prenuclear glides in Hefei Mandarin
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure the timing coordination of consonant-glide-vowel sequences and use the relative movement of gestures to infer which part of the syllable the glide behaves like.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Hefei Mandarin CjV and CwV syllables are analyzed acoustically, comparing glide timing with competing onset and rime accounts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Prenuclear-glide organization in Hefei Mandarin is analyzed from recordings by 10 local college students, with three excluded and seven participants retained. Annotated acoustic time points and formants define stability, duration, and centering measures for jV/CjV, wV/CwV, and related syllable pairs; linear mixed-effects models with participant effects test RSD and duration differences. The evidence is a small controlled production sample, not a recognition or perceptual generalization benchmark.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper finds that both glides are more likely part of the rime, agreeing with prior evidence for [j] but differing from earlier results for [w].
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper finds that both glides are more likely part of the rime, agreeing with prior evidence for [j] but differing from earlier results for [w].
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The dialect, speakers, acoustic method, and competing analyses bound the inference; timing alone cannot settle every phonological representation or generalize across Mandarin varieties.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
family_synthesis.transfer_question: What would have to remain invariant for this family to work across a new speaker, language, room, device, or task, and which paper evidence here actually tests that transfer?
family_synthesis.evidence_boundary: The shared story is supported only by the reviewed papers listed here; D2 entries support the problem and stated method, while D3 entries support the reported mechanism and evaluation. It is not a venue-wide prevalence claim.

concept_families.boundary: A label such as a phoneme is not itself a physical movement or a complete account of coarticulation.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is Speech is a timed coordination of several moving constrictions, not a sequence of isolated sounds; overlap lets one gesture affect its neighbors. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Reconstruction of the Complete Vocal Tract Contour Through Acoustic to Articulatory Inversion Using Real-Time MRI Data: The paper infers coordinated vocal-tract movement from acoustic evidence; it is about the physical source/filter relationship, not ordinary word recognition.; Enhancing Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Multi-Target Pretraining for Low-Resource Settings: Multi-target pretraining uses linguistic and articulatory labels to make acoustic-to-articulatory inversion useful under scarce paired data and lower inference cost.; Articulatory modeling of the S-shaped F2 trajectories observed in Öhman's spectrographic analysis of VCV syllables: The S-shaped formant trajectory is a physical consequence of coordinated articulator movement, not an arbitrary curve in a feature plot. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A label such as a phoneme is not itself a physical movement or a complete account of coarticulation.
concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 11 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

records.subtheme_name: Representing a changing sound
records.question: What must be preserved when a continuous signal is made into manageable measurements?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech reaches a microphone as changing air pressure after vocal-fold vibration, mouth shape, room reflections, and electronics have already mixed together. The subtheme asks: What must be preserved when a continuous signal is made into manageable measurements?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with local frequency content, but that shortcut misses the boundary: A window discards some exact timing and long-range phase; two signals with similar spectra may still sound different.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make local frequency content, multiple time scales, sampling and quantization explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Augment in-domain data, add glottal-activity information to spectral features, and normalize features with fMLLR.
subtheme_boundary: A window discards some exact timing and long-range phase; two signals with similar spectra may still sound different.
Adding resolutions is not automatically informative; it can increase computation or preserve nuisance variation.
A high sample rate cannot restore information lost through clipping, poor microphones, or an absent frequency range.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: On Enhancing the Performance of Children's ASR Task in Limited Data Scenario: The abstract ties children's recognition to limited data and acoustic features; this is a measurement/variation problem, not evidence of a new physical production model.; Influence of Proficiency and L2 Experience on Dynamic Spectral Cue Utilization in L2 Vowel Perception and Production: L2 listeners and speakers weight changing spectral cues differently; the paper treats the measured spectrum as evidence whose usefulness depends on experience and task.; Frequency-Domain Enhanced Extreme Bandwidth Extension Network with ICCRN for Superior Speech Quality: Frequency-domain bandwidth extension reconstructs missing high-frequency structure under perceptual and signal constraints.; Introducing EMOPARKNZ: the Emotional Speech Database from New Zealand English Speakers with Parkinson’s Disease: An emotional speech database from speakers with Parkinson's disease makes changing voice quality measurable across health and affect.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Augment in-domain data, add glottal-activity information to spectral features, and normalize features with fMLLR.
Track vowel-inherent spectral change across the vowel and compare perception-production alignment with proficiency and immersion experience.
Use frequency-domain enhancement with an ICCRN-style recurrent representation to preserve global spectral structure while reconstructing the absent band.
Create a dedicated New Zealand English database with multiple emotions, speakers, and acoustic analysis, then test human recognition.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: On Enhancing the Performance of Children's ASR Task in Limited Data Scenario
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Augment in-domain data, add glottal-activity information to spectral features, and normalize features with fMLLR.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study compares a baseline with augmented data, MFCCs plus glottal parameters, and fMLLR-normalized features.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: As a consequence of applying fMLLR and then concatenating the normalized MFCC features with glottal activity parameters, a relative reduction in character error rate by 40% over the baseline is obtained.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The combined normalized MFCC and glottal features give a reported 40% relative character-error-rate reduction over baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The combined normalized MFCC and glottal features give a reported 40% relative character-error-rate reduction over baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is limited to the child's speech data and tested feature pipeline; languages, age ranges, and transfer to new schools or microphones are not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Influence of Proficiency and L2 Experience on Dynamic Spectral Cue Utilization in L2 Vowel Perception and Production
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Track vowel-inherent spectral change across the vowel and compare perception-production alignment with proficiency and immersion experience.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Polish learners produce and perceive English /e-æ/ and /i-I/; dynamic formant movement is measured over vowel duration.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The acquisition of English vowels as an L2 is complex, yet most studies focus on static measures, with little attention to dynamic spectral cues like Vowel-Inherent Spectral Change (VISC).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Advanced learners improve, especially for /i-I/; formant movement increases with proficiency, while length of residence is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Advanced learners improve, especially for /i-I/; formant movement increases with proficiency, while length of residence is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The learner group, contrasts, language experience, and measurements bound the result; other L1s and natural interaction need separate evidence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Frequency-Domain Enhanced Extreme Bandwidth Extension Network with ICCRN for Superior Speech Quality
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use frequency-domain enhancement with an ICCRN-style recurrent representation to preserve global spectral structure while reconstructing the absent band.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model operates on frequency representations, combines local and global context, and is compared against EBEN and other bandwidth-extension baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations on the French LibriSpeech dataset show significant improvements, including clearer spectrograms, fewer generator parameters, and lower computational costs, advancing the state of the art in bandwidth extension.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The tests show gains over the original EBEN, including a 40-person MUSHRA comparison; the authors report clearer high-frequency detail and less distortion.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The tests show gains over the original EBEN, including a 40-person MUSHRA comparison; the authors report clearer high-frequency detail and less distortion.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: French LibriSpeech, sampling setup, listeners, and author-reported metrics bound the result; other languages remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Introducing EMOPARKNZ: the Emotional Speech Database from New Zealand English Speakers with Parkinson’s Disease
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Create a dedicated New Zealand English database with multiple emotions, speakers, and acoustic analysis, then test human recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: EMOPARKNZ contains 1,950 recordings from 13 speakers across five emotions; acoustic measures and a 22-listener perception test are reported.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: A preliminary perception test with 22 New Zealand English listeners achieved 63% classification accuracy across the five emotions, aligning with the performance reported for similar emotional speech databases.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports emotion-dependent acoustic differences and 63% listener classification accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports emotion-dependent acoustic differences and 63% listener classification accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Thirteen speakers, New Zealand English, Parkinson's disease, and the selected emotions bound the resource; clinical severity and broader populations remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Universal Speech Enhancement with Regression and Generative Mamba
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a linear-time state-space model that represents time and frequency together, maps rather than only masks the spectrum, and switches to flow-based generation when content is missing.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: USEMamba applies time/frequency Mamba blocks to compressed STFT features, uses sampling-frequency-independent windows, and combines time, multi-resolution STFT, and phase losses. A flow variant samples missing spectrogram content; a simple energy rule selects the generative output for bandwidth-extension and packet-loss regions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our approach primarily relies on regression-based modeling, which performs well across most distortions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On the URGENT 2025 conditions spanning seven distortions, five languages, and several sampling rates, the combined system achieved second place in the blind Track 1 phase; regression worked best for most conditions while generation helped packet loss and bandwidth extension.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On the URGENT 2025 conditions spanning seven distortions, five languages, and several sampling rates, the combined system achieved second place in the blind Track 1 phase; regression worked best for most conditions while generation helped packet loss and bandwidth extension.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The regression model was trained only on English, the challenge data and distortions define the tested generality, and the flow output sometimes had residual noise or wrong phonemes for long packet losses. Ranking and objective metrics do not establish human usefulness in every language or device; no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Neural Spectral Band Generation for Audio Coding
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Encode compact side information about the missing band and use a learned generator conditioned on that information and the decoded core band.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Neural spectral band generation uses an encoder-decoder to quantize high-frequency side information, reconstructs the band from core audio plus that information, and trains the whole codec with adversarial perceptual criteria.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Neural spectral-band generation is trained with about 70 hours of sound events, 30 hours of music, and 30 hours of speech, then evaluated on 43 USAC-standardization items: 11 speech, 18 music, and 14 mixed. NMR, 2f-model MMS, and ViSQOL MOS form the objective rate-distortion metrics; a 14-participant A/B test uses nine randomly selected clips.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Using AAC as the core codec, the paper reports that n-SBG outperforms conventional SBR at comparable bitrates, especially at low rates, though some codec/rate combinations introduce audible noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Using AAC as the core codec, the paper reports that n-SBG outperforms conventional SBR at comparable bitrates, especially at low rates, though some codec/rate combinations introduce audible noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The core codec, bitrate, adversarial training, signal types, and perceptual metric bound the claim; plausible high-frequency detail is not guaranteed to be the original detail or to improve every downstream speech task.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: An interpretable speech foundation model for depression detection by revealing prediction-relevant acoustic features from long speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Model the full speech recording and expose which time-frequency regions and acoustic properties drive the decision.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper uses a speech-level Audio Spectrogram Transformer on long-duration speech and introduces an interpretation method that identifies prediction-relevant acoustic features, comparing it with a segment-level AST.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Depression detection uses 698 D-Vlog waveforms from 961 annotated vlogs, split by unique YouTube account into stratified train/development sets (294/261 train and 73/69 development depression/normal instances). Speech-level and segment-level AST models are compared with AUC on the development set, with 5,000 bootstrap samples for 95% intervals and DeLong's test; no independent test set is used.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better depression detection than the segment-level model and identifies reduced loudness and F0 as relevant signals consistent with prior clinical findings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better depression detection than the segment-level model and identifies reduced loudness and F0 as relevant signals consistent with prior clinical findings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset, diagnostic labels, recording protocol, attention interpretation, and screening threshold bound the claim; a predictive acoustic correlate is not a clinical cause or validated diagnosis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Adaptive Differential Denoising for Respiratory Sounds Classification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use an adaptive differential denoising procedure whose behavior changes with the observed respiratory signal, then test classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes adaptive differential denoising for respiratory-sound classification and compares it with less adaptive processing.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on the ICBHI2017 dataset show that our method achieves 65.53% of the Score, which is improved by 1.99% over the previous sota method.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved respiratory-sound classification with the proposed denoising approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved respiratory-sound classification with the proposed denoising approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset, labels, recording hardware, noise conditions, and evaluation split limit generalization to clinical deployment or diagnosis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Functional Connectivity and Hilbert-Based Features for Covert Speech EEG Variability Analysis and Classification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent covert speech with Hilbert envelopes, instantaneous phase, and functional connectivity across frequency bands, then train a subject-independent sequence classifier.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Phase Locking Value and coherence summarize coordination among EEG channels. Band-specific Hilbert features feed a BiLSTM, while inter-trial, inter-class, and inter-subject analyses separate stable structure from variability.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We also propose a subject-independent classification model using Hilbert envelope and instantaneous phase features across EEG frequency bands with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) architecture, achieving 59.14% classification accuracy across five speech categories.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The reported subject-independent model reaches 59.14% accuracy across five covert-speech categories and reveals both shared and class-specific connectivity patterns.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The reported subject-independent model reaches 59.14% accuracy across five covert-speech categories and reveals both shared and class-specific connectivity patterns.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Covert speech EEG is not ordinary spoken audio, sample and subject variability constrain the result, class accuracy is not communicative utility, and no independent execution was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Band-Split Self-supervised Mamba for Infant-centered Audio Analysis
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Split the spectrum into bands, learn band-specific projections, and let a band-agnostic Mamba encoder model temporal relations while self-supervised pretraining uses unlabeled in-domain audio.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Band-specific features preserve local spectral evidence while the state-space sequence model carries information over time; self-supervised and supervised objectives share the representation before downstream classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Recent advances in self-supervised learning on large unlabeled datasets and supervised training on limited annotated data have improved performance in this domain.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: BS-SSAMBA improves infant-centered audio analysis in the reported experiments and benefits from combining unlabeled in-domain audio with limited annotations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: BS-SSAMBA improves infant-centered audio analysis in the reported experiments and benefits from combining unlabeled in-domain audio with limited annotations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Infant audio is adjacent to, not identical with, human speech; task labels, home environments, class balance, and domain-specific data bound transfer to adult speech systems.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Evaluating Deep Speaker Embedding Robustness to Domain, Sampling Rate, and Codec Variations
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Stress several embedding models across far-field, noise, music, sampling-rate, and compression shifts and measure how much verification performance moves.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates ECAPA-TDNN, TitaNet, ECAPA2, and ReDimNet on domain, sampling-rate, and codec variations, including far-field speech, noise, and music interference.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speaker verification systems based on deep speaker embeddings perform well under matched training and evaluation conditions, but performance degrades under domain shifts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: All models degrade under mismatched domains; ReDimNet degrades least in the tested settings, while downsampling and low-bitrate compression further hurt performance and expose reliance on high-frequency information.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: All models degrade under mismatched domains; ReDimNet degrades least in the tested settings, while downsampling and low-bitrate compression further hurt performance and expose reliance on high-frequency information.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, codecs, sampling rates, threshold calibration, and attack/evaluation protocol bound the result; robustness to these shifts does not imply fairness or security against adaptive attacks.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Echoes of Phonetics:  Unveiling Relevant Acoustic Cues for ASR via Feature Attribution
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Apply feature attribution across plosives, fricatives, and vowels and compare the highlighted regions with known acoustic events in time and frequency.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study analyzes a modern Conformer ASR system, identifying attribution patterns for vowels, sibilant/non-sibilant fricatives, and plosives including release bursts and formants.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: By analyzing plosives, fricatives, and vowels, we assess how feature attributions align with their acoustic properties in the time and frequency domains, also essential for human speech perception.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that the model uses full vowel spans and especially the first two formants, captures sibilant spectra more strongly, and emphasizes plosive release/burst cues, with differences by speaker sex.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that the model uses full vowel spans and especially the first two formants, captures sibilant spectra more strongly, and emphasizes plosive release/burst cues, with differences by speaker sex.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Attribution method, baseline model, phoneme set, speaker distribution, and interpretation assumptions bound the result; saliency is evidence of sensitivity, not a causal proof that the model listens as a human does.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Leveraging AM and FM Rhythm Spectrograms for Dementia Classification and Assessment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent amplitude and frequency modulation rhythms as spectrograms, compare interpretable handcrafted summaries with a learned fusion of acoustic and linguistic representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study derives Rhythm Formant Analysis AM/FM spectrograms, tests handcrafted features and a ViT-plus-BERT fusion for dementia classification and regression, and compares against eGeMAPs and Mel spectrograms.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Notably, our handcrafted features outperform eGeMAPs with a relative improvement of 14.2% in classification accuracy and comparable performance in the regression task.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 14.2% relative classification-accuracy improvement over eGeMAPs for handcrafted features and further gains when rhythm spectrograms are fused with linguistic and acoustic models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 14.2% relative classification-accuracy improvement over eGeMAPs for handcrafted features and further gains when rhythm spectrograms are fused with linguistic and acoustic models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Corpus, labels, recording length, disease definition, model fusion, and accuracy/regression metrics bound the result; an acoustic association is not a clinical diagnosis or causal mechanism.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Data-Driven Diffusion-based Approach for Audio Deepfake Explanations
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Relate detector decisions to localized time-frequency structure with a data-driven explanation model.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A spectro-temporal explanation connects model output to changing acoustic regions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluating explainability techniques, such as SHAP and LRP, in the context of audio deepfake detection is challenging due to lack of clear ground truth annotations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a diffusion approach for explaining neural audio deepfake decisions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a diffusion approach for explaining neural audio deepfake decisions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Deepfake types, explanation faithfulness, model family, and listener interpretation bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Extended High-frequency Cues to Phoneme Recognition: Insights from ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a phoneme recognizer as a controlled probe of which frequency bands help under masking and spatial separation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A neural network decodes phonemes from cochleagrams of broadband, 8-kHz-low-pass, and 6-kHz-low-pass speech under quiet and masked conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Compared with filtered speech, broadband speech improved phoneme recognition accuracy in masked conditions, particularly at lower TMRs, but showed no benefit in quiet.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Broadband speech improves phoneme accuracy in masked conditions, especially at lower TMR, while adding no quiet-condition benefit; removing extended high frequencies increases consonant omissions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Broadband speech improves phoneme accuracy in masked conditions, especially at lower TMR, while adding no quiet-condition benefit; removing extended high frequencies increases consonant omissions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: VCTK speech, selected maskers, cochleagram assumptions, and a model-based probe bound the conclusion; audiological benefit and general ASR deployment are not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Low Complex IIR Adaptive Hear-Through Ambient Filtering for Overcoming Practical Constraints in Earbuds
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Estimate a virtual sensing path and adapt a low-complexity IIR hear-through filter with stability-aware updates for different earbud fittings and directions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The virtual sensor models the sound pressure at the eardrum; an adaptive IIR filter updates the feedforward path, while constraints on poles/coefficients prevent unstable compensation. Indoor and outdoor acoustic simulations test convergence and delay.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Most studies have proposed usage of fixed-filter or adaptive finite impulse response (FIR) HT techniques, which can lead to mismatch between the modelled and desired open ear response for different users and fittings or lead to higher computations and larger processing delays.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposed low-complexity IIR method reports improved hear-through performance under practical constraints and reduced complexity relative to larger adaptive alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposed low-complexity IIR method reports improved hear-through performance under practical constraints and reduced complexity relative to larger adaptive alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is simulation-heavy and depends on acoustic-path and fitting assumptions; user listening, hardware latency, and individualized hearing benefit are not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Relationship between objective and subjective perceptual measures of speech in individuals with head and neck cancer
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure several perceptual dimensions and objective proxies in longitudinal head-and-neck-cancer speech, then inspect their correlation structure for common-cause confounding.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Trained listeners rate intelligibility, articulation, voice quality, phonation, rate, nasality, and noise; objective measures such as NAD, PCX, PER, SPEED, and SNR are compared using Pearson correlations across 53 Dutch participants.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study examined the link between perceptual speech assessments and objective acoustic measures in a large head and neck cancer (HNC) dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Subjective intelligibility correlates strongly with articulation (r=.95) and voice quality (r=.92); NAD correlates .90 with intelligibility, while phonation and nasality lack reliable objective counterparts in this cohort.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Subjective intelligibility correlates strongly with articulation (r=.95) and voice quality (r=.92); NAD correlates .90 with intelligibility, while phonation and nasality lack reliable objective counterparts in this cohort.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The population is Dutch readers with head-and-neck cancer, not general speech; neural features are not fully interpretable, running spontaneous speech is absent, and correlation does not prove clinical decision validity.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: LSPnet: an ultra-low bitrate hybrid neural codec
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine LSP-based parametric coding, direct neural sample prediction, and joint STFT/cross-entropy training in a hybrid LPCNet-style codec.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: LSPs stabilize spectral-envelope quantization; the neural predictor models sample distributions; time-frequency losses jointly constrain local waveform and spectral behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Building upon the LPCNet framework, combined with a parametric encoder, we introduce several key improvements by incorporating line spectral pairs (LSP) to improve quantization error performance and eliminate explicit LPC estimation by directly predicting the probability distribution of audio samples using a deep neural network, and employing a joint time-frequency training strategy combining short-time Fourier transform (STFT) loss with cross-entropy (CE) loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports high speech quality at 1.2 kbps and lower complexity than compared end-to-end codecs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports high speech quality at 1.2 kbps and lower complexity than compared end-to-end codecs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, bitrate, codec baselines, quality metrics, hardware, and real-time implementation bound transfer; reported quality is not proof for every channel or listener.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.
family_synthesis.named_contrast: On Enhancing the Performance of Children's ASR Task in Limited Data Scenario versus Influence of Proficiency and L2 Experience on Dynamic Spectral Cue Utilization in L2 Vowel Perception and Production
family_synthesis.mechanism_contrast: On Enhancing the Performance of Children's ASR Task in Limited Data Scenario addresses the pressure by The study compares a baseline with augmented data, MFCCs plus glottal parameters, and fMLLR-normalized features.; Influence of Proficiency and L2 Experience on Dynamic Spectral Cue Utilization in L2 Vowel Perception and Production addresses it by Polish learners produce and perceive English /e-æ/ and /i-I/; dynamic formant movement is measured over vowel duration.. The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.
family_synthesis.evidence_contrast: The first paper reports The combined normalized MFCC and glottal features give a reported 40% relative character-error-rate reduction over baseline.; the second reports Advanced learners improve, especially for /i-I/; formant movement increases with proficiency, while length of residence is not significant.. These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.
family_synthesis.failure_boundary_contrast: The first paper leaves open: The evidence is limited to the child's speech data and tested feature pipeline; languages, age ranges, and transfer to new schools or microphones are not established.; the second leaves open: The learner group, contrasts, language experience, and measurements bound the result; other L1s and natural interaction need separate evidence.. Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
family_synthesis.transfer_question: What would have to remain invariant for this family to work across a new speaker, language, room, device, or task, and which paper evidence here actually tests that transfer?
family_synthesis.evidence_boundary: The shared story is supported only by the reviewed papers listed here; D2 entries support the problem and stated method, while D3 entries support the reported mechanism and evaluation. It is not a venue-wide prevalence claim.
family_synthesis.unresolved_question: What changes when this move is tested outside the speakers, languages, rooms, devices, or benchmark conditions represented by the 18 D3 paper(s)?
