concept_families.boundary: A high sample rate cannot restore information lost through clipping, poor microphones, or an absent frequency range.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is A digital recording keeps a finite set of amplitude measurements, so the sampling rate and numeric precision set what can still be recovered. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Neural Spectral Band Generation for Audio Coding: Neural spectral-band generation asks which frequency information can be reconstructed after audio coding removes or compresses it.; Evaluating Deep Speaker Embedding Robustness to Domain, Sampling Rate, and Codec Variations: The paper tests how sampling rate, codecs, and far-field/noisy channels alter speaker embeddings, making the recording representation the boundary.; Bringing Interpretability to Neural Audio Codecs: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate sampling-and-quantization under time-frequency-measurement; this resolves taxonomy membership only. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A high sample rate cannot restore information lost through clipping, poor microphones, or an absent frequency range.
concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 3 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

records.subtheme_name: Rooms, devices, and unusual sensors
records.question: How does the path from talker to sensor alter the speech evidence?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech reaches a microphone as changing air pressure after vocal-fold vibration, mouth shape, room reflections, and electronics have already mixed together. The subtheme asks: How does the path from talker to sensor alter the speech evidence?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with reverberant room mixture, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Reverberation is not just additive stationary noise; its delay pattern depends on room geometry and position.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make reverberant room mixture, microphone and channel coloration, non-airborne speech sensing explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Transcode millions of multilingual files through PSTN, VoIP, and neural codecs, then compare quality by language and gender.
subtheme_boundary: Reverberation is not just additive stationary noise; its delay pattern depends on room geometry and position.
Channel normalization can remove useful speaker or environment information along with nuisance coloration.
A sensor that works in quiet laboratory placement is not automatically a replacement for ordinary audio in daily use.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: On the Language and Gender Biases in PSTN, VoIP and Neural Audio Codecs: The study examines how codecs and channel changes interact with language and gender patterns, making the recording path part of recognition evidence.; AISHELL-5: The First Open-Source In-Car Multi-Channel Multi-Speaker Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Diarization and Recognition: The dataset and baseline preserve the room, vehicle, microphone-array, and multi-speaker path that transforms speech before recognition.; Voxplorer: Voice data exploration and projection in an interactive dashboard: An interactive voice-data dashboard exposes how recording conditions and speaker variables shape the projections used to explore speech.; Improving Low-Resource Dialect Classification Using Retrieval-based Voice Conversion: Voice conversion is used to vary speakers and dialect conditions, testing whether a classifier learns dialect evidence or the recording and speaker mix.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Transcode millions of multilingual files through PSTN, VoIP, and neural codecs, then compare quality by language and gender.

Release a multi-channel, multi-speaker in-car corpus with near-field references, far-field door microphones, real driving conditions, noise recordings, and a reproducible separation-plus-ASR baseline.
Put feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, filtering, and projection into an interactive dashboard.
Use retrieval-based voice conversion to put examples into a more uniform target-speaker space, then combine it with ordinary augmentations and test whether dialect classification improves.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: On the Language and Gender Biases in PSTN, VoIP and Neural Audio Codecs
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Transcode millions of multilingual files through PSTN, VoIP, and neural codecs, then compare quality by language and gender.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study measures speech quality after representative codec paths across more than two million multilingual files.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The study transcodes 2,061,600 VoxForge files and 75,600 DARPA-TIMIT files through PSTN, VoIP, and neural codecs at specified bitrates, then computes ViSQOL speech-mode quality. Language effects are analyzed across 17 languages and gender effects on TIMIT metadata; codec/bitrate and subgroup are the denominators.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: PSTN codecs show strong gender bias and neural codecs introduce language bias in the reported analysis.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: PSTN codecs show strong gender bias and neural codecs introduce language bias in the reported analysis.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Codec set, languages, gender labels, quality measure, and files define the boundary; causal mechanisms and mitigation in deployed networks remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: AISHELL-5: The First Open-Source In-Car Multi-Channel Multi-Speaker Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Diarization and Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Release a multi-channel, multi-speaker in-car corpus with near-field references, far-field door microphones, real driving conditions, noise recordings, and a reproducible separation-plus-ASR baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: AISHELL-5 records 2–4 Mandarin speakers in a hybrid vehicle across more than 60 scenarios, with four far-field channels and headset reference microphones. The baseline uses acoustic echo cancellation, independent vector analysis or SpatialNet separation, VAD segmentation, and ASR; the paper reports separate evaluation sets for oracle and predicted segmentation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper delineates AISHELL-5, the first open-source in-car multi-channel multi-speaker Mandarin automatic speech recognition (ASR) dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The corpus contains over 100 hours of speech from 260 participants plus about 40 hours of environmental noise; the baseline exposes large differences between near/far-field and processed conditions, with the reported ASR/front-end results establishing the challenge difficulty.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The corpus contains over 100 hours of speech from 260 participants plus about 40 hours of environmental noise; the baseline exposes large differences between near/far-field and processed conditions, with the reported ASR/front-end results establishing the challenge difficulty.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpus is Mandarin and vehicle-specific, with its seating, microphones, and scenario design defining the boundary. The baseline does not establish that one separation method is best in all cars, and dataset availability is not independent reproduction of the reported scores.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Voxplorer: Voice data exploration and projection in an interactive dashboard
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Put feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, filtering, and projection into an interactive dashboard.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Voxplorer exposes precomputed high-dimensional voice data and can extract features from recordings directly for interactive exploration.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Voxplorer is evaluated as an interactive voice-data exploration dashboard: feature extraction, dimensionality reduction, filtering, and projection are tested on the paper's voice datasets through the supported visual-analysis workflow. The evidence concerns exploratory usability and inspectable projections rather than a held-out recognition metric or listener denominator.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper presents a reusable dashboard intended to broaden voice-analysis exploration; no scientific performance score is claimed.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper presents a reusable dashboard intended to broaden voice-analysis exploration; no scientific performance score is claimed.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Usability, projection choices, and feature-tool assumptions determine what researchers see; the dashboard does not establish causal voice categories.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Low-Resource Dialect Classification Using Retrieval-based Voice Conversion
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use retrieval-based voice conversion to put examples into a more uniform target-speaker space, then combine it with ordinary augmentations and test whether dialect classification improves.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: RVC converts low-resource German dialect samples toward a uniform target speaker; experiments compare RVC alone and with frequency masking and segment removal for dialect classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Dialect classification uses 10-second segments with speaker-disjoint train/validation/test partitions; each validation/test split samples speakers by dialect and the experiment repeats 250 random subsets. Retrieval-based voice conversion is compared with frequency masking and segment-removal augmentation using mean weighted F1, with Mann–Whitney U tests for run comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved dialect-classification performance from RVC augmentation, with further gains when combined with frequency masking and segment removal.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved dialect-classification performance from RVC augmentation, with further gains when combined with frequency masking and segment removal.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dialect data, target speaker, conversion fidelity, train/test speaker split, and classifier architecture bound the claim; higher accuracy does not prove that all dialect cues survived conversion.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Influence of Room Acoustics on Objective Voice Assessment Methods in the Context of Speech and Language Therapy
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure room impulse responses and compare dry and room-affected AVQI and ABI values across 35 speech-therapy rooms, two microphone positions, and 1,644 voice samples.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study simulates room conditions with measured impulse responses and noise, computes the difference between room and dry measures, and fits mixed-effects models with room as a fixed effect, the dry score and its interaction, and subject as a random effect.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: These objective measures reduce diagnostic variability by eliminating subjective evaluations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Across the rooms, voice-quality measures generally deteriorate by 0–2 units; the smartphone is more affected than the lavalier microphone, and room effects are significant for almost all rooms. Only 8 of 35 rooms meet the stricter A4 reverberation recommendation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Across the rooms, voice-quality measures generally deteriorate by 0–2 units; the smartphone is more affected than the lavalier microphone, and room effects are significant for almost all rooms. Only 8 of 35 rooms meet the stricter A4 reverberation recommendation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The rooms, simulated signals, microphones, and Saarbrücken database define the tested boundary; the study does not establish a correction for other clinics or devices. Reported model fits and significance tests are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: AuralNet: Hierarchical Attention-based 3D Binaural Localization of Overlapping Speakers
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a gated coarse-to-fine model that first detects sectors and then regresses azimuth/elevation with a masked multitask loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: AuralNet processes binaural signals with multi-head attention, jointly detects sources and estimates azimuth/elevation, and is tested in noisy-reverberant conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: AuralNet is tested on synthetic binaural TIMIT convolved with ITA HRTFs, with 98,136 training samples, 2,088 single-source validation samples, and 2,800 multi-source test samples across seen and unseen rooms, speech, source counts, and 20/10/0-dB SNR. Detection accuracy, F1, and detection-aware angular error measure source-sector detection and azimuth/elevation error; comparisons are reported for one-, two-, and three-talker cases.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports superiority over recent methods in its noisy-reverberant multi-source experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports superiority over recent methods in its noisy-reverberant multi-source experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The room simulation/recordings, binaural setup, sector design, and source overlap define the claim; far-field microphone arrays and speech-specific attribution remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Sub-band based Adaptive IIR Algorithm with Biquad Filter Stability Constraints for Feedforward Hear-Through Equalization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt a low-order sub-band IIR equalizer and enforce stability with a biquad/all-pass constraint based on the least-mean-square fourth criterion.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The reference microphone signal is split into sub-bands; feedforward FxLMS/F adaptation updates IIR paths, while cascaded biquads compensate phase/group delay and constrain poles during changing indoor/outdoor conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The adaptive IIR hear-through filter is evaluated in 16-kHz simulations against FxBLMS/F, equation-error adaptive IIR, delayless sub-band FIR, and fixed-filter baselines. Single-source tests use multi-tone, bandlimited-noise, and broadband-noise stimuli; dynamic indoor/outdoor simulations vary moving and multiple source directions. Steady-state MSE and convergence behavior are the reported outcomes, with the proposed filter reaching -50 dB or lower SS-MSE in the three single-source tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports up to 13 dB improvement over compared adaptive methods in simulated scenarios, with stable behavior and similar complexity in dynamic indoor/outdoor tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports up to 13 dB improvement over compared adaptive methods in simulated scenarios, with stable behavior and similar complexity in dynamic indoor/outdoor tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is simulation-based and depends on acoustic paths, filter orders, and stability settings; user perception, individualized ears, and end-to-end hardware latency are not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Fine-tune Before Structured Pruning: Towards Compact and Accurate Self-Supervised Models for Speaker Diarization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Fine-tune the self-supervised WavLM model on diarization before structured pruning, and use knowledge distillation to preserve the task behavior while removing redundant structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The teacher supplies representations or logits for the student; structured channel/layer removal creates a compact model, and diarization error rate on far-field meeting corpora measures the retained segmentation and attribution ability.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on far-field single-channel AMI, AISHELL-4, and AliMeeting datasets show that our method can remove redundant parameters of WavLM Base+ and WavLM Large by up to 80% without any performance degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On AMI, AISHELL-4, and AliMeeting, the paper reports that fine-tuning before pruning improves the accuracy/size trade-off over pruning without that order.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On AMI, AISHELL-4, and AliMeeting, the paper reports that fine-tuning before pruning improves the accuracy/size trade-off over pruning without that order.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset microphone layouts, pruning ratios, teacher/student settings, and DER's treatment of overlap bound the claim; compact diarization is not universal robustness or real-device validation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: L3C-DeepMFC: Low-Latency Low-Complexity Deep Marginal Feedback Cancellation with Closed-Loop Fine Tuning for Hearing Aids
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Estimate the desired speech's complex spectrum in time-frequency bands and adapt the feedback canceller with closed-loop fine tuning while keeping the model small.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: L3C-DeepMFC uses complex spectrum mapping, full- and sub-band recurrent components, and closed-loop fine tuning for marginal feedback cancellation; evaluation varies feedback paths and reports latency, complexity, and speech quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations using the AISHELL-3 dataset confirm its competitive performance across various gains, significantly improving the maximum stable gain (MSG).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports low-latency, low-complexity feedback cancellation with improved speech quality relative to its baselines under tested hearing-aid conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports low-latency, low-complexity feedback cancellation with improved speech quality relative to its baselines under tested hearing-aid conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Feedback paths, delay budget, hardware assumptions, noise, and quality metrics bound the result; lab cancellation performance is not the same as clinical benefit for every listener.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SepVAC: Multitask Learning of Speaker Separation, Speaker Localization, Microphone Array Localization, and Room Acoustic Parameter Estimation in Various Acoustic Conditions
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Predict speech separation and the physical recording conditions together, then use curriculum learning to stabilize training.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SepVAC jointly estimates separated speech, speaker locations, microphone-array location, and room acoustic parameters on SMS-WSJ-Plus.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In our evaluation using SMS-WSJ-Plus dataset, it outperforms the state-of-the-art SpatialNet baseline by 0.67 points in word error rate (WER).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 0.67-point WER improvement over SpatialNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 0.67-point WER improvement over SpatialNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is author-reported on SMS-WSJ-Plus and its simulated acoustic conditions; real rooms, imperfect localization, and independent reproduction remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Conformer-based Ultrasound-to-Speech Conversion
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a Conformer that combines local acoustic-image patterns with longer temporal context, and compare a simpler model with a bi-LSTM extension and a standard CNN.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Two Conformer architectures map ultrasound from four speakers in Ultrasuite-Tal80 to mel spectrograms, then HiFi-GAN produces audio; MSE, mel-cepstral distortion, and a MUSHRA listening test are compared with a 2-D CNN.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speaker-specific models were trained on the data of four speakers from the Ultrasuite-Tal80 dataset, while the generated mel spectrograms were synthesized to audio waveform using a HiFi-GAN vocoder.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports no statistically significant objective improvement for either Conformer, but better perceptual quality for the bi-LSTM model; the base model matches the CNN while training about three times faster.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports no statistically significant objective improvement for either Conformer, but better perceptual quality for the bi-LSTM model; the base model matches the CNN while training about three times faster.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Four speakers, speaker-specific training, ultrasound alignment, vocoder quality, and the listening panel bound the result; perceptual improvement is not evidence of speaker-independent silent speech or clinical usefulness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Direction-Aware Neural Acoustic Fields for Few-Shot Interpolation of Ambisonic Impulse Responses
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a spatially continuous neural field that takes source/listener geometry and direction as inputs and predicts ambisonic impulse responses between sparse measurements.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Direction-Aware Neural Acoustic Fields model ambisonic room impulse responses with a neural field and add explicit directional information, evaluating few-shot interpolation against prior monaural/binaural fields.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: However, previous NF-based methods have focused on monaural omnidirectional or at most binaural listeners, which does not precisely capture the directional characteristics of a real sound field at a single point.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved few-shot interpolation of directional ambisonic responses over prior neural-field formulations in its room measurements.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved few-shot interpolation of directional ambisonic responses over prior neural-field formulations in its room measurements.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Room geometry, microphone/ambisonic order, sampling locations, interpolation range, and waveform metrics bound the claim; interpolation quality does not prove accurate rendering in unseen rooms or perceptual equivalence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Selective Auditory Attention Decoding in Naturalistic Conversations Using EEG-Based Speech Envelope Tracking in Multi-Speaker Environments
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Reconstruct each speech envelope from EEG with a time-lagged ridge model and identify the attended speaker by whichever reconstructed envelope correlates best.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A multivariate linear model maps 62 EEG channels over 0–200 ms lags to speech-envelope samples; leave-one-trial-out validation compares Pearson correlations for target and distractor streams before and after exogenous switches.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speech envelope reconstruction from EEG showed higher accuracy for the attended speaker than distractors, with single-trial classification at 76%.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Across 36 trials, target-speaker decoding averages 76% ± 12%; performance remains above chance as windows shrink from 20 seconds to 2 seconds, and reconstruction briefly rises after attention switches.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Across 36 trials, target-speaker decoding averages 76% ± 12%; performance remains above chance as windows shrink from 20 seconds to 2 seconds, and reconstruction briefly rises after attention switches.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The experiment uses controlled speakers and exogenous switches, short windows still perform poorly, EEG signal-to-noise limits real-time use, and neural decoding is not equivalent to robust everyday source separation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: French Listening Tests for the Assessment of Intelligibility, Quality, and Identity of Body-Conducted Speech Enhancement
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Evaluate EBEN with separate listening tasks for intelligibility, quality, and identity, then correlate each human measure with candidate objective metrics across sensor types and sex.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Forehead-accelerometer, rigid-in-ear, and throat-microphone signals from Vibravox are enhanced by EBEN; French Modified Rhyme Tests, MUSHRA, and A/B identification are compared with STOI, N-MOS, and ECAPA2 similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study evaluates the Extreme Bandwidth Extension Network (EBEN) model on body-conduction sensors through listening tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: EBEN improves reported quality and intelligibility but slightly harms female throat-microphone identity; STOI correlates strongly with MUSHRA quality (ρ=.87) and ECAPA2 with identification (ρ=.90), while no tested metric reliably predicts intelligibility change.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: EBEN improves reported quality and intelligibility but slightly harms female throat-microphone identity; STOI correlates strongly with MUSHRA quality (ρ=.87) and ECAPA2 with identification (ρ=.90), while no tested metric reliably predicts intelligibility change.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The study uses quiet recordings, selected sensors and speakers, one enhancement model, and finite listening tests. Correlation with a perceptual proxy does not establish general clinical or operational usefulness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Recreating Neural Activity During Speech Production with Language and Speech Model Embeddings
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use pretrained language and speech-model embeddings as regressors for high-gamma activity, then compare how linguistic and acoustic representations reconstruct spatio-temporal neural signals.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Embedding vectors are aligned to neural time windows and mapped to high-gamma responses; reconstruction quality is evaluated across electrodes, time, and representational sources.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Reconstructed neural signals are evaluated against high-gamma ground-truth activity using correlation metrics and signal reconstruction quality assessments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Language and speech embeddings reconstruct measurable neural activity characteristics, with differences across model type and brain locations reported as evidence about linguistic versus acoustic information.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Language and speech embeddings reconstruct measurable neural activity characteristics, with differences across model type and brain locations reported as evidence about linguistic versus acoustic information.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Neural recordings, participant count, electrode coverage, alignment choices, and correlational reconstruction limit causal interpretation; a good reconstruction is not a speech decoder or clinical interface.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Articulatory Feature Prediction from Surface EMG during Speech Production
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use an EMG encoder with convolutional and Transformer layers to predict EMA positions, pitch, loudness, and auxiliary phonemes, making articulatory structure an intermediate target.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model minimizes L2 losses for EMA, pitch, and loudness and cross-entropy for phonemes. The predicted EMA coordinates represent tongue, lip, and jaw movement rather than an opaque speech label.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our approach achieves a high prediction correlation of approximately 0.9 for most articulatory features.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On 7,565 utterances from one male American English speaker, the paper reports strong EMA and loudness prediction and evaluates held-out utterances using correlations against acoustic-inversion targets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On 7,565 utterances from one male American English speaker, the paper reports strong EMA and loudness prediction and evaluates held-out utterances using correlations against acoustic-inversion targets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Targets are pseudo-ground truth from acoustic-to-articulatory inversion, the speaker is not diverse, experiments focus on vocalized open-vocabulary speech, and feature prediction is not the same as intelligible silent-speech synthesis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unified Microphone Conversion: Many-to-Many Device Mapping via Feature-wise Linear Modulation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a unified many-to-many microphone conversion model using feature-wise linear modulation to condition conversion on source and target devices.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: FiLM parameters modulate intermediate features according to device identities, allowing one model to represent multiple channel mappings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experimental results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art by 2.6% and reduces variability by 0.8% in macro-average F1 score.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports unified microphone conversion results across device mappings without paired examples for every target pair.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports unified microphone conversion results across device mappings without paired examples for every target pair.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Device inventory, pairing protocol, training coverage, content preservation metrics, and acoustic conditions bound transfer; channel conversion is not the same as recognizer invariance.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Effect of Noise Floor in Room Impulse Response on Speech Perception Under Spherical Harmonics-based Spatial Sound Reproduction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Vary RIR noise floor and compare speech-in-noise listening in spherical-harmonic reproduction against the rooms where the RIRs were measured.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The RIR encodes direct and reflected paths; its residual floor changes the rendered reverberant tail, which is tested through intelligibility comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Subjective listening test measuring the intelligibility of speech in noise was conducted under the spatial sound reproduction implemented using practically measured RIR with varying level of noise floor.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better reproducibility with low-noise-floor RIRs in highly reverberant rooms and at 5 m, while truncation usually did not help.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better reproducibility with low-noise-floor RIRs in highly reverberant rooms and at 5 m, while truncation usually did not help.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Rooms, source distances, RIR measurement, listening protocol, and speech-in-noise task bound transfer; perceptual reproducibility is not exact physical localization.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.
family_synthesis.named_contrast: On the Language and Gender Biases in PSTN, VoIP and Neural Audio Codecs versus AISHELL-5: The First Open-Source In-Car Multi-Channel Multi-Speaker Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Diarization and Recognition
family_synthesis.mechanism_contrast: On the Language and Gender Biases in PSTN, VoIP and Neural Audio Codecs addresses the pressure by The study measures speech quality after representative codec paths across more than two million multilingual files.; AISHELL-5: The First Open-Source In-Car Multi-Channel Multi-Speaker Speech Dataset for Automatic Speech Diarization and Recognition addresses it by AISHELL-5 records 2–4 Mandarin speakers in a hybrid vehicle across more than 60 scenarios, with four far-field channels and headset reference microphones. The baseline uses acoustic echo cancellation, independent vector analysis or SpatialNet separation, VAD segmentation, and ASR; the paper reports separate evaluation sets for oracle and predicted segmentation.. The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.
family_synthesis.evidence_contrast: The first paper reports PSTN codecs show strong gender bias and neural codecs introduce language bias in the reported analysis.; the second reports The corpus contains over 100 hours of speech from 260 participants plus about 40 hours of environmental noise; the baseline exposes large differences between near/far-field and processed conditions, with the reported ASR/front-end results establishing the challenge difficulty.. These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.
family_synthesis.failure_boundary_contrast: The first paper leaves open: Codec set, languages, gender labels, quality measure, and files define the boundary; causal mechanisms and mitigation in deployed networks remain open.; the second leaves open: The corpus is Mandarin and vehicle-specific, with its seating, microphones, and scenario design defining the boundary. The baseline does not establish that one separation method is best in all cars, and dataset availability is not independent reproduction of the reported scores.. Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
family_synthesis.transfer_question: What would have to remain invariant for this family to work across a new speaker, language, room, device, or task, and which paper evidence here actually tests that transfer?
family_synthesis.evidence_boundary: The shared story is supported only by the reviewed papers listed here; D2 entries support the problem and stated method, while D3 entries support the reported mechanism and evaluation. It is not a venue-wide prevalence claim.
family_synthesis.unresolved_question: What changes when this move is tested outside the speakers, languages, rooms, devices, or benchmark conditions represented by the 18 D3 paper(s)?

concept_families.definition: The microphone hears direct sound plus delayed reflections, so a word can overlap its own earlier energy and blur boundaries.
concept_families.boundary: Reverberation is not just additive stationary noise; its delay pattern depends on room geometry and position.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Influence of Room Acoustics on Objective Voice Assessment Methods in the Context of Speech and Language Therapy: Room acoustics alter clinical voice measures, so the paper tests the boundary between speaker quality and recording-path effects.; Direction-Aware Neural Acoustic Fields for Few-Shot Interpolation of Ambisonic Impulse Responses: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate reverberant-mixture under room-channel-and-sensing; this resolves taxonomy membership only.; Unified Variational and Physics-aware Model for Room Impulse Response Estimation: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate reverberant-mixture under room-channel-and-sensing; this resolves taxonomy membership only. records.subtheme_name: Suppressing background noise without erasing speech
records.question: Which variation is nuisance and which is the quiet speech cue needed for intelligibility?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: A listener often hears several talkers, music, echo, and device noise at once, yet needs one person's words or an intelligible mixture. The subtheme asks: Which variation is nuisance and which is the quiet speech cue needed for intelligibility?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with time-frequency masking, but that shortcut misses the boundary: A binary or soft mask can create musical noise and cannot reliably separate sources that occupy the same region.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make time-frequency masking, speech-prior denoising, changing and adverse noise explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Use a three-stage framework: acoustic structure extraction, coarse full-band noise reduction, and spectral refinement.
subtheme_boundary: A binary or soft mask can create musical noise and cannot reliably separate sources that occupy the same region.
A plausible completion can hallucinate phonetic detail the microphone never captured.
A result on fixed background noise does not establish performance under changing or speech-like interference.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: A Three-Stage Beamforming with Harmonic Guidance for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement: The three-stage system estimates acoustic structure, reduces full-band noise, and refines the spectrum; its boundary is enhancement quality versus faithful speech recovery.; Structured Codebook Based Hierarchical Framework for DNN for Computationally Efficient Speech Enhancement: Structured codebooks reduce enhancement cost by exploiting regularities in speech parameters.; Test-Time Training for Speech Enhancement: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate speech-prior-denoising within noise-enhancement.; QUADS: Quantized Distillation Framework for Efficient Speech Language Understanding: Quantized distillation tests how much speech-understanding quality survives when an audio-language system is made smaller and cheaper.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Use a three-stage framework: acoustic structure extraction, coarse full-band noise reduction, and spectral refinement.
Replace one expensive DNN with simpler hierarchical predictors backed by structured speech-parameter codebooks.
Use a Y-shaped enhancement model with self-supervised reconstruction or masked-spectrogram tasks during test-time adaptation.
Train the student with distillation and quantization constraints together through multiple stages.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Three-Stage Beamforming with Harmonic Guidance for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a three-stage framework: acoustic structure extraction, coarse full-band noise reduction, and spectral refinement.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Noisy multi-channel inputs produce speech-structure features that interact with spatial cues before later refinement stages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on LibriSpeech-based datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms the reference method.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improvements over a reference method on LibriSpeech-based datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improvements over a reference method on LibriSpeech-based datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is benchmark-bound and the summary does not establish performance in arbitrary rooms, languages, or devices.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Structured Codebook Based Hierarchical Framework for DNN for Computationally Efficient Speech Enhancement
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Replace one expensive DNN with simpler hierarchical predictors backed by structured speech-parameter codebooks.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Hierarchically clustered log-power-spectrum vectors drive codebook stages and enhancement predictors evaluated on VoiceBank-DEMAND.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This is achieved by using structured codebooks of speech parameters, like log power spectra, that are generated by exploiting hierarchical relation between the speech training data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The framework reduces computation while retaining comparable or improved enhancement scores over the reference systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The framework reduces computation while retaining comparable or improved enhancement scores over the reference systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: One corpus and parameterized spectral targets bound the evidence; downstream ASR and perceptual benefit are not fully established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Test-Time Training for Speech Enhancement
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a Y-shaped enhancement model with self-supervised reconstruction or masked-spectrogram tasks during test-time adaptation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The main enhancement task shares representations with an auxiliary task optimized on the current noisy signal, with strategies trading adaptation gain against test-time cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper introduces a novel application of Test-Time Training (TTT) for Speech Enhancement, addressing the challenges posed by unpredictable noise conditions and domain shifts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports consistent speech-quality improvements over its baseline on synthetic and real-world datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports consistent speech-quality improvements over its baseline on synthetic and real-world datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The adaptation steps, compute budget, noise conditions, and author-reported metrics bound the result; listener benefit and long-term stability remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: QUADS: Quantized Distillation Framework for Efficient Speech Language Understanding
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train the student with distillation and quantization constraints together through multiple stages.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: QUADS jointly optimizes a pretrained SLU model for low-bit regimes and evaluates it on SLURP and FSC.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We propose QUADS, a unified framework that optimizes both through multi-stage training with a pre-trained model, enhancing adaptability to low-bit regimes while maintaining accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 71.13% SLURP and 99.20% FSC accuracy, 60–73x lower GMACs, and 83–700x smaller models with bounded degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 71.13% SLURP and 99.20% FSC accuracy, 60–73x lower GMACs, and 83–700x smaller models with bounded degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result depends on tasks, bit settings, and hardware interpretation of the counts; latency and energy on deployed devices remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Scaling and Enhancing LLM-based AVSR:  A Sparse Mixture of Projectors Approach
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Route audio and visual inputs through sparse modality-specific projectors so capacity grows without activating every expert on every example.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Llama-SMoP uses sparsely gated mixtures of projectors with modality-specific routers and experts and is evaluated on ASR, visual speech recognition, and AVSR under noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Llama-SMoP is evaluated on 433 hours of LRS3 for ASR, VSR, and AVSR, with Llama-AVSR, DCI, and MM-Fuser baselines. WER is measured across model sizes and audio-noise SNR levels from 7.5 to −2.5 dB; the DEDR routing strategy is reported as the strongest SMoP variant.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The DEDR configuration reports the strongest results among the tested variants, with ablations supporting expert activation, scalability, and noise robustness.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The DEDR configuration reports the strongest results among the tested variants, with ablations supporting expert activation, scalability, and noise robustness.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Model size, routing policy, datasets, noise, and compute accounting bound the claim; sparse projector success does not automatically transfer to every multimodal LLM.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards Bitrate-Efficient and Noise-Robust Speech Coding with Variable Bitrate RVQ
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use variable-bitrate residual vector quantization to allocate more representation to important speech frames and combine it with a feature denoiser.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes Variable Bitrate RVQ for noise-robust speech coding.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The codec experiments train on EARS-WHAM with 86.8 hours of training, 1.7 hours validation, and 3.7 hours test audio, using emotion/style variation and paired noisy-clean speech. Intrusive PESQ, STOI, ESTOI, and SI-SDR plus non-intrusive NISQA are evaluated, and Bjøntegaard-Delta rate compares bitrate at matched distortion across 16 and 48 kHz settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved rate-distortion trade-offs and perceptual quality over constant-bitrate baselines in noisy conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved rate-distortion trade-offs and perceptual quality over constant-bitrate baselines in noisy conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Noise conditions, bitrates, codec architecture, datasets, perceptual measures, and model sizes bound the result; a cleaner perceptual signal is not necessarily a faithful waveform.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: DiffDSR: Dysarthric Speech Reconstruction Using Latent Diffusion Model
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Restore phoneme embeddings with a pretrained speech encoder, preserve speaker information through an identity encoder, and generate speech with latent diffusion.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Separate content and identity conditioning feed a diffusion generator that samples a reconstructed waveform in latent space.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Through evaluations on the widely-used UASpeech corpus, our proposed model shows notable enhancements in speech intelligibility and speaker similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved intelligibility and speaker similarity in its dysarthric speech reconstruction evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved intelligibility and speaker similarity in its dysarthric speech reconstruction evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speaker, severity, reference data, perceptual metrics, and diffusion sampling bound transfer; reconstructed speech is not clinical treatment evidence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Device-Directed Speech Detection
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use adaptive knowledge distillation from a frozen ASR acoustic encoder, with task-specific adapters jointly trained with a smaller device-directed-speech student.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes adaptive knowledge distillation for device-directed speech detection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To this end, we propose knowledge distillation (KD) to enhance DDSD accuracy while ensuring efficient deployment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports EER improvements of 26% for keyword and 19% for keyword-free follow-up invocations, with gains across transformer and conformer students.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports EER improvements of 26% for keyword and 19% for keyword-free follow-up invocations, with gains across transformer and conformer students.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Invocation types, EER, teacher/student architectures, training data, and device conditions bound deployment claims; a benchmark detector cannot infer intent perfectly in every home.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: First Analyze Then Enhance: A Task-Aware System for Speech Separation, Denoising, and Dereverberation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Analyze the degradation first, route the signal only through the needed modules, and train the modules separately before integrating them.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A lightweight analyzer uses frozen Whisper/WavLM features, LSTMs, pooling, and a classifier to choose among clean, mixture, noisy/reverberant, and combined conditions. A separator with an attractor estimates an unknown speaker count; a refiner handles noise and reverberation. NAT pretrains separation under noise and DIT trains separator/refiner paths before joint fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The analyze-then-enhance system is evaluated on mixed speech with variable speaker counts using separation, denoising, and dereverberation metrics against its analyzer/enhancer baselines. The controlled tests vary the number of speakers and acoustic degradation; the paper reports the measured signal-recovery and perceptual-quality outcomes within those mixture conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On Libri-3Mix-derived data covering eleven clean, noisy, reverberant, mixed, and combined conditions, FATE reports comparable enhancement quality while reducing unnecessary processing and avoiding overprocessing clean inputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On Libri-3Mix-derived data covering eleven clean, noisy, reverberant, mixed, and combined conditions, FATE reports comparable enhancement quality while reducing unnecessary processing and avoiding overprocessing clean inputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The degradations are simulated and drawn from specified mixtures, noises, and rooms; real rooms, analyzer errors, and out-of-distribution combinations are not established. The reported score is author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improved Intelligibility of Dysarthric Speech using Conditional Flow Matching
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use discrete self-supervised acoustic units and conditional flow matching with a non-autoregressive Diffusion Transformer to map impaired to clearer speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study compares mel-spectrogram and quantized SSL features, controls the output voice with WavLM-derived information, and evaluates generated speech for dysarthric intelligibility.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Conditional flow matching for dysarthric-speech reconstruction is tested on seen and unseen speakers, comparing discrete-unit and mel-spectrogram inputs against wav2vec2-base-960h and a dataset-finetuned wav2vec2 baseline. WER measures transcription intelligibility and 23 self-reported English listeners rate 10 random test utterances on a 1–5 MOS scale; seen/unseen speaker results are separated.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that discrete acoustic units improve intelligibility and converge faster than the mel-spectrogram alternative.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that discrete acoustic units improve intelligibility and converge faster than the mel-spectrogram alternative.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is bounded to the speakers, severity range, target voice, and tested listening/evaluation protocol; naturalness, identity preservation, and clinical benefit remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Objective and Subjective Evaluation of Diffusion-Based Speech  Enhancement for Dysarthric Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare two diffusion enhancers with a signal-processing baseline on typical and dysarthric speech, then measure ASR, objective quality, and listener judgments.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The systems enhance two English dysarthric corpora; Whisper-Turbo is evaluated before and after enhancement and fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We applied speech enhancement to both typical and dysarthric speech and evaluate the ASR performance using Whisper-Turbo, and the subjective and objective speech quality of the original and enhanced dysarthric speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The study reports a systematic comparison rather than a single score; gains and tradeoffs depend on corpus, enhancer, and evaluation target.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The study reports a systematic comparison rather than a single score; gains and tradeoffs depend on corpus, enhancer, and evaluation target.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpora, listener tests, Whisper model, and enhancement settings bound the result; a recognition gain is not automatically a clinical benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multitalker Babble in English Vowel Perception Training: A Comparison between Humans and Neural Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare human vowel-perception training with multitalker babble against neural-model responses.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Babble context is manipulated and perceptual/model error patterns are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Since perception experiments with humans are complex and time-consuming and neural models are inspired by the human brain, we explore the use of neural models and study how well their performance aligns with the results for human listeners.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a comparison of human and neural-model responses in multitalker babble.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a comparison of human and neural-model responses in multitalker babble.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Listeners, babble construction, vowel contrasts, training duration, and model architecture bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: FUSE: Universal Speech Enhancement using Multi‐Stage Fusion of Sparse Compression and Token Generation Models for the URGENT 2025 Challenge
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use three stages: a discriminative sparse-compression enhancer, a codec-token generator that reconstructs missing detail, and a fusion network that combines their different strengths; shift averaging and network blending stabilize the outputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Stage 1 predicts an enhanced waveform with mel and SI-SDR losses. Stage 2 conditions masked codec-token prediction on noisy and Stage-1 features and decodes the predicted tokens. Stage 3 receives the noisy signal and both estimates, then adds speaker, phoneme, and perceptual losses. The data contain 2.5K hours of speech, 550 hours of noise, 60K room responses, seven distortion types, and blind samples with an unseen language.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experimental results on challenging multilingual datasets with variable sampling rates and diverse distortion types validate the effectiveness of our approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On the blind challenge set, the system reports DNSMOS 2.94, NISQA 3.25, UTMOS 2.19, MOS 3.44, and CER 77.09; it ranks behind the top system on several signal-level measures but leads the listed systems on perceptual measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On the blind challenge set, the system reports DNSMOS 2.94, NISQA 3.25, UTMOS 2.19, MOS 3.44, and CER 77.09; it ranks behind the top system on several signal-level measures but leads the listed systems on perceptual measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The challenge mixtures, five training languages, unseen Japanese test condition, and 900-sample blind set define the evidence. The sequential three-stage inference and shift operations restrict real-time use; all results are author-reported and no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Diffusion Buffer: Online Diffusion-based Speech Enhancement with Sub-Second Latency
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a sliding buffer whose corruption schedule gives more noise to frames near the present, then denoise older frames with a controlled delay.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The buffer defines a causal-to-delayed window; diffusion steps operate on that window and output frames once their future context is sufficient.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Diffusion Buffer is evaluated on the 54-hour EARS-WHAM speech-enhancement corpus, whose noisy mixtures span 0–15 dB SNR. PESQ and reference-free WVMOS are reported, with ESTOI used in the intelligibility comparison; tests vary buffer size and reverse diffusion steps and compare vanilla score-based enhancement, OUVE, BBED, and DEMUCS. WVMOS values clipped below 1.0 are a stated metric-handling boundary.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better results than standard diffusion baselines and GPU input-output latency around 0.3–1 seconds.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better results than standard diffusion baselines and GPU input-output latency around 0.3–1 seconds.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: GPU/hardware assumptions, buffer size, noise mixtures, real-time scheduling, and perceptual metrics bound the result; a reported latency range is not a full conversational user study.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multistage Universal Speech Enhancement System for URGENT Challenge
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Cascade specialized modules in a deliberate order: declipping, separation, packet-loss compensation, and spectral inpainting, with a detector deciding when the first and third modules are needed.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Model the degraded signal as a composition of distortion operators; use Demucs for declipping, BSRoformer for separation, BS-PLCNet in a PQMF subband domain for packet loss, and a time-frequency recurrent inpainting network for spectral artifacts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that our system outperforms in multiple evaluation metrics, particularly in improving subjective speech quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The system reports URGENT challenge results competitive with the compared systems; adding inpainting and self-distillation improves several quality measures, while downstream accuracy and objective metrics do not all move together.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The system reports URGENT challenge results competitive with the compared systems; adding inpainting and self-distillation improves several quality measures, while downstream accuracy and objective metrics do not all move together.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge datasets, distortion order, detector errors, resampling to 48 kHz for some modules, metric choice, and author-reported rankings bound the claim; plausible filling is not recovery of the original samples.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Model as Loss: A Self-Consistent Training Paradigm
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use the same model's encoder as a task-specific loss, forcing enhanced output and clean reference to agree in the model's learned feature space.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A speech-enhancement decoder is trained against features from its own encoder and compared with handcrafted and pretrained deep-feature losses on standard benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our approach outperforms pre-trained deep feature losses on standard speech enhancement benchmarks, offering better perceptual quality and robust generalization to both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better perceptual quality than pretrained feature losses and robust generalization in both in-domain and out-of-domain tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better perceptual quality than pretrained feature losses and robust generalization in both in-domain and out-of-domain tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The encoder, training data, noise conditions, perceptual metrics, and benchmark protocols bound the result; feature agreement is not identical to intelligibility or listener preference.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: FlowSE: Efficient and High-Quality Speech Enhancement via Flow Matching
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use flow matching to learn a continuous transport from noisy to clean speech and combine it with efficient architecture and multi-resolution objectives.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A neural velocity field maps a noisy waveform toward the clean distribution; consistency of the trajectory permits few-step integration while spectral and waveform losses preserve detail.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: FlowSE is evaluated on the DNS Challenge Interspeech 2021 test set under reverberant, non-reverberant, and real-recording conditions, plus a simulated VCTK/noise test set with unseen mixtures. DNSMOS is the primary speech-quality measure on the challenge set; the simulated set reports WER and real-time factor, with comparisons to diffusion and non-diffusion enhancement systems. The paper explicitly notes that standard PESQ/SI-SNR may not reflect perceptual quality and uses neural MOS accordingly.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved enhancement quality against generative baselines in both its evaluated scenarios with lower inference cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved enhancement quality against generative baselines in both its evaluated scenarios with lower inference cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Training data, noise conditions, step count, real-time hardware, perceptual metrics, and speaker preservation tests bound the claim; enhancement scores do not establish conversational benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Novel Deep Learning Framework for Efficient Multichannel Acoustic Feedback Control
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine spatial and temporal processing in a recurrent controller and train it in the feedback loop, with teacher forcing and a Wiener-filter hybrid as alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A convolutional recurrent network controls multichannel acoustic feedback; in-loop, teacher-forced, and hybrid training are compared in complex acoustic environments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We introduce a Convolutional Recurrent Network that efficiently combines spatial and temporal processing, significantly enhancing speech enhancement capabilities with lower computational demands.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved speech enhancement with lower computational demand across the proposed training strategies.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved speech enhancement with lower computational demand across the proposed training strategies.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The device geometry, microphones, loudspeakers, feedback paths, training regime, and metrics bound the result; laboratory suppression does not establish stable operation for every room or device.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.
family_synthesis.named_contrast: A Three-Stage Beamforming with Harmonic Guidance for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement versus Structured Codebook Based Hierarchical Framework for DNN for Computationally Efficient Speech Enhancement
family_synthesis.mechanism_contrast: A Three-Stage Beamforming with Harmonic Guidance for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement addresses the pressure by Noisy multi-channel inputs produce speech-structure features that interact with spatial cues before later refinement stages.; Structured Codebook Based Hierarchical Framework for DNN for Computationally Efficient Speech Enhancement addresses it by Hierarchically clustered log-power-spectrum vectors drive codebook stages and enhancement predictors evaluated on VoiceBank-DEMAND.. The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.
family_synthesis.evidence_contrast: The first paper reports The paper reports improvements over a reference method on LibriSpeech-based datasets.; the second reports The framework reduces computation while retaining comparable or improved enhancement scores over the reference systems.. These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.
family_synthesis.failure_boundary_contrast: The first paper leaves open: The evidence is benchmark-bound and the summary does not establish performance in arbitrary rooms, languages, or devices.; the second leaves open: One corpus and parameterized spectral targets bound the evidence; downstream ASR and perceptual benefit are not fully established.. Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
family_synthesis.transfer_question: What would have to remain invariant for this family to work across a new speaker, language, room, device, or task, and which paper evidence here actually tests that transfer?
family_synthesis.evidence_boundary: The shared story is supported only by the reviewed papers listed here; D2 entries support the problem and stated method, while D3 entries support the reported mechanism and evaluation. It is not a venue-wide prevalence claim.
family_synthesis.unresolved_question: What changes when this move is tested outside the speakers, languages, rooms, devices, or benchmark conditions represented by the 18 D3 paper(s)?

concept_families.definition: Estimate how much each local frequency region belongs to speech, then attenuate regions dominated by noise.
concept_families.boundary: A binary or soft mask can create musical noise and cannot reliably separate sources that occupy the same region.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is Estimate how much each local frequency region belongs to speech, then attenuate regions dominated by noise. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as A Three-Stage Beamforming with Harmonic Guidance for Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement: The three-stage system estimates acoustic structure, reduces full-band noise, and refines the spectrum; its boundary is enhancement quality versus faithful speech recovery.; WTFormer: A Wavelet Conformer Network for MIMO Speech Enhancement with Spatial Cues Peservation: A spatially aware enhancement model must suppress interference while preserving the speech cues carried by multiple microphone channels. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A binary or soft mask can create musical noise and cannot reliably separate sources that occupy the same region.

records.subtheme_name: Choosing one source from a mixture
records.question: How can a system decide which part of a mixture belongs to the target talker?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: A listener often hears several talkers, music, echo, and device noise at once, yet needs one person's words or an intelligible mixture. The subtheme asks: How can a system decide which part of a mixture belongs to the target talker?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with blind source separation, but that shortcut misses the boundary: The mixture may not contain enough information to identify sources uniquely; permutation and source-count assumptions matter.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make blind source separation, spatial filtering, target-conditioned separation explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Make target location explicit in a location-aware target-speaker extraction model.
subtheme_boundary: The mixture may not contain enough information to identify sources uniquely; permutation and source-count assumptions matter.
A single microphone or moving speaker removes the spatial cue the method depends on.
Conditioning can lock onto the wrong talker or encode identity without guaranteeing intelligible content.
