d3_comparison_matrix.title: Location-Aware Target Speaker Extraction for Hearing Aids
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Make target location explicit in a location-aware target-speaker extraction model.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Spatial features condition separation toward the selected direction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The evaluation using objective measures demonstrates that our extended model outperforms the baseline system with our novel encoding method achieving superior performance in 16 out of 21 cases.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports location-aware target-speaker extraction for hearing-aid scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports location-aware target-speaker extraction for hearing-aid scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Array geometry, motion, layout, processing, and intelligibility metric bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: ReSepNet: A Unified-Light Model for Recursive Speech Separation with Unknown Speaker Count
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Separate one stream at a time and let a lightweight authorization block decide when recursion should stop.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ReSepNet applies a dual-path transformer repeatedly; each iteration estimates one source and cross-correlation decides whether another iteration is needed. It trains on two/three-speaker mixtures and tests on four/five.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We demonstrate the effectiveness of ReSepNet on the WSJ0 datasets, achieving state-of-the-art separation performance and accurate speaker count estimation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports higher SI-SNR improvement than listed baselines and generalization from two/three-speaker training to four/five-speaker tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports higher SI-SNR improvement than listed baselines and generalization from two/three-speaker training to four/five-speaker tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is synthetic WSJ0 mixtures, 8-kHz four-second windows, and a bounded count range; real rooms and end-to-end recognition are not tested. Results are author-reported.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Deep-Simplex Multichannel Speech Separation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a deep-simplex formulation that combines multichannel spatial evidence with a representation able to handle recursive or variable separation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model consumes multichannel mixtures, estimates source structure and spatial cues, and recursively extracts separated streams; experiments compare source-count and computational behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: While deep-learning-based models often outperform conventional methods, they require large training datasets and struggle to generalize to new settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports multichannel separation results with a deep-simplex approach designed for variable source conditions and compares it with established separators.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports multichannel separation results with a deep-simplex approach designed for variable source conditions and compares it with established separators.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Performance depends on microphone geometry, room conditions, source count, and the reference metrics; synthetic mixtures may not represent real overlap. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Relative cue weighting in multilingual stop voicing production
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure nine acoustic correlates in Malay, English, and Mandarin speech from early multilingual Malaysians and use random forests to compare cue weighting.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies relative cue weighting in multilingual stop-voicing production.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The analysis uses 7,504 annotated stop tokens from Malaysian speakers across Malay, English, and Mandarin, with four dominance/repertoire groups. Closure voicing, VOT, burst intensity, vowel duration, and onset f0/F1 slopes are normalized by language and speaker and modeled with random-forest classification and cue-weight comparisons across languages and speaker groups.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports language-specific production for all early multilinguals, dominance-driven variation, and a salient role for closure voicing in Malaysian English.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports language-specific production for all early multilinguals, dominance-driven variation, and a salient role for closure voicing in Malaysian English.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The Malaysian speakers, three languages, stop inventory, nine correlates, and random-forest analysis bound generalization to other multilingual populations or contrasts.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Study of Real-world Audio-Visual Corpus Design and Production: A Perspective from MISP Challenges
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Design the corpus around deployment scenarios, synchronized equipment, annotation and alignment procedures, and explicit task requirements, then inspect how those choices shape downstream results.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper analyzes the MISP 2022–2024 corpora for audio-visual wakeup, diarization, enhancement, and recognition, covering scenario selection, recording equipment/processes, manual transcription, and alignment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this context, the MISP challenges were organized at ICASSP 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports broad adoption of the corpora by over 110 teams and identifies design strengths and limitations that affect audio-visual speech-processing comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports broad adoption of the corpora by over 110 teams and identifies design strengths and limitations that affect audio-visual speech-processing comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge construction, participant selection, language, room/device coverage, and annotation policy bound generalization; downloading or winning on a corpus does not prove deployment realism.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SoundSculpt: Direction and Semantics Driven Ambisonic Target Sound Extraction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Condition an ambisonic-in/ambisonic-out extractor jointly on target direction and semantic embeddings, and test whether the cues complement one another.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The network maps multichannel ambisonic mixtures to a target sound field; direction and image-derived semantic embeddings guide the mask or representation used for extraction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Trained and evaluated on synthetic and real ambisonic mixtures, SoundSculpt demonstrates superior performance compared to various signal processing baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: SoundSculpt outperforms the reported signal-processing baselines on synthetic and real ambisonic mixtures, with joint spatial-semantic conditioning helping in difficult cases.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: SoundSculpt outperforms the reported signal-processing baselines on synthetic and real ambisonic mixtures, with joint spatial-semantic conditioning helping in difficult cases.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Synthetic scene construction, ambisonic order, semantic detector quality, room conditions, and target definition bound transfer; benchmark improvement is not guaranteed perceptual source isolation in arbitrary rooms.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Spatio-Spectral Diarization of Meetings by Combining TDOA-based Segmentation and Speaker Embedding-based Clustering
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Segment with time-difference-of-arrival cues, cluster speaker embeddings, and combine spatial and spectral evidence.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: TDOA detects regions, embeddings assign speakers, cACGMM optionally refines them, and compact/distributed microphone setups are tested.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The spatio-spectral diarization pipeline is evaluated on 10-minute LibriCSS eight-speaker meetings with 0–40% overlap and LibriW ASN re-recordings in two rooms with T60 values of 200/800 ms. Four microphones are used for diarization and DER is reported without a forgiveness collar; downstream seven-channel ASR uses concatenated minimum-permutation WER via MeetEval.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The combined pipeline outperforms single-channel pyannote in reported compact and distributed meeting scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The combined pipeline outperforms single-channel pyannote in reported compact and distributed meeting scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Layouts, datasets, overlap, and spatial cues bound the result; evaluations are author-reported.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: NeuroSpex+: Dual-Task Training of Neuro-Guided Speaker Extraction with Speech Envelope and Waveform
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train jointly to reconstruct both target waveform and target speech envelope, reinforcing the extraction mask.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A shared model predicts the target signal and its envelope; the dual losses constrain both fine waveform detail and slower attended-speech structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: NeuroSpex+ uses 128 KULeuven speech-EEG trials from 16 subjects in subject-independent 16-fold cross-validation, with 4-second windows yielding 39,984 training and 2,856 validation/test segments per fold. Speaker extraction is evaluated with SDRi, SI-SDRi, PESQ, and STOI; envelope reconstruction uses Pearson correlation, compared with NeuroSpex, NeuroHeed, and BISS.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: NeuroSpex+ reports improved overall signal quality over baselines in the evaluated neuro-guided extraction setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: NeuroSpex+ reports improved overall signal quality over baselines in the evaluated neuro-guided extraction setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: EEG alignment, subjects, mixtures, signal metric, and lab conditions bound transfer; signal quality is not a demonstrated BCI communication benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: MOPSA: Mixture of Prompt-Experts Based Speaker Adaptation for Elderly Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Cluster speaker prompts into experts and let a router mix acoustic and language prompts for the new speaker at run time.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MOPSA uses K-means speaker prompt clusters and a router around Whisper, with separate acoustic and language-level prompts, tested on English and Cantonese elderly speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Top-K most distinctive speaker prompt clusters derived using K-means serve as experts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports relative WER/CER reductions of 4.21% and 5.40% and up to 16.12x real-time speedup over offline adaptation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports relative WER/CER reductions of 4.21% and 5.40% and up to 16.12x real-time speedup over offline adaptation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, elderly populations, prompt clusters, and Whisper versions bound the claim; broader disorders, languages, and online failure recovery remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Synchronous analysis of abnormal acoustic and linguistic production in Parkinson's speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure acoustic and linguistic production synchronously in the same speech material and examine their joint relationship.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study synchronizes analysis of abnormal acoustic and linguistic production in Parkinson's speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Parkinson's-speech analysis uses 80 speakers, 40 with Parkinson's disease and 40 healthy controls, reading and retelling a text. Five-fold external nested cross-validation evaluates frame-wise and subject-wise classification with accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1; lexical/linguistic analyses use only held-out test predictions to avoid leakage.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports coordinated acoustic and linguistic findings in Parkinson's speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports coordinated acoustic and linguistic findings in Parkinson's speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Cohort, task, disease stage, annotation, and statistical design limit clinical generalization; association is not diagnosis or causation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: IDIR: Identifying and Distilling Informative Relations for Speaker Verification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Distill informative within-speaker and between-speaker relations, then add a margin that pulls same-speaker pairs together and pushes different-speaker pairs apart.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: IDIR identifies informative relations in each mini-batch, distills them from teacher to student, and uses margin-adjusted similarity scores for speaker verification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations with a simple x-vector student network demonstrate the method's superb performance across three test sets, showcasing its merits and effectiveness.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved speaker-verification performance over feature-matching distillation and stronger separation of same- and different-speaker relations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved speaker-verification performance over feature-matching distillation and stronger separation of same- and different-speaker relations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Teacher/student architectures, pair mining, margin, dataset, and verification protocol bound the claim; relational distillation does not ensure robustness to domain, overlap, or fairness shifts.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Deep learning based spatial aliasing reduction in beamforming for audio capture
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Predict a signal-dependent de-aliasing filter with a U-Net and apply it to conventional beamforming, comparing independent-channel and cross-channel designs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model estimates a filter from multichannel spectro-temporal input; the corrected beamformer output is evaluated in common spatial-capture scenarios against conventional and learned alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Spatial aliasing affects spaced microphone arrays, causing directional ambiguity above certain frequencies, degrading spatial and spectral accuracy of beamformers.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports reduced spatial aliasing and improved spatial/spectral capture measures for the proposed deep-learning correction in the tested scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports reduced spatial aliasing and improved spatial/spectral capture measures for the proposed deep-learning correction in the tested scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Array geometry, source locations, reverberation, training mixtures, and scenario coverage constrain generalization; simulated or benchmark gains do not establish robustness for every microphone layout.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: CabinSep: IR-Augmented Mask-Based MVDR for Real-Time In-car Speech Separation with Distributed Heterogeneous Arrays
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine channel-aware spatial features with mask-based MVDR, augment training with both simulated and real impulse responses, and evaluate the separated signal through ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The mask estimates speech/noise structure from multichannel features; MVDR uses spatial covariance to preserve the chosen target, while mixed impulse-response augmentation exposes zone-boundary variation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Separating overlapping speech from multiple speakers is crucial for effective human-vehicle interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: CabinSep reports a 17.5% relative ASR error reduction over DualSep on real recordings at 0.4 GMACs, with better behavior around speaker-zone boundaries.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: CabinSep reports a 17.5% relative ASR error reduction over DualSep on real recordings at 0.4 GMACs, with better behavior around speaker-zone boundaries.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Cabin geometry, array placement, impulse-response coverage, ASR backend, and compute measure constrain generalization; ASR improvement is not proof of perceptual superiority for every listener.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Overlap-Adaptive Hybrid Speaker Diarization and ASR-Aware Observation Addition for MISP 2025 Challenge
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine overlap-adaptive diarization with ASR-aware observation addition and a cascaded meeting-recognition system.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A hybrid segmentation/clustering diarizer selects its model by overlap, while ASR-aware observations compensate for weak guided separation before recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our system achieved character error rates (CER) of 9.48% on Track 2 and concatenated minimum permutation character error rate (cpCER) of 11.56% on Track 3, ultimately securing first place in both tracks and thereby demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed methods in real-world meeting scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The system reports 9.48% CER and 11.56% cpCER and first place in both MISP tracks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The system reports 9.48% CER and 11.56% cpCER and first place in both MISP tracks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge tracks, meeting conditions, and author-reported ranking limit generalization and independent reproduction.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Neural Speech Extraction with Human Feedback
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use human feedback to guide neural speech extraction toward the target source.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Human preference supplies a target-selection signal alongside acoustic separation; the model is evaluated on extraction behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present the first neural target speech extraction (TSE) system that uses human feedback for iterative refinement.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports neural speech extraction with human feedback.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports neural speech extraction with human feedback.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Feedback population, mixture construction, target definition, signal metrics, and model scope bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: End-to-End DOA-Guided Speech Extraction in Noisy Multi-Talker Scenarios
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Guide an end-to-end target extractor with DOA and beamwidth embeddings so the requested spatial region becomes an explicit conditioning signal.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model combines spatial and temporal features, uses the DOA as a center and beamwidth as the permitted region, and generates the target waveform for enhancement and ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: DOA-guided speech extraction is evaluated on synthetic six-speaker, noisy, reverberant 4-second mixtures generated from LibriSpeech and DEMAND, with 14.4k/3.6k/2k train/validation/test mixtures. SDRi, SI-SDRi, and PESQ measure extraction quality while parameter count measures efficiency; ablations vary one-hot versus cyclic DOA embeddings, beamwidth, and inactive DOA inputs, and comparisons include MVDR and JNF. A downstream two-dataset ASR test reports WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports stronger target enhancement, interference suppression, and downstream ASR performance in the evaluated noisy multi-talker scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports stronger target enhancement, interference suppression, and downstream ASR performance in the evaluated noisy multi-talker scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: DOA estimation, array geometry, spatial overlap, noise type, beamwidth selection, and benchmark composition bound transfer; reported ASR gains do not establish universal spatial hearing quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: FlowTSE: Target Speaker Extraction with Flow Matching
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Condition flow matching on enrollment and mixture mel-spectrograms, and condition a vocoder on the mixture’s complex STFT when phase matters.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A learned flow transports a noisy conditional distribution toward target speech; complex-STFT conditioning supplies phase information that mel features discard.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: While most existing approaches are discriminative, recent generative methods for TSE achieve strong results.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that FlowTSE matches or outperforms strong target-speaker-extraction baselines on standard benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that FlowTSE matches or outperforms strong target-speaker-extraction baselines on standard benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Enrollment quality, speaker/noise shift, phase-vocoder design, benchmark mixtures, and signal metrics bound transfer; extraction quality is not automatically improved ASR or hearing-aid benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Online Audio-Visual Autoregressive Speaker Extraction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a lightweight visual front end and an autoregressive acoustic encoder that feeds past separated speech back into the online model, then test target-switching scenes.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Visual embeddings select the target, while the recurrent acoustic path summarizes prior separated audio; the mask is updated causally under a compute budget.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In the streaming regime, most studies optimize the audio network only, leaving the visual frontend less explored.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On LRS3, the paper reports competitive separation quality with about 0.1M visual parameters and 2.1 MACs/s, and evaluates switching attention.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On LRS3, the paper reports competitive separation quality with about 0.1M visual parameters and 2.1 MACs/s, and evaluates switching attention.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: LRS3 faces, switching schedule, audiovisual synchronization, causal latency, and separation metrics bound transfer; benchmark separation is not a full human-attention study.

concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 9 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

records.subtheme_name: Removing echo and repairing missing evidence
records.question: When should the system cancel an unwanted copy and when must it reconstruct what is no longer observed?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: A listener often hears several talkers, music, echo, and device noise at once, yet needs one person's words or an intelligible mixture. The subtheme asks: When should the system cancel an unwanted copy and when must it reconstruct what is no longer observed?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with acoustic echo cancellation, but that shortcut misses the boundary: The loudspeaker path changes with movement and delay; an imperfect estimate can cancel near-end speech.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make acoustic echo cancellation, packet-loss concealment, perceptual enhancement explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Separate linguistic/prosodic prediction from neural phase reconstruction, then use a neural vocoder and a learned MOSA evaluator.
subtheme_boundary: The loudspeaker path changes with movement and delay; an imperfect estimate can cancel near-end speech.
Short plausible continuation is not recovery of the original utterance and becomes unsafe over long gaps.
A perceptual score can hide distortions important for recognition, speaker identity, or forensic use.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: MiSTR: Multi-Modal iEEG-to-Speech Synthesis with Transformer-Based Prosody Prediction and Neural Phase Reconstruction: Neural-signal speech reconstruction separates content/prosody prediction from waveform phase reconstruction.; Voice-ENHANCE: Speech Restoration using a Diffusion-based Voice Conversion Framework: The system reconstructs missing or damaged speech with a speaker-agnostic stage followed by identity-guided diffusion restoration.; A Deformable Convolution GAN Approach for Speech Dereverberation in Cochlear Implant Users: Dereverberation repairs temporal smearing especially harmful to cochlear-implant listeners; the target is intelligible speech, not merely a cleaner spectrum.; Modality-Agnostic Multimodal Emotion Recognition using a Contrastive Masked Autoencoder: Modality-agnostic emotion recognition must recover useful affective evidence when one audio or visual channel is missing or corrupted.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Separate linguistic/prosodic prediction from neural phase reconstruction, then use a neural vocoder and a learned MOSA evaluator.
Stage a speaker-agnostic generative restoration model first, then use a clean target-speaker embedding to refine the restored speech through a voice-conversion-style diffusion decoder.
Let deformable convolution move its receptive field to the distortion, and evaluate both signal measures and listeners with cochlear implants.
Align modalities contrastively and use masked reconstruction in one modality-agnostic model, then test unimodal, multimodal, and missing-modality cases.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: MiSTR: Multi-Modal iEEG-to-Speech Synthesis with Transformer-Based Prosody Prediction and Neural Phase Reconstruction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Separate linguistic/prosodic prediction from neural phase reconstruction, then use a neural vocoder and a learned MOSA evaluator.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MiSTR uses a multimodal iEEG encoder, Transformer spectrogram/prosody prediction, and a neural phase vocoder with adaptive spectral correction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluated on a public iEEG dataset, MiSTR achieves state-of-the-art speech intelligibility, with a mean Pearson correlation of 0.91 between reconstructed and original Mel spectrograms, improving over existing neural speech synthesis baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports higher fidelity and naturalness than listed baselines and MOSA 3.38.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports higher fidelity and naturalness than listed baselines and MOSA 3.38.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset, subjects, protocol, learned evaluator, and paper-reported comparisons limit clinical claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Voice-ENHANCE: Speech Restoration using a Diffusion-based Voice Conversion Framework
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Stage a speaker-agnostic generative restoration model first, then use a clean target-speaker embedding to refine the restored speech through a voice-conversion-style diffusion decoder.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: GSR predicts additive corrections to mel features with a ResU-Net and vocoder, covering noise, reverberation, bandwidth extension, clipping, packet loss, and codec artifacts. The second stage extracts HuBERT discrete content and an ECAPA speaker embedding, predicts a coarse spectrogram, and uses a diffusion U-Net conditioned on content and identity to generate the final waveform.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: By employing this two-stage approach, we have achieved speech quality objective metric scores comparable to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods across multiple datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that GSR+VC obtains strong objective quality scores across simulated noise, packet loss, bandwidth, reverberation, and codec conditions and compares favorably with the cited restoration systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that GSR+VC obtains strong objective quality scores across simulated noise, packet loss, bandwidth, reverberation, and codec conditions and compares favorably with the cited restoration systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Training uses a proprietary restoration corpus and evaluation uses small/simulated validation settings; non-intrusive quality proxies do not establish word correctness or speaker-faithful repair. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Deformable Convolution GAN Approach for Speech Dereverberation in Cochlear Implant Users
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Let deformable convolution move its receptive field to the distortion, and evaluate both signal measures and listeners with cochlear implants.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A deformable-convolution GAN is trained for dereverberation, first tested on REVERB and then assessed in listening tests with normal-hearing and CI users.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We first evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method on REVERB challenge dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports markedly improved CI speech intelligibility by preserving envelope and transient structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports markedly improved CI speech intelligibility by preserving envelope and transient structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The claim is bounded to REVERB conditions, the tested listeners, and the GAN configuration; broader hearing profiles, rooms, and independent replication remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Modality-Agnostic Multimodal Emotion Recognition using a Contrastive Masked Autoencoder
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align modalities contrastively and use masked reconstruction in one modality-agnostic model, then test unimodal, multimodal, and missing-modality cases.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes a contrastive masked-autoencoder model for modality-agnostic multimodal emotion recognition on MSP-Podcast.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experimental results on the MSP-Podcast corpus show that our unified model achieves state-of-the-art performance, and improves both unimodal and multimodal baselines by 1-5% relative in respective evaluation metrics with the capability to handle missing modalities for two emotion recognition tasks in a more compact model.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improvements over unimodal and multimodal baselines and robustness to missing modalities.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improvements over unimodal and multimodal baselines and robustness to missing modalities.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Corpus, emotion labels, missingness pattern, modality quality, and reconstruction objective bound the claim; emotion inference is not guaranteed to be socially reliable.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Listen through the Sound: Generative Speech Restoration Leveraging Acoustic Context Representation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add an acoustic-context representation that describes the distortion and its intensity, then condition the restoration model on it.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ACX refines CLAP-derived environmental embeddings and conditions the diffusion restoration model UNIVERSE++ across distortion conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Specifically, we employ the diffusion-based generative restoration model, UNIVERSE++, as a backbone to evaluate the effectiveness of contextual representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better restoration and reduced performance variability with acoustic context.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better restoration and reduced performance variability with acoustic context.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is tied to the distortion set, CLAP features, and diffusion backbone; unseen devices, rooms, and perceptual listeners remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Discovering Directions of Uncertainty in Speech Inpainting
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use Neural Principal Probability Components to represent the posterior over possible inpaintings and compare it with dropout sampling.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: NPPC predicts principal components of the conditional output distribution; traversing components produces alternative spectrograms and transcripts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our empirical results demonstrate that these directions capture diverse and meaningful variations in both speech content and style, while more precisely capturing the predictive error compared to a more costly Bayesian deep learning approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Principal directions change word identity and pitch; NPPC captures diverse outputs while matching or improving dropout error.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Principal directions change word identity and pitch; NPPC captures diverse outputs while matching or improving dropout error.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The data, posterior approximation, audio examples, and benchmark define the result; calibration and user decision rules remain unresolved.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Linguistic Masking and Its Release in Simulated Electric-acoustic Hearing
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare electric-acoustic stimulation with implant-only simulation under Mandarin, Cantonese, and English two-talker maskers.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Mandarin sentences are mixed with language-controlled babble, processed by noise vocoders simulating CI or EAS hearing, and scored through sentence recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The present study aimed to investigate this advantage in the context of linguistic masking, i.e., when the target speech and masker were from the same or different languages, and how combined stimulation and different linguistic masker affected linguistic release from masking (LRM).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The study reports a combined-stimulation advantage across all three masker languages and language-specific differences in release from masking.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The study reports a combined-stimulation advantage across all three masker languages and language-specific differences in release from masking.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Normal-hearing listeners, vocoder simulations, Mandarin targets, and the selected masker languages limit direct claims about real CI users and everyday rooms.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Extended Loss: Incorporating Long Context into Training Models when using Short Audio Frames
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Keep long-context information in each training batch while producing short-frame outputs, so the model learns continuity without increasing application delay.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes Extended Loss for acoustic echo cancellation with short audio frames and limited latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Most existing works focus on architecture design and ignore practical issues such as the effect of frame length on the performance of end-to-end AEC models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports reduced boundary discontinuities and improved short-frame AEC performance under the tested real-time conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports reduced boundary discontinuities and improved short-frame AEC performance under the tested real-time conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Echo paths, frame size, batch context, hardware, and evaluation signals bound the claim; continuity on the benchmark is not proof of every room or device.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Efficient Neural and Numerical Methods for High-QualityOnline Speech Spectrogram Inversion via Gradient Theorem
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Predict phase derivatives with a tiny network and exploit the tridiagonal positive-semidefinite structure of the resulting least-squares system.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The online inversion model uses 8k parameters, adds at most one hop of latency, and applies a linear-complexity solver after predicting derivative information.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The spectrogram-inversion methods are trained on LibriSpeech train-clean-360 (363.6 hours, 921 speakers) and evaluated on 50 random utterances from test-clean (5.4 hours, 40 speakers). ESTOI, SI-SDR, and PESQ compare the proposed neural/numerical methods across window sizes from 128 to 8192, with runtime also reported.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 30x smaller network, a further halving of neural cost with one-hop latency, and orders-of-magnitude solver speedup while retaining quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 30x smaller network, a further halving of neural cost with one-hop latency, and orders-of-magnitude solver speedup while retaining quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Spectrogram settings, audio domain, latency definition, and samples bound the claim; listening tests and hardware deployment remain separate checks.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Vision-Integrated High-Quality Neural Speech Coding
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Integrate visual cues into a high-quality neural speech coder and measure quality, rate, and behavior across audio-visual conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper presents a vision-integrated high-quality neural speech coding system.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: VNSC is evaluated on the TaL80 corpus: 11,478 training, 810 validation, and 1,140 mutually exclusive test utterances from 81 speakers, at a 6-kbps codec rate. PESQ, CSIG, CBAK, COVL, STOI, and ViSQOL compare visual-available and visual-unavailable VNSC with MDCTCodec, SoundStream, Encodec, and HiFi-Codec; a validation ablation varies feature-fusion depth and image reconstruction loss, and a noisy test set adds SSNR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports high-quality neural coding results for the tested audio-visual conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports high-quality neural coding results for the tested audio-visual conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Video quality, synchronization, speakers, bitrate, decoder, and missing-video behavior bound the claim; visual assistance can introduce privacy and spoofing risks.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: PAST: Phonetic-Acoustic Speech Tokenizer
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a phonetic-acoustic tokenizer and evaluate whether its tokens capture both speech sound structure and useful phonetic distinctions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: PAST is a phonetic-acoustic speech tokenizer.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Results demonstrate that PAST surpasses existing evaluated baseline tokenizers across common evaluation metrics, including phonetic representation and speech reconstruction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports tokenizer quality and downstream speech-representation results for the proposed phonetic-acoustic units.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports tokenizer quality and downstream speech-representation results for the proposed phonetic-acoustic units.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Token rate, codebook, languages, speakers, reconstruction target, and downstream tasks bound the claim; discrete units are not automatically linguistically complete.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: VoiceNoNG: Robust High-Quality Speech Editing Model without Hallucinations
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a robust high-quality speech editor whose context use is constrained and evaluate whether edits remain faithful without hallucinations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: VoiceNoNG is a robust high-quality speech-editing model designed to avoid hallucinations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Voicebox and VoiceCraft are the current most representative models for non-autoregressive and autoregressive speech editing, respectively.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports speech-editing quality and reduced hallucination behavior for the tested edits.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports speech-editing quality and reduced hallucination behavior for the tested edits.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Edit type, context length, speaker set, alignment, metrics, and human judgments bound the claim; no-hallucination behavior is not guaranteed under arbitrary prompts.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Benchmarking Neural Speech Codec Intelligibility with SITool
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Provide a standardized rhyme-test toolkit and compare its subjective results with objective intelligibility measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SITool runs Diagnostic and Modified Rhyme Tests in laboratory or crowdsourcing settings; thirteen codecs are evaluated with phoneme, gender, and wordlist analyses.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speech intelligibility assessment is essential for evaluating neural speech codecs, yet most evaluation efforts focus on overall quality rather than intelligibility.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Some neural codecs outperform traditional codecs in subjective intelligibility, but objective agreement varies and scores show gender- and wordlist-specific differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Some neural codecs outperform traditional codecs in subjective intelligibility, but objective agreement varies and scores show gender- and wordlist-specific differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The codec set, English tests, listener screening, and objective metrics bound the conclusion; the toolkit does not remove human evaluation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SpeechRefiner: Towards Perceptual Quality Refinement for Front-End Algorithms
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use SpeechRefiner to learn perceptual quality refinement for outputs from varied front-end algorithms and evaluate quality and faithfulness.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SpeechRefiner targets perceptual quality refinement for front-end speech algorithms.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Such deficiencies are typically not captured by metrics like SI-SNR but are noticeable to human listeners.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports perceptual and signal-quality improvements for refined front-end outputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports perceptual and signal-quality improvements for refined front-end outputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Front-end types, distortion, training targets, listeners, metrics, and content preservation bound the result; quality improvement is not guaranteed for unseen algorithms.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: HWB-Net: A Novel High-Performance and Efficient Hybrid Waveform Bandwidth Extension Method
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a hybrid waveform bandwidth-extension network and evaluate reconstruction quality, speech content, and perceptual naturalness.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: HWB-Net is a high-performance efficient hybrid waveform bandwidth-extension method.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations demonstrate HWB-Net’s competitive performance and practical viability for real-time communication through balanced efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports quality and efficiency results for HWB-Net on bandwidth-extension tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports quality and efficiency results for HWB-Net on bandwidth-extension tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Bandwidth limit, speakers, noise, training targets, metrics, and listening protocol bound the result; plausible detail is not recovered ground truth.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Neural Codec Approach for Noise-Robust Bandwidth Expansion
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a neural codec approach that jointly supports noise-robust bandwidth expansion and evaluates speech quality under noisy inputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes a neural codec approach for noise-robust bandwidth expansion.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We investigated several strategies for generating the clean indices and compared our approach with state-of-the-art methods on the Valentini-Botinhao noisy test set.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports bandwidth-expansion quality and noise robustness for the proposed neural codec.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports bandwidth-expansion quality and noise robustness for the proposed neural codec.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Noise types, bandwidth, codec rate, speakers, targets, and perceptual evaluation bound the result; plausible high-frequency detail is not ground truth.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Rollback Speech: Smart Feedback Prompts for Lost Utterances in Unstable Online Calls
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare local and remote ASR streams, identify unreceived content after reconnection, extract keywords from the missing segment, and prompt the speaker to repeat only the relevant information.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The system is an interaction loop: dual transcripts provide two views of the communication event, discrepancy detection estimates the missing interval, and keyword extraction compresses the repair request into actionable cues.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: When connection issues cause parts of a speaker’s audio to be lost, the system uses dual automatic speech recognition (ASR) outputs—one local and one remote—to detect which utterances were not received.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper demonstrates a WebRTC/WebSocket prototype using Whisper and NLTK keyword extraction in a simulated brief disconnection; it is a show-and-tell feasibility demonstration rather than a controlled recovery benchmark.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper demonstrates a WebRTC/WebSocket prototype using Whisper and NLTK keyword extraction in a simulated brief disconnection; it is a show-and-tell feasibility demonstration rather than a controlled recovery benchmark.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Two-person demonstration conditions, simulated network failure, ASR errors, keyword quality, privacy/latency trade-offs, and absence of a listening study bound the result.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: TS-URGENet: A Three-stage Universal Robust and Generalizable Speech Enhancement Network
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a three-stage pipeline: filling, separation, and restoration.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The filling stage predicts lost regions, separation suppresses noise/reverb/clipping, and restoration repairs bandwidth, codec, and remaining loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: TS-URGENet is evaluated on an official validation set and an official blind test set using DNSMOS, NISQA, UTMOS, PESQ/POLQA, ESTOI, SDR, MCD, LSD, SpeechBERTScore, phonetic similarity, speaker similarity, content accuracy, and MOS. Ablations add metric-aware fine-tuning terms and joint-stage training; the blind test compares the final model with a baseline across the full metric panel. The official blind-set origin and metric-specific tradeoffs bound the claim beyond the reported benchmark.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The system ranked second in URGENT Track 1.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The system ranked second in URGENT Track 1.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge conditions, author-reported ranking, and no independent run limit the claim.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Analysis and Extension of a Near-End Listening Enhancement Method Based on Long-Term Fractile Noise Statistics
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Estimate long-term fractile noise statistics and use them to guide near-end listening enhancement, then test the method against speech and noise conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper analyzes and extends a near-end listening-enhancement method based on long-term fractile noise statistics.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Near-end listening enhancement is evaluated in simulations using speech from Dantale II, American English, AEMST, and TIMIT, competing-speaker noise, speech-shaped noise, and UrbanSound8K backgrounds across SNR conditions. OptFractASII and competing spectral-shaping/time-frequency allocation methods are compared with ESTOI, STGI, and related intelligibility/quality measures; results are pooled over speech datasets and grouped SNR ranges. The evidence is simulation-based and does not establish listener-level or real-device performance.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports listening-enhancement results for the proposed statistical method and its extension.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports listening-enhancement results for the proposed statistical method and its extension.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Noise type, recordings, listeners, parameter settings, and perceptual tests limit generalization; improved quality is not identical to improved intelligibility.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Room Impulse Response as a Prompt for Acoustic Echo Cancellation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Give the model a room impulse response as a prompt so it can condition cancellation on acoustic structure at test time.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ICCRN receives several RIR-prompt fusion variants; tests cover matched and mismatched synthetic RIRs plus recorded real RIRs in double-talk and far-end single-talk conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Data-driven acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) methods, predominantly trained on synthetic or constrained real-world datasets, encounter performance declines in unseen echo scenarios, especially in real environments where echo paths are not directly observable.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Fusion method (d) is strongest on mismatched and real-RIR ICCRN tests; the reported real-RIR double-talk values are PESQ 2.19 and ERLE 4.79.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Fusion method (d) is strongest on mismatched and real-RIR ICCRN tests; the reported real-RIR double-talk values are PESQ 2.19 and ERLE 4.79.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The selected model, fusion choices, RIRs, and author-reported tables bound the claim; independent reproduction and broad room coverage remain absent.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

family_synthesis.mechanism_contrast: MiSTR: Multi-Modal iEEG-to-Speech Synthesis with Transformer-Based Prosody Prediction and Neural Phase Reconstruction addresses the pressure by MiSTR uses a multimodal iEEG encoder, Transformer spectrogram/prosody prediction, and a neural phase vocoder with adaptive spectral correction.; Voice-ENHANCE: Speech Restoration using a Diffusion-based Voice Conversion Framework addresses it by GSR predicts additive corrections to mel features with a ResU-Net and vocoder, covering noise, reverberation, bandwidth extension, clipping, packet loss, and codec artifacts. The second stage extracts HuBERT discrete content and an ECAPA speaker embedding, predicts a coarse spectrogram, and uses a diffusion U-Net conditioned on content and identity to generate the final waveform.. The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

No independent reproduction was performed.. Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
family_synthesis.transfer_question: What would have to remain invariant for this family to work across a new speaker, language, room, device, or task, and which paper evidence here actually tests that transfer?
family_synthesis.evidence_boundary: The shared story is supported only by the reviewed papers listed here; D2 entries support the problem and stated method, while D3 entries support the reported mechanism and evaluation. It is not a venue-wide prevalence claim.

concept_families.definition: Use the known far-end playback signal to predict the speaker signal that returns through the room, then subtract that predicted copy.
concept_families.boundary: The loudspeaker path changes with movement and delay; an imperfect estimate can cancel near-end speech.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is Use the known far-end playback signal to predict the speaker signal that returns through the room, then subtract that predicted copy. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as CAGCRN: Real-Time Speech Enhancement with a Lightweight Model for Joint Acoustic Echo Cancellation and Noise Suppression: The preserved abstract identifies a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate acoustic-echo-cancellation under echo-and-reconstruction; this upgrades a provisional candidate to analyst-reviewed taxonomy membership only.; Exploiting Echo Path Priors for Enhanced Stereo Acoustic Echo Cancellation: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate acoustic-echo-cancellation under echo-and-reconstruction; this resolves taxonomy membership only.; Room Impulse Response as a Prompt for Acoustic Echo Cancellation: Room impulse response prompts condition echo cancellation on the physical echo path to improve mismatch generalization. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: The loudspeaker path changes with movement and delay; an imperfect estimate can cancel near-end speech.
concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 1 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

concept_families.definition: When transmitted audio frames disappear, infer a short continuation from nearby waveform or speech structure so playback does not break.
concept_families.boundary: Short plausible continuation is not recovery of the original utterance and becomes unsafe over long gaps.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is When transmitted audio frames disappear, infer a short continuation from nearby waveform or speech structure so playback does not break. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Discovering Directions of Uncertainty in Speech Inpainting: Speech inpainting represents multiple plausible repairs so missing evidence is not mistaken for known content.; Extended Loss: Incorporating Long Context into Training Models when using Short Audio Frames: Short audio windows can hide long-range context; the paper asks whether adding broader context restores information needed for the decision.; Rollback Speech: Smart Feedback Prompts for Lost Utterances in Unstable Online Calls: The preserved abstract identifies a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate packet-loss-concealment under echo-and-reconstruction; this upgrades a provisional candidate to analyst-reviewed taxonomy membership only. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: Short plausible continuation is not recovery of the original utterance and becomes unsafe over long gaps.
concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 4 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

records.subtheme_name: Mapping continuous acoustics to linguistic units
records.question: How can changing sound be assigned to phones, words, or tokens without visible boundaries?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech has no visible spaces between words, and pronunciation, speed, accent, noise, and hesitation vary even when the intended sentence is the same. The subtheme asks: How can changing sound be assigned to phones, words, or tokens without visible boundaries?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with acoustic-to-token mapping, but that shortcut misses the boundary: The highest-scoring sequence may exploit dataset regularities instead of matching the actual speech.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make acoustic-to-token mapping, learned speech units, pronunciation variation explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Benchmark CTC, Whisper, and LLM-enhanced decoders, including bridge networks and a Q-Former that connects Whisper acoustic features to Vicuna for context-aware decoding.
subtheme_boundary: The highest-scoring sequence may exploit dataset regularities instead of matching the actual speech.
A useful pretraining prediction need not produce units aligned with words, phonemes, or human categories.
Adding variants without evidence can increase confusions and may encode an accent as an error.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Bridging ASR and LLMs for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Benchmarking Self-Supervised and Generative Approaches: The central comparison is how acoustic encoders and language-aware decoders map dysarthric speech to words; the clinical population is an important boundary, not the main mechanism.; HuBERT-VIC: Improving Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition of Speech Foundation Model via Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization: VICReg constraints make noisy speech representations retain useful acoustic units before recognition.; Analysis of Semantic and Acoustic Token Variability Across Speech, Music, and Audio Domains: The paper studies what discrete audio tokens preserve and how token predictability changes across domains; it is a representation question, not a claim of universal semantic units.; From Weak Labels to Strong Results: Utilizing 5,000 Hours of Noisy Classroom Transcripts with Minimal Accurate Data: Noisy classroom transcripts provide weak supervision; the central move is learning word mappings while separating unreliable labels from a small accurate set.
