d3_comparison_matrix.title: Bridging ASR and LLMs for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Benchmarking Self-Supervised and Generative Approaches
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Benchmark CTC, Whisper, and LLM-enhanced decoders, including bridge networks and a Q-Former that connects Whisper acoustic features to Vicuna for context-aware decoding.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The comparison keeps TORGO and UASpeech speaker-independent splits and evaluates WER by dysarthria severity. The decoder choice changes how much linguistic context can repair uncertain acoustic evidence.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study systematically benchmarks these models with different decoding strategies, including CTC, seq2seq, and LLM-enhanced decoding (BART, GPT-2, Vicuna).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Whisper improves over CTC baselines, and Whisper-Vicuna reports the lowest WER in the tested TORGO and UASpeech comparisons; all results remain author-reported.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Whisper improves over CTC baselines, and Whisper-Vicuna reports the lowest WER in the tested TORGO and UASpeech comparisons; all results remain author-reported.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset splits, severity labels, model scale, decoding prompts, and WER limit the claim; lower WER does not prove faithful preservation of disfluencies or speaker intent.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: HuBERT-VIC: Improving Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition of Speech Foundation Model via Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add variance, invariance, and covariance constraints during HuBERT pretraining.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: HuBERT-VIC applies VICReg terms to noisy representations and compares masked prediction with regularizer ablations on MUSAN-noised LibriSpeech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Noise robustness in speech foundation models (SFMs) has been a critical challenge, as most models are primarily trained on clean data and experience performance degradation when the models are exposed to noisy speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: All three regularizers give the best reported WER and show complementary ablation effects.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: All three regularizers give the best reported WER and show complementary ablation effects.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: MUSAN, SNR choices, HuBERT, and LibriSpeech bound the result; real conversational noise is not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Analysis of Semantic and Acoustic Token Variability Across Speech, Music, and Audio Domains
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare acoustic codec tokens and semantic speech tokens across domains using rank-frequency distributions, perplexity, and token usage patterns.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study measures statistical structure and predictability of token sequences, then compares domain-specific codeword usage.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Using up to 1,000 held-out samples per speech, music, and sound domain, the study compares semantic and acoustic token distributions from HuBERT, EnCodec, and DAC. It evaluates rank-frequency/power-law behavior, N-gram language-model perplexity, normalized cross-entropy predictability, and TF-IDF/token-usage distributions; the domain and model are the comparison denominators.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports similar statistical/predictable sequence patterns across domains but domain-dependent token usage.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports similar statistical/predictable sequence patterns across domains but domain-dependent token usage.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The analysis supports representation observations, not a universal optimal token design or downstream task improvement.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: From Weak Labels to Strong Results: Utilizing 5,000 Hours of Noisy Classroom Transcripts with Minimal Accurate Data
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Pretrain on weak transcripts, then fine-tune on accurate data so broad coverage supplies structure and gold data corrects its errors.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Weakly Supervised Pretraining uses 5,000 hours of noisy classroom transcripts followed by fine-tuning on a small accurate set; synthetic and real weak transcripts are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Synthetic corruption experiments fine-tune Robust-wav2vec2 with deletion, misspelling, sound-alike, repetition, and timestamp corruption at 25/50/75/100% mixed with clean transcripts, then fine-tune with 10 minutes of precise data. A real-world NCTE classroom case uses 5,235 hours, 17 gold classes/13 hours, and Wav2vec2 ASR; the paper compares recognition error across corruption and data configurations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that WSP outperforms alternative strategies in synthetic and real weak-label settings for classroom ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that WSP outperforms alternative strategies in synthetic and real weak-label settings for classroom ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Classroom domain, weak-label generation, gold-data size, transcript quality, and WER protocol bound the result; weak supervision can still reproduce systematic omissions or speaker bias.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Mixture of LoRA Experts for Low-Resourced Multi-Accent Automatic Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Keep several small accent-specific adapters and let the system combine them, with or without knowing the accent.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MAS-LoRA attaches low-rank adapters specialized to accents to Whisper and evaluates known- and unknown-accent routing on L2-ARCTIC.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our experiments, conducted using Whisper on the L2-ARCTIC corpus, demonstrate significant improvements in Word Error Rate compared to regular LoRA and full fine-tuning when the accent is unknown.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports lower WER than those baselines, stronger gains when the accent is known, and less catastrophic forgetting.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports lower WER than those baselines, stronger gains when the accent is known, and less catastrophic forgetting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is tied to L2-ARCTIC, its accent set, Whisper, and routing assumptions; spontaneous speech and accents outside the corpus remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: CHSER: A Dataset and Case Study on Generative Speech Error Correction for Child ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Create a large hypothesis-to-reference dataset for children and learn a generative correction model whose errors can be inspected by type.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: CHSER contains 200K pairs across ages and speaking styles; fine-tuned generative correction is tested in zero-shot and ASR-fine-tuned settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems struggle with child speech due to its distinct acoustic and linguistic variability and limited availability of child speech datasets, leading to high transcription error rates.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports up to 28.5% relative WER reduction zero-shot and 13.3% after ASR fine-tuning, but insertions and child disfluencies remain difficult.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports up to 28.5% relative WER reduction zero-shot and 13.3% after ASR fine-tuning, but insertions and child disfluencies remain difficult.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpus, languages, ASR hypotheses, and correction model bound the result; preserving clinically meaningful disfluencies outside these settings remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Word stress in self-supervised speech models: A cross-linguistic comparison
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use simple diagnostic classifiers across languages and stress systems, then compare whether the encoded distinction changes with the language's stress structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Wav2vec 2.0 embeddings are probed for stressed versus unstressed syllables in Dutch, English, German, Hungarian, and Polish.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We train diagnostic stress classifiers on S3M embeddings and show that they can distinguish between stressed and unstressed syllables in read-aloud short sentences with high accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Stress is decoded with high accuracy, and the representations show language-specific differences, with a larger contrast between variable-stress and fixed-stress languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Stress is decoded with high accuracy, and the representations show language-specific differences, with a larger contrast between variable-stress and fixed-stress languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Read-aloud sentences, languages, layer choices, probe capacity, and diagnostic accuracy bound the inference; recoverable information is not proof that the model uses stress causally.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SardinianVoxes: A Speech Recognition Dataset for the Sardinian Languages
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a reproducible audio-text corpus with explicit variety annotation and evaluate both pretrained and fine-tuned recognizers across varieties.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SardinianVoxes contains about 170 hours of transcribed speech, and the paper defines a benchmark for state-of-the-art and fine-tuned speech-to-text models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: First, we present the design and implementation of a reproducible pipeline that led to the preparation of SardinianVoxes, an audio-text dataset comprising approximately 170 hours of transcribed speech, carefully annotated to reflect the internal linguistic diversity of Sardinian.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper contributes a public resource and evaluation protocol intended to make Sardinian speech technology measurable.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper contributes a public resource and evaluation protocol intended to make Sardinian speech technology measurable.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The reported resource, varieties, transcription quality, and benchmark models bound the claim; future collection and independent use are still needed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: DC-Spin: A Speaker-invariant Speech Tokenizer for Spoken Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use double-codebook speaker-invariant clustering to retain phonetic structure while suppressing speaker variation, then test whether the resulting tokens are easy to model and resynthesize.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SpinHuBERT supplies the speech representation and DC-Spin separates speaker-invariant and phonetic information into codebooks; the tokens are tested in zero-shot spoken-language tasks and resynthesis.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: DC-Spin is evaluated through zero-shot spoken-language-model tasks TSC, sWUGGY, and sBLIMP, plus speech resynthesis on Expresso dev/test utterances using original speaker/style IDs. It reports accuracy for the language tasks and ASR-WER, speaker similarity, and UTMOS for resynthesized speech, comparing against neural codec/tokenizer baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that tokens with phoneme alignment or simple language-model structure are useful downstream and improve the tested zero-shot and resynthesis proxies.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that tokens with phoneme alignment or simple language-model structure are useful downstream and improve the tested zero-shot and resynthesis proxies.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The tokenizers, languages, proxy tasks, and resynthesis setup bound the result; token usefulness is not the same as complete spoken meaning.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Using Neurogram Similarity Index Measure (NSIM) to Model Hearing Loss and Cochlear Neural Degeneration
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare modeled auditory-nerve neurograms with a Neurogram Similarity Index and relate the measure to phoneme recognition and simulated cochlear neural degeneration.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper evaluates NSIM as an objective measure of hearing loss and cochlear neural degeneration.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Specifically study 1, shows that NSIM can be used to map performance of individuals with hearing loss on phoneme recognition task with reasonable accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that NSIM maps phoneme-recognition performance and is sensitive to simulated degeneration, suggesting a candidate noninvasive biomarker.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that NSIM maps phoneme-recognition performance and is sensitive to simulated degeneration, suggesting a candidate noninvasive biomarker.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Auditory-periphery model, task, simulations, participant data, and mapping assumptions bound clinical interpretation; a candidate biomarker is not a validated diagnosis.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Decoding Speaker-Normalized Pitch from EEG for Mandarin Perception
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Record EEG during Mandarin speech perception and compare decoding of raw versus speaker-normalized pitch contours with a model that captures temporal context.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper decodes speaker-normalized pitch from EEG during Mandarin perception.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model can decode pitch contours with modest errors, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art EEG regression methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposed CE-ViViT approach achieved modest-error decoding, with speaker-normalized contours decoded more accurately than raw contours in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposed CE-ViViT approach achieved modest-error decoding, with speaker-normalized contours decoded more accurately than raw contours in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Participants, Mandarin tones, EEG sessions, normalization rule, model, and modest-error metric bound the neural claim; better decoding does not by itself reveal the full perceptual code.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: DiceHuBERT: Distilling HuBERT with a Self-Supervised Learning Objective
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Replace the HuBERT teacher with a smaller student trained directly under HuBERT's iterative self-supervised objective.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: DiceHuBERT distills HuBERT using the same self-supervised objective and evaluates the compact model on phoneme recognition, ASR, and SUPERB tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: DiceHuBERT compares HuBERT distillation methods on phoneme error rate, word error rate, unsupervised error rate, equal-error rate, and classification accuracy, with explicit upper and lower bounds. The paper notes that model/data choices and the 60k-hour pretraining scale limit direct comparison across the reported speech tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports over 21% improvement in phoneme recognition and over 14% in ASR relative to existing distillation methods, with competitive multi-task results.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports over 21% improvement in phoneme recognition and over 14% in ASR relative to existing distillation methods, with competitive multi-task results.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Teacher/student sizes, SUPERB tasks, training data, and comparison baselines bound the result; benchmark transfer does not establish equal behavior under every deployment constraint.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: On-device Streaming Discrete Speech Units
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Shrink the attention window and model size for streaming discrete speech units, measuring the compute reduction against recognition error.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper develops on-device streaming discrete speech units.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our results demonstrate that we can reduce floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 50% with only a relative increase of 6.5% in character error rate (CER) on the ML-SUPERB 1h dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On ML-SUPERB 1h, the paper reports a 50% FLOP reduction for a 6.5% relative CER increase.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On ML-SUPERB 1h, the paper reports a 50% FLOP reduction for a 6.5% relative CER increase.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset size, causal window, unit clustering, hardware, FLOPs accounting, and CER bound practical generalization; the trade-off may change for other languages or latency targets.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Exploring auditory feedback mechanisms in speech recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add Hopf-oscillator compression and olivocochlear feedback mechanisms to an ASR front end, then compare recognition behavior and biological plausibility.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper explores auditory feedback mechanisms in speech recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In the present study, to the extent to which current compute power allows, we investigate how to incorporate the Hopf mechanism and the olivocochlear feedback mechanisms into ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that adding the larger feedback loop appears beneficial for ASR, while describing the current implications as modest.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that adding the larger feedback loop appears beneficial for ASR, while describing the current implications as modest.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Approximate oscillator model, compute limits, ASR task, feedback implementation, and modest gains bound interpretation; improved recognition does not validate the whole biological mechanism.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: What do self-supervised speech models know about Dutch?  Analyzing advantages of language-specific pre-training
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare English, multilingual, and Dutch self-supervised models with linguistic probes and downstream Dutch ASR across read and conversational speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Hidden layers are probed for phonetic and lexical structure, then models are fine-tuned and evaluated on five Dutch test sets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Here we test the encoding of Dutch phonetic and lexical information in internal representations of self-supervised Wav2Vec2 models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Language-specific pretraining yields lower WER, while probe and fine-tuning rankings need not coincide.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Language-specific pretraining yields lower WER, while probe and fine-tuning rankings need not coincide.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Models, Dutch corpora, probes, and fine-tuning limit generalization; decodability is not causal proof of ASR behavior.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards a Unified Benchmark for Arabic Pronunciation Assessment: Qur’anic Recitation as Case Study
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Construct a unified Arabic pronunciation-assessment benchmark around Qur'anic recitation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Audio, pronunciation targets, and assessment labels are aligned for model comparison.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present a unified benchmark for mispronunciation detection in Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) using Qur'anic recitation as a case study.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper presents a benchmark and case study for Arabic pronunciation assessment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper presents a benchmark and case study for Arabic pronunciation assessment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Recitation tradition, annotation, coverage, and metrics bound transfer; automatic scores are not teacher judgment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Child Speech Recognition and Reading Mistake Detection by Using Prompts
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use prompts to condition recognition and mistake detection on the child's intended reading task.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Prompt information narrows the hypothesis space: acoustic evidence is interpreted with task and expected linguistic content.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Automatic reading aloud evaluation can provide valuable support to teachers by enabling more efficient scoring of reading exercises.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improving child speech recognition and reading-mistake detection using prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improving child speech recognition and reading-mistake detection using prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Child age, language, prompt design, annotation policy, and error definitions bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving End-to-end Mixed-case ASR with Knowledge Distillation and Integration of Voice Activity Cues
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Distill word-recognition knowledge from an unformatted teacher into a formatted student and add voice-activity cues to support boundary and formatting decisions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A mixed-case end-to-end ASR student receives knowledge from a unicase teacher and voice-activity information; case-sensitive and insensitive outputs are measured.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our approach incorporates knowledge distillation from UC teacher to MC student models not only to improve capitalization and punctuation accuracy but also to maximize phone classification capability in MC ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The method reports up to a 9.2% relative error reduction at comparable decoding cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The method reports up to a 9.2% relative error reduction at comparable decoding cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Training data, formatting conventions, teacher quality, decoding budget, and reported error definitions bound the result; punctuation accuracy is not the same as transcript understanding.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: EnCodecMAE: leveraging neural codecs for universal audio representation learning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use discrete targets from a neural codec in a masked autoencoder and test the representation across tasks, model sizes, input forms, self-training, and data mixtures.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: EnCodecMAE is pretrained on diverse audio and evaluated on pitch, genre, speech commands, emotion, sound events, and environmental sound tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate our approach, EnCodecMAE, across various tasks and find that, on average, it outperforms state-of-the-art audio representation models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports average gains over prior audio representations and finds that larger models, task-dependent inputs, self-training, and diverse data each matter.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports average gains over prior audio representations and finds that larger models, task-dependent inputs, self-training, and diverse data each matter.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The task suite, pretraining mixture, labels, model comparisons, and aggregate averages bound the claim; average transfer does not prove universal suitability for speech.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.

records.subtheme_name: Boundaries, timing, and sequence constraints
records.question: How does the system decide where units begin, end, and depend on one another?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech has no visible spaces between words, and pronunciation, speed, accent, noise, and hesitation vary even when the intended sentence is the same. The subtheme asks: How does the system decide where units begin, end, and depend on one another?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with temporal alignment, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Forced alignment assumes the transcript is correct and can conceal recognition errors.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make temporal alignment, long-context decoding, disfluency and event preservation explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Fine-tune Whisper on DementiaBank and an in-house dataset, explicitly evaluating filler inclusion and F1 as well as WER.
subtheme_boundary: Forced alignment assumes the transcript is correct and can conceal recognition errors.
Context can override a rare but correct word, especially when the language model has a strong prior.
Removing them may improve readability while destroying evidence needed for conversation analysis or diagnosis.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: WhisperD: Dementia Speech Recognition and Filler Word Detection with Whisper: The explicit filler-inclusion analysis makes preservation of disfluencies part of the target rather than treating them as transcription noise; the dementia population is the evaluation boundary.; ASR-based segmentation for the analysis of larger child-speech datasets: Performance evaluation on vowels from Australian-English speaking children aged 4 to 11 years: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate alignment within boundaries-and-sequence-structure.; Song Form-aware Full-Song Text-to-Lyrics Generation with Multi-Level Granularity Syllable Count Control: Song-form-aware lyrics generation must align syllable count and linguistic content with musical timing across a full song.; Bidirectional Spoken-Written Text Conversion with Large Language Models: Spoken and written forms require a controlled conversion boundary after recognition; the paper addresses that normalization step.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: WhisperD: Dementia Speech Recognition and Filler Word Detection with Whisper
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Fine-tune Whisper on DementiaBank and an in-house dataset, explicitly evaluating filler inclusion and F1 as well as WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Shorter training clips adapt the model to fragmented speech; transcripts are scored for word errors and filler detection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this work, we fine-tune Whisper with the open-source dementia speech dataset (DementiaBank) and our in-house dataset to improve its word error rate (WER).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a medium model WER of 0.24 and stronger results than off-the-shelf models in its evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a medium model WER of 0.24 and stronger results than off-the-shelf models in its evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The dataset is 11.39 hours, some audio is mumbled or unintelligible, and diagnostic or clinical benefit is not established by ASR scores alone.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: ASR-based segmentation for the analysis of larger child-speech datasets: Performance evaluation on vowels from Australian-English speaking children aged 4 to 11 years
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare human-human reliability with manual-versus-Montreal-Forced-Aligner boundaries across child ages and inspect systematic discrepancies.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates vowel boundaries in Australian-English child speech and asks how alignment error changes from ages four to eleven.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Annotation of segment boundaries in child speech presents a persistent challenge, particularly with large-scale datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that MFA falls short of human annotation, with smaller discrepancies for older children.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that MFA falls short of human annotation, with smaller discrepancies for older children.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is tied to the tested vowels, ages, language variety, and annotators; it supports semi-automatic caution rather than universal aligner failure.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Song Form-aware Full-Song Text-to-Lyrics Generation with Multi-Level Granularity Syllable Count Control
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate complete lyrics conditioned on text and song form while controlling syllable counts at word, phrase, line, and paragraph levels.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes song-form-aware full-song lyrics generation with multi-level syllable control.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Song-form-aware lyric generation is evaluated on approximately 340K training, 18K validation, and 10K evaluation samples from Genius Song Lyrics after toxicity filtering. Perplexity, syllable-count deviation, syllable-count error rate, and BERT-S similarity are compared across full, paragraph, line, phrase, and word generation levels against Front-P and related baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports controlled lyrics-generation experiments and makes generated samples available for inspection.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports controlled lyrics-generation experiments and makes generated samples available for inspection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Text prompts, song forms, syllable-count rules, dataset construction, and evaluation criteria bound the claim; syllable fit is not the same as singability, musicality, or authorship.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Bidirectional Spoken-Written Text Conversion with Large Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use LLM-generated dual transcriptions, iterative supervised/semi-supervised expansion, and a bidirectional text-conversion model supporting both ITN and TN.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model learns mappings in both directions; generated paired text supplies supervision while iterative learning enlarges the conversion data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: However, constructing such datasets is costly and time-consuming.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 13.4% ERR improvement in the evaluated conversion setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 13.4% ERR improvement in the evaluated conversion setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: LLM generation quality, language conventions, error metric, transcript domain, and iterative-label bias bound transfer; normalization success is not ASR acoustic accuracy.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A semi-automatic pipeline for transcribing and segmenting child speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Correct the transcript before forced alignment and adapt the acoustic model toward child speech, then compare automatic measurements with manual annotations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: WhisperX supplies a transcription, manual correction changes the lexical scaffold, and MFA places segment boundaries; adaptation changes the acoustic model used for alignment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study evaluates both automated transcription (WhisperX) and forced alignment (MFA) in developing a semi-automated pipeline for obtaining acoustic vowel measures from field recordings from 275 children speaking a non-standard, English dialect, Scottish English.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Manual transcript correction improves acoustic vowel measures, and adaptation of the pretrained MFA model helps, while merely increasing the adaptation sample does not add the same improvement.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Manual transcript correction improves acoustic vowel measures, and adaptation of the pretrained MFA model helps, while merely increasing the adaptation sample does not add the same improvement.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The 275-child Scottish-English field corpus, manual reference quality, recording conditions, and selected vowel measures bound transfer; alignment quality is not a complete child-speech recognizer evaluation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Exploring SSL Discrete Speech Features for Zipformer-based Contextual ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare discrete speech tokens and continuous features for pooled or concatenated context in a Zipformer-Transducer, measuring both recognition gains and efficiency.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates contextual Z-T systems on 1,000-hour GigaSpeech-M and DementiaBank Pitt elderly speech, using SSL discrete tokens, WavLM features, and preceding/current/future context variants.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Their efficacy and efficiency in modelling preceding, current and future speech utterance contexts using concatenation or pooling projection of Z-T encoder embeddings are extensively shown on the 1000-hr GigaSpeech-M and DementiaBank Pitt elderly speech datasets over comparable contextual Z-T baselines using filterbank or continuous WavLM features}.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Discrete-token contextual systems reduce WER by 0.39 and 1.41 absolute points on the two tasks and achieve up to 4.36x training speedup over continuous WavLM context systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Discrete-token contextual systems reduce WER by 0.39 and 1.41 absolute points on the two tasks and achieve up to 4.36x training speedup over continuous WavLM context systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Corpora, context windows, tokenization, speed hardware, and statistical test bound the result; better contextual WER does not prove robust dialogue understanding or causal use of future context in deployment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SiamCTC:  Learning Speech Representations through Monotonic Temporal Alignment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use CTC to learn a flexible monotonic alignment between views inside a Siamese learner.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Two encoders produce sequences and CTC sums over valid monotonic paths while training the representations to agree at content level.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: SiamCTC is evaluated on LibriSpeech train-clean-100 with HuBERT and WavLM encoders and compared with Spin and LASER variants under SUPERB conditions. Phoneme Error Rate and Word Error Rate are reported on LibriSpeech test-clean, with additional speed-perturbed evaluation and ablations of the monotonic-alignment loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: SiamCTC improves representation robustness at diverse speaking rates in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: SiamCTC improves representation robustness at diverse speaking rates in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Augmentation, language, CTC targets, downstream tasks, and rate range bound transfer; robustness is not universal recognition accuracy.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards Multi-Level Transcript Segmentation: LoRA Fine-Tuning for Table-of-Contents Generation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate a hierarchical table of contents and use a metric that respects its levels; add pause duration only when training can use it.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: TOC-NEMO uses LoRA fine-tuning and optional pause cues on AMI, VideoAula, and LectureDE; zero-shot prompting and supervised baselines provide comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations on English meeting recordings and multilingual lecture transcripts (Portuguese, German) show significant improvements over established topic segmentation baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Fine-tuned TOC-NEMO plus pause cues reports the strongest linear scores, including AMI F1 30.34/B 24.81 and VideoAula F1 67.34/B 55.18.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Fine-tuned TOC-NEMO plus pause cues reports the strongest linear scores, including AMI F1 30.34/B 24.81 and VideoAula F1 67.34/B 55.18.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, prompts, annotations, and metric behavior constrain the result; transcript segmentation is not proof of human topic understanding.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: The Multimodal Information Based Speech Processing (MISP) 2025 Challenge: Audio-Visual Diarization and Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Fuse audio and video across diarization, recognition, and joint diarization-recognition tasks, then compare systems under a shared challenge protocol.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MISP 2025 defines AVSD, AVSR, and AVDR tasks with multi-device meeting data; systems combine acoustic and visual streams and are scored on speaker attribution and transcription.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present the challenge’s objectives, tasks, dataset, baseline systems, and solutions proposed by participants.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The challenge reports DER 8.09%, CER 9.48%, and cpCER 11.56% for its top systems, with the largest gain in the joint task.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The challenge reports DER 8.09%, CER 9.48%, and cpCER 11.56% for its top systems, with the largest gain in the joint task.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge data, camera placement, meeting types, language, and leaderboard protocols define the claim; deployment in unseen rooms or privacy-constrained camera settings remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: StutterCut: Uncertainty-Guided Normalised Cut for Dysfluency Segmentation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent overlapping windows as a graph, refine edge weights with a weakly supervised pseudo-oracle, and use uncertainty-aware normalized cuts to segment events; add real frame-level annotations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Speech embeddings form graph nodes, similarity edges are adjusted by a classifier, and Monte Carlo dropout controls how strongly uncertain predictions affect the partition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: However, most methods only classify dysfluencies at the utterance level.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: StutterCut reports better F1 and more precise stuttering-onset detection on real and synthetic data, and the extended FluencyBank boundaries make the evaluation less dependent on synthetic events.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: StutterCut reports better F1 and more precise stuttering-onset detection on real and synthetic data, and the extended FluencyBank boundaries make the evaluation less dependent on synthetic events.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dysfluency types, annotation quality, speaker population, synthetic-real mismatch, and feedback protocol constrain the claim; segmentation accuracy is not demonstrated therapy benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Dynamic Context-Aware Streaming Pretrained Language Model For Inverse Text Normalization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a pretrained language model with dynamic chunk sizes and controlled right-context during training and inference.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model changes its available context as speech arrives, using right-context information without abandoning the streaming budget.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Despite its importance, the integration of streaming ITN within streaming ASR remains largely unexplored due to challenges in accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability, particularly in low-resource and limited-context scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports accuracy comparable to non-streaming ITN and better than prior streaming models on Vietnamese data while maintaining low latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports accuracy comparable to non-streaming ITN and better than prior streaming models on Vietnamese data while maintaining low latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Vietnamese data, benchmark, and author-reported latency/results limit cross-language and independent deployment claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Transcript-Prompted Whisper with Dictionary-Enhanced Decoding for Japanese Speech Annotation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Condition a pretrained ASR model on the ground-truth transcript so it emits phrase-level graphemes and labels together, then use dictionary-enhanced decoding to correct phonemic labels.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Transcript-Prompted Whisper fine-tunes a large ASR model for simultaneous phrase and annotation output and applies a dictionary-based correction stage for Japanese speech-data construction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we propose a method for annotating phonemic and prosodic labels on a given audio-transcript pair, aimed at constructing Japanese text-to-speech (TTS) datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved phonemic/prosodic annotation behavior and a practical pipeline for constructing Japanese TTS data from audio-transcript pairs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved phonemic/prosodic annotation behavior and a practical pipeline for constructing Japanese TTS data from audio-transcript pairs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Ground-truth transcript quality, dictionary coverage, Japanese phonology, label definitions, and annotation evaluation bound the result; automatic labels still require quality control before becoming training truth.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Word Level Timestamp Generation for Automatic Speech Recognition and Translation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a forced aligner as a teacher to create timestamp supervision, add a timestamp token, and train the end-to-end Canary model to emit start and end times with words.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Teacher-generated word intervals become sequence targets; the model's timestamp tokens interleave with recognized or translated content, allowing boundary prediction inside the decoder.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our method demonstrates precision and recall rates between 80% and 90%, with timestamp prediction errors ranging from 20 to 120 ms across four languages, with minimal WER degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports word-level timestamp generation for Canary with the proposed token and teacher-supervised training in the evaluated ASR/translation settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports word-level timestamp generation for Canary with the proposed token and teacher-supervised training in the evaluated ASR/translation settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Teacher timing quality, tokenization, language, speaking rate, and evaluation alignment constrain transfer; timestamp agreement does not by itself prove subtitle readability or translation quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: VoiceNet: Multilingual On-Device Phoneme-To-Audio Alignment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train an end-to-end model for phoneme recognition and text-independent forced alignment, with optional text conditioning.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: VoiceNet predicts phoneme evidence and timing on-device; text adds a constraint when available, and device tests expose latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our experiments demonstrate competitive performance of VoiceNet compared with state-of-the-art Phoneme Recognition and Forced Alignment results on LibriSpeech and multilingual dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports competitive multilingual alignment and 6 ms average CPU phoneme inference on Galaxy devices.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports competitive multilingual alignment and 6 ms average CPU phoneme inference on Galaxy devices.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Device, language, phoneme inventory, transcript availability, and splits bound transfer; latency is not alignment quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: MOVER: Combining Multiple Meeting Recognition Systems
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use MOVER’s staged alignment, segment grouping, word/timing combination, and speaker reconciliation across complete meeting hypotheses.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The method constructs correspondences between speaker-labeled time intervals before combining words and timings, preserving the meeting structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we propose Meeting recognizer Output Voting Error Reduction (MOVER), a novel system combination method for meeting recognition tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: MOVER reports successful combination on CHiME-8 DASR and NOTSOFAR-1 multi-channel tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: MOVER reports successful combination on CHiME-8 DASR and NOTSOFAR-1 multi-channel tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Task formats, diarization errors, interval alignment, system diversity, and scoring rules bound transfer; fusion gains do not prove every component is complementary.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Who knows best? Effects of speech disfluencies on incentivized decision-making
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use an incentivized web decision task with conflicting information and compare choices as a function of speech fluency.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The experiment treats disfluency as part of the observed communication signal and measures choice behavior rather than only an attitude rating.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We sought to address this question with a web-based decision task in which participants were asked to choose between two conflicting sources of information.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The study reports that listeners take speech fluency into account when deciding whom or what to believe.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The study reports that listeners take speech fluency into account when deciding whom or what to believe.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Task stakes, speakers, disfluency types, online sample, and source-conflict design bound transfer; choice bias is not proof that disfluencies carry truthful information.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Cross-Attention based on Positional Alignment during Inference for Robust Long-form Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add positional alignment to cross-attention at inference so attention scores favor acoustically corresponding positions during long-form decoding.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Position-aware attention reshapes the correspondence between decoder states and encoder frames without changing the recognized content target.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The proposed method achieves an error reduction rate (ERR) of 88.41% (from 26.41% to 3.06%) for audio longer than 20 seconds on a LibriSpeech evaluation set constructed by concatenating three utterances.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved robust long-form recognition from inference-time positional alignment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved robust long-form recognition from inference-time positional alignment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Model, long-form segmentation, positional formulation, decoding settings, and evaluation corpora bound transfer; reported robustness is not universal streaming reliability.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: What the Filler? Both ASR Systems and Humans Struggle More With Other Kinds of Disfluencies Than With Filler Particles
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Present the same disfluent utterances to human listeners and multiple ASR systems, and compare error patterns across structure and acoustic factors.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The matched transcription experiment uses participant recall and ASR WER to compare shared difficulty patterns.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Since disfluencies are frequent in conversational speech, they have received notable attention: from speech technologists to make automatic speech recognition (ASR) more robust and from speech scientists to learn more about human speech processing.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports similar difficulty characteristics for humans and ASR and no WER effect from filler presence alone.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports similar difficulty characteristics for humans and ASR and no WER effect from filler presence alone.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: 54 listeners, nine systems, utterance design, languages, and WER/recall definitions bound transfer; matched error patterns do not establish cognitive equivalence.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Effects of speech disfluencies on incentivized decision-making: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate disfluency-preservation under boundaries-and-sequence-structure; this resolves taxonomy membership only. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: Removing them may improve readability while destroying evidence needed for conversation analysis or diagnosis.
concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 4 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

records.subtheme_name: Recognizing new speakers, domains, and words
records.question: How can recognition remain useful when the test speech differs from training speech?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech has no visible spaces between words, and pronunciation, speed, accent, noise, and hesitation vary even when the intended sentence is the same. The subtheme asks: How can recognition remain useful when the test speech differs from training speech?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with speaker adaptation, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Adaptation can overfit a short sample and degrade when the talker changes state or the enrollment is wrong.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make speaker adaptation, domain and context biasing, open-vocabulary recognition explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Adapt the audio side using representative target-domain sound examples and test transfer across environments.
subtheme_boundary: Adaptation can overfit a short sample and degrade when the talker changes state or the enrollment is wrong.
A biased vocabulary can turn uncertainty into confident but context-shaped substitutions.
Open vocabulary expands recall but makes spelling, segmentation, and evaluation less settled.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Domain Adaptation Method and Modality Gap Impact in Audio-Text Models for Prototypical Sound Classification: Audio-side adaptation tests whether an audio-text representation preserves open-vocabulary labels across acoustic domains.; Spot and Merge: A Hybrid Context Biasing Approach for Rare Word and Out of Vocabulary Recognition: The method finds bias phrases in cross-attention and merges them with ASR output, using task context to resolve otherwise difficult terms.; Continuous Learning for Children's ASR: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting with Elastic Weight Consolidation and Synaptic Intelligence: Importance-weighted continual learning protects earlier child-speech mappings while adapting to sequential speakers.; NGPU-LM: GPU-Accelerated N-Gram Language Model for Context-Biasing in Greedy ASR Decoding: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate domain-and-context-biasing within adaptation-and-open-vocabulary.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Adapt the audio side using representative target-domain sound examples and test transfer across environments.
Use LoRA adaptation and a spot-and-merge method that detects bias phrases in cross-attention and merges them with ASR output.
Protect parameters important for earlier batches with EWC or SI, and compare online checkpoint-selection policies.
Represent n-gram transitions for parallel GPU lookup and inject their scores into greedy decoding for CTC, transducer, and attention models.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Domain Adaptation Method and Modality Gap Impact in Audio-Text Models for Prototypical Sound Classification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt the audio side using representative target-domain sound examples and test transfer across environments.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The method aligns audio representations to the target domain and compares audio-based with text-based adaptation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our domain adaptation technique enhances accuracy across various backgrounds and SNR conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Audio-based adaptation gives the largest reported gains across tested conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Audio-based adaptation gives the largest reported gains across tested conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Sound set, target examples, class construction, and reported accuracy limit open-world claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Spot and Merge: A Hybrid Context Biasing Approach for Rare Word and Out of Vocabulary Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use LoRA adaptation and a spot-and-merge method that detects bias phrases in cross-attention and merges them with ASR output.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Attention weights identify likely bias phrases; the method combines those candidates with the base transcription and uses an auxiliary attention loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Unlike existing methods, our approach maintains strong performance even with larger biasing lists, achieving a 1.0% absolute word error rate (WER) reduction on LibriSpeech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 1.0% absolute WER reduction on LibriSpeech and improved OOV recognition on in-house contact-center data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 1.0% absolute WER reduction on LibriSpeech and improved OOV recognition on in-house contact-center data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The in-house data are not independently available in this atlas, and future multilingual/low-resource extension remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Continuous Learning for Children's ASR: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting with Elastic Weight Consolidation and Synaptic Intelligence
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Protect parameters important for earlier batches with EWC or SI, and compare online checkpoint-selection policies.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Whisper-small trains on ten sequential MyST batches. EWC adds an importance-weighted quadratic penalty; SI accumulates importance from parameter movement and loss reduction; models use no selection, rolling-window, or best-so-far selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Using a custom protocol on the MyST corpus, tailored to the online learning setting, we achieve relative word error rate (WER) reductions of 5.21 % with EWC and 4.36 % with SI, compared to the fine-tuning baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: EWC and SI keep WER more stable across ten batches and improve over ordinary sequential fine-tuning under the protocol.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: EWC and SI keep WER more stable across ten batches and improve over ordinary sequential fine-tuning under the protocol.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The protocol is simulated from MyST, uses English child speech and Whisper-small, and treats parameter importance as a proxy rather than a privacy guarantee.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: NGPU-LM: GPU-Accelerated N-Gram Language Model for Context-Biasing in Greedy ASR Decoding
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent n-gram transitions for parallel GPU lookup and inject their scores into greedy decoding for CTC, transducer, and attention models.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: NGPU-LM uses hash-based transition lookup and customizable greedy decoding so context biasing can recover domain words with less than 7% reported overhead.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The proposed approach can eliminate more than 50% of the accuracy gap between greedy and beam search for out-of-domain scenarios while avoiding significant slowdown caused by beam search.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports recovery of more than half the greedy/beam accuracy gap in out-of-domain tests and up to 10.6% relative WER improvement in its experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports recovery of more than half the greedy/beam accuracy gap in out-of-domain tests and up to 10.6% relative WER improvement in its experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The results depend on tested ASR architectures, domains, GPU implementation, and author-reported measurements; deployment energy and other hardware remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Effect of Loudspeaker Emitted Speech on ASR performance
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure the distribution shift caused by loudspeaker emission and evaluate recognition under that realistic channel.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies ASR performance for loudspeaker-emitted speech and compares recognition across the tested playback conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Most of the automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems are trained on the natural speech signals, recorded directly from the human speakers and gives higher word error rate (WER) for the loudspeaker speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a measurable ASR impact from loudspeaker emission under its experimental conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a measurable ASR impact from loudspeaker emission under its experimental conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is bounded to the loudspeaker, room, microphones, and ASR systems tested; other devices and adaptive compensation remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Robust fine-tuning of speech recognition models via model merging: application to disordered speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Average weights from multiple checkpoints or fine-tuning trajectories, and add a selective rule that keeps a candidate only when it reduces development-set WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study fine-tunes Whisper on the SAP dysarthric-speech data. MAST averages checkpoints along one trajectory, MAcT averages models from different hyperparameter trajectories, and SMAcT scans candidate models and retains those that improve the merged ensemble. The procedure is also tested with 1-hour, 10-hour, and full training subsets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our best multi-run merging approach achieved a 12% relative decrease of WER over classic fine-tuning, and a 16.2% relative decrease on long-form audios, a major loss contributor in dysarthric ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports gains for long utterances and low-data settings, including a 7.6% relative reduction from 18.5 to 17.1 WER with 10 hours of data; smaller Base and Turbo models improve too, but less consistently than Large.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports gains for long utterances and low-data settings, including a 7.6% relative reduction from 18.5 to 17.1 WER with 10 hours of data; smaller Base and Turbo models improve too, but less consistently than Large.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The SAP data, Whisper family, selected development subset, and merging order determine the result. The selective procedure uses WER on a development subset and may itself be selection-sensitive; no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: BR-ASR: Efficient and Scalable Bias Retrieval Framework for Contextual Biasing ASR in Speech LLM
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Retrieve a small relevant candidate set from speech and bias text, train against homophone confusion, and inject only the retrieved candidates without retraining the recognizer.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Speech-and-bias contrastive learning ranks relevant entries; a dynamic curriculum trains the system on increasingly difficult homophones; pruning then supplies a compact list to the ASR decoder.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on LibriSpeech test-clean/-other achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) biased word error rates (B-WER) of 2.8%/7.1% with 2000 bias words, delivering 45% relative improvement over prior methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 2.8%/7.1% biased WER with 2,000 words, only 0.3/2.9% absolute degradation at 200,000 entries, 99.99% pruning, and 20 ms query latency on the tested split.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 2.8%/7.1% biased WER with 2,000 words, only 0.3/2.9% absolute degradation at 200,000 entries, 99.99% pruning, and 20 ms query latency on the tested split.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The reported latency, languages, bias lists, and ASR systems define the boundary; rare names outside the retrieval distribution and interactive user correction remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Theoretical proposal for a unified Bayesian model of adaptation in non-interactive and interactive speech production
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Extend a unified Bayesian perception-production framework so adaptation is an inference problem over intended and heard speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: COSMO-style latent variables connect production and perception; Bayesian updating changes beliefs about the speech system under feedback or interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: However, existing computational models accounting for adaptation appear segregated: feedback effects during non-interactive, altered speech are mostly accounted for by speech production models, whereas accommodation effects during interactive speech are mostly accounted for by speech perception models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposal shows how both experimental paradigms can be described within one Bayesian framework.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposal shows how both experimental paradigms can be described within one Bayesian framework.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: This is a theoretical proposal, not an independent behavioral validation; parameterization, priors, and task fit remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: CMT-LLM: Contextual Multi-Talker ASR Utilizing Large Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Make multi-talker transcription and contextual biasing one sequence-generation task: represent speakers in first-in-first-out order and filter the biasing list before placing relevant rare words into the language model prompt.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A speech encoder produces frame representations, convolution downsamples them, a projector matches the LLM hidden size, and an LLM emits text separated by speaker-change tokens. A first decoding pass supplies evidence for a two-stage filter that selects rare words from a list of up to 1,000 before a second pass.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments show that our approach outperforms traditional contextual biasing methods, achieving a WER of 7.9% on LibriMix and 32.9% on AMI SDM when the biasing size is 1,000, demonstrating its effectiveness in complex speech scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports WER of 7.9% on LibriMix and 32.9% on AMI SDM at biasing size 1,000, outperforming compared contextual-biasing approaches in its reported settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports WER of 7.9% on LibriMix and 32.9% on AMI SDM at biasing size 1,000, outperforming compared contextual-biasing approaches in its reported settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: FIFO serialization imposes an ordering convention; the bias list and first-pass filter supply information that may not exist in every deployment. WER does not separately reveal speaker attribution, rare-word recall, or hallucination cost, and results were not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Ranking and Selection of Bias Words for Contextual Bias Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train a scorer that ranks and selects bias words from an NER-derived list before contextual Whisper decoding.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A bias-word ranking network selects candidates from the IS21 list and evaluates contextual Whisper on LibriSpeech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: First, to guide the model to focus on the most important words, we propose a novel network serving as a scorer for bias word ranking and selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports more than 40% relative reduction in biased WER from ranking and selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports more than 40% relative reduction in biased WER from ranking and selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: NER list, LibriSpeech, Whisper context mechanism, and bias-word definition bound the result; new domains and errors in entity extraction remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Adversarial Deep Metric Learning for Cross-Modal Audio-Text Alignment in Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adversarially train a modality classifier so audio and text encoders produce modality-invariant embeddings, then optimize deep metric alignment for open-vocabulary KWS.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The encoders map acoustic queries and text enrollments into a shared space; the adversarial classifier penalizes recoverable modality identity while the metric objective pulls matched keyword pairs together.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) and LibriPhrase datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Modality-invariant alignment improves the audio-text retrieval decision used for unseen-keyword spotting in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Modality-invariant alignment improves the audio-text retrieval decision used for unseen-keyword spotting in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Vocabulary, languages, negative sampling, enrollment text, threshold calibration, and speaker/channel variation bound the claim; open-vocabulary benchmark accuracy is not unrestricted lexical understanding.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Fully End-to-end Streaming Open-vocabulary Keyword Spotting with W-CTC Forced Alignment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Integrate W-CTC forced alignment into a fully end-to-end streaming system.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: CTC paths supply word-span alignment while the text encoder and verifier are trained in the same pipeline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In previous work, word-aligned datasets were created by forced alignment algorithms such as the Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA) to train text encoder and verifier models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports superior performance on the Libriphrase hard set.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports superior performance on the Libriphrase hard set.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Benchmark, language, and author-reported result limit generalization and independent reproducibility.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: GLCLAP: A Novel Contrastive Learning Pre-trained Model for Contextual Biasing in ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train a contrastive audio-text retriever at both global sentence and local word scales, then use the retrieved bias words during ASR decoding.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: GLCLAP learns global and local audio-text relations for contextual biasing, retrieving matched entities from a user-specified list before the ASR decoder uses them.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This multi-scale information has led to a remarkable improvement in bias word retrieval accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a marked improvement in bias-word retrieval accuracy and downstream contextual ASR performance over sentence-level contrastive approaches.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a marked improvement in bias-word retrieval accuracy and downstream contextual ASR performance over sentence-level contrastive approaches.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Entity list, prompt quality, language, negative sampling, retrieval threshold, and ASR decoder bound the result; a better retrieved list cannot correct an incorrect user prompt or guarantee unbiased ordinary decoding.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Synthetic Data Training for Contextual Biasing Models with a Keyword-Aware Cost Function
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a keyword-aware cost function when training synthetic contextual-biasing data so difficult and useful examples receive the right pressure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper improves synthetic-data training for contextual biasing with a keyword-aware cost function.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: By adapting Whisper to 10 hours of synthetic data, our method reduced the word error rate on the NSC Part 2 test set from 29.71% to 11.81%.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved contextual-biasing performance for the proposed synthetic-data objective.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved contextual-biasing performance for the proposed synthetic-data objective.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Keyword lists, synthetic-data quality, language, decoder, and evaluation distribution limit generalization; better keyword recall can still create false activations.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Efficient Trie-based Biasing using K-step Prediction for Rare Word Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train a K-step predictor to look ahead and estimate whether a rare word will complete, avoiding score revocation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The decoder predicts future steps from a prefix; synthetic data fine-tunes Whisper so contextual biasing becomes learned look-ahead.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: By fine-tuning Whisper with only 10 hours of synthetic data, our method reduces the word error rate on the NSC Part 2 test set from 30.86% to 12.19%.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On NSC Part 2, reported WER falls from 30.86% to 12.19% after 10 hours of synthetic-data fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On NSC Part 2, reported WER falls from 30.86% to 12.19% after 10 hours of synthetic-data fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Synthetic realism, rare-word list, decoder, beam settings, and WER denominator bound the claim.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: WCTC-Biasing: Retraining-free Contextual Biasing ASR with Wildcard CTC-based Keyword Spotting and Inter-layer Biasing
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use wildcard CTC keyword spotting and inter-layer biasing to add contextual evidence at inference time without retraining.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: CTC keyword scores detect flexible keyword evidence; inter-layer bias signals steer decoding while retaining the base acoustic model.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To address this issue, we propose a method to improve recognition accuracy of such rare words in CTC-based models without additional training or text-to-speech systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports retraining-free contextual recognition improvements using WCTC-Biasing.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports retraining-free contextual recognition improvements using WCTC-Biasing.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Keyword lists, wildcard design, domains, decoder thresholds, and test distributions bound transfer; contextual gains do not guarantee lower errors on arbitrary speech.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multilingual Query-by-Example KWS for Indian Languages using Transliteration
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use multilingual ASR character logits in a shared Devanagari transliteration space for query and target audio.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The ASR maps ten languages to transliterated characters; posterior sequences become retrieval features.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Using the Kathbath dataset for training and the IndicSUPERB QbE evaluation set, our approach achieves significant improvements.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The method raises reported MTWV from 0.015 to 0.504 on IndicSUPERB and exceeds the Marathi baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The method raises reported MTWV from 0.015 to 0.504 on IndicSUPERB and exceeds the Marathi baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Language, script, ASR errors, query duration, and splits constrain transfer; script unification is not translation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Effects of Speaker Count, Duration, and Accent Diversity on Zero-Shot Accent Robustness in Low-Resource ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Factor the training-data budget by speaker count, per-speaker duration, and accent diversity, then test zero-shot accents.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Controlled data-composition experiments compare ASR performance across unseen accents and languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Zero-shot accent robustness is evaluated with CER on L2-ARCTIC English, MAGICDATA Mandarin, and CommonVoice Spanish, varying speaker count, per-speaker duration, accent diversity, and single-speaker training. Test scope includes 24 non-native English speakers/six accents, 43 Mandarin speakers/28.1 hours, 647 Spanish speakers/2.3 hours, and an approximately 3.2-hour English test subset; topline models are trained with test accents in-distribution, while single-speaker tests use L1-ARCTIC and FLEURS. CER is used because it correlates strongly with WER in the reported evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that more speakers help more than more hours per speaker, while accent-diversity gains are minimal under controlled speaker count.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that more speakers help more than more hours per speaker, while accent-diversity gains are minimal under controlled speaker count.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, accent labels, low-resource budgets, model/training choices, and zero-shot evaluation bound transfer; this is not a universal data-collection law.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.
