d3_comparison_matrix.title: Co-Speech Motion for Virtual Agents in Dialogue Using LLM-Driven Primitive Action Selection
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use an LLM to plan context and select reusable primitive actions that can be adapted across agents.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The proposed model uses LLM-driven primitive action selection for co-speech motion in virtual agents and robots.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Leveraging the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) for contextual planning and understanding, we propose an LLM-based motion control model that uses a primitive action selection strategy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper presents a flexible and scalable approach, but the preserved evidence does not establish a numerical gain.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper presents a flexible and scalable approach, but the preserved evidence does not establish a numerical gain.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Full mechanism, baselines, human judgments, and cross-embodiment transfer require the paper's detailed evaluation; the result is not a claim of human-like motion.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Fact-Controlled Diagnosis of Hallucinations in Medical Text Summarization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Construct a fact-controlled leave-one-out dataset and a natural hallucination dataset, then compare detection methods in the clinical setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies fact-controlled diagnosis of hallucinations in medical text summarization from patient-clinician dialogues.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we conduct an evaluation of hallucination detection methods in the medical domain, and construct two datasets for the purpose: A fact-controlled Leave-N-out dataset - generated by systematically removing facts from source dialogues to induce hallucinated content in summaries; and a natural hallucination dataset - arising organically during LLM-based medical summarization.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that general-domain detectors struggle on clinical hallucinations and evaluates specialized diagnostic approaches.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that general-domain detectors struggle on clinical hallucinations and evaluates specialized diagnostic approaches.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Synthetic deletion, clinical language, annotation, summarizer, and detector thresholds limit generalization; detection is not prevention or clinical validation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: From Words to Waves: Analyzing Concept Formation in Speech and Text-Based Foundation Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use latent concept analysis to compare speech-only, text-only, and joint foundation models and ask which conceptual structures are shared or modality-specific.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper analyzes concept formation in speech and text-based foundation models using an unsupervised latent-concept method.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To support reproducibility, we have released our code along with a curated audio version of the SST-2 dataset for public access.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports comparative latent conceptual structures across speech, text, and joint models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports comparative latent conceptual structures across speech, text, and joint models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Model choice, layer, analysis method, prompts, and human interpretation bound the claim; a latent cluster is not automatically a human concept.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: AC/DC: LLM-based Audio Comprehension via Dialogue Continuation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train the model to continue a dialogue after an audio-triggered caption, making the target a conversational response.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: An audio encoder feeds an adapter and language model; interleaved audio/text examples use token cross-entropy, with LoRA tested on AudioCaps, WavCaps, and Clotho.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: As a result, our model enables zero-shot instruction-following capability without multitask instruction tuning, even trained solely on audio captioning datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Dialogue-continuation training enables zero-shot instruction following and improves reported AQA, while AAC gains are mixed.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Dialogue-continuation training enables zero-shot instruction following and improves reported AQA, while AAC gains are mixed.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Generated captions, benchmarks, and an LLM judge define the evidence; human usefulness for deaf or hard-of-hearing users is not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Vela: Scalable Embeddings with Voice Large Language Models for Multimodal Retrieval
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt a multimodal language model to produce a universal embedding, using prompts and text-pair training without requiring paired audio in the final training stage.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Vela uses selected prompts and in-context examples, then trains on text pairs; retrieval is tested on ordinary and newly designed long/complex benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Furthermore, we introduce new benchmarks that expose CLAP models' limitations in handling long texts and complex retrieval tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that Vela outperforms traditional CLAP models and is more robust on long, complex retrieval tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that Vela outperforms traditional CLAP models and is more robust on long, complex retrieval tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The abstract says code is forthcoming and the result is tied to the chosen benchmarks and prompts; open-world audio, speech-specific retrieval, and independent reproduction remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Language-Guided Contrastive Audio-Visual Masked Autoencoder with Automatically Generated Audio-Visual-Text Triplets from Videos
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate frame captions, filter audio-caption pairs with a CLAP similarity check, and train a text-guided contrastive masked autoencoder over audio, video, and text.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A pretrained text encoder guides masked audio-visual reconstruction and contrastive learning; automatically formed triplets are used for retrieval and classification tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate LG-CAV-MAE on audio-visual retrieval tasks, as well as an audio-visual classification task.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports up to 5.6% recall@10 improvement for retrieval and 3.2% for classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports up to 5.6% recall@10 improvement for retrieval and 3.2% for classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The video domains, caption generator, CLAP filter, and downstream tasks define the result; spoken conversation and human annotation quality outside those videos remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Face2VoiceSync: Lightweight Face-Voice Consistency for Text-Driven Talking Face Generation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate the talking-face motion and speech jointly from face and text, with a consistency constraint linking the visual identity and vocal output.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Face2VoiceSync targets text-driven talking-face generation from a face image and text, producing animation and corresponding speech while evaluating the consistency of face and voice attributes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Accordingly, we propose a novel framework, Face2VoiceSync, with several novel contributions: 1) Voice-Face Alignment, ensuring generated voices match facial appearance; 2) Diversity & Manipulation, enabling generated voice control over paralinguistic features space; 3) Efficient Training, using a lightweight VAE to bridge visual and audio large-pretrained models, with significantly fewer trainable parameters than existing methods; 4) New Evaluation Metric, fairly assessing the diversity and identity consistency.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved face-voice consistency and text-driven talking-face generation quality relative to fixed-speech baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved face-voice consistency and text-driven talking-face generation quality relative to fixed-speech baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Face identities, text prompts, speech/face datasets, consistency metric, and synchronization quality bound the claim; a consistency score does not prove that a viewer will find the character natural or trustworthy.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pick and Summarize: Integrating Extractive and Abstractive Speech Summarization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: First identify useful excerpts from the speech, then use that auxiliary selection signal to guide abstractive summary generation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: An extractive-abstractive model is trained on a web-presentation corpus, with an extractive summary predicted from raw speech alongside the final text summary.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on a web presentation corpus demonstrate consistent gains with our proposed method, achieving up to 1.4-point gains in METEOR score over a strong abstractive summarization baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The method gives consistent gains and up to 1.4 METEOR points over a strong abstractive baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The method gives consistent gains and up to 1.4 METEOR points over a strong abstractive baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpus, reference summaries, metric, summary length, and presentation style bound the result; lexical overlap does not prove that all important facts were preserved.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards Human-like Multimodal Conversational Agent by Generating Engaging Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use audio-visual context to generate both the response text and a description of the voice style, then synthesize speech that carries the selected paralinguistic cues.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The system builds a multi-sensory conversation dataset and uses a multimodal language model to produce text plus voice descriptions, which guide speech generation in dialogue examples.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Human conversation involves language, speech, and visual cues, with each medium providing complementary information.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports more engaging and contextually suitable speech than text-only baselines and shows gains from visual and audio modalities.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports more engaging and contextually suitable speech than text-only baselines and shows gains from visual and audio modalities.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset role-play, judge criteria, synthetic or recorded voices, conversation domain, and lack of exact-speaker replication bound the claim; engagement scores do not establish long-term human trust or natural conversation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Teaching Audio-Aware Large Language Models What Does Not Hear: Mitigating Hallucinations through Synthesized Negative Samples
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Synthesize negative samples that explicitly represent what the audio does not contain and train the model to distinguish heard evidence from plausible language completion.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper teaches audio-aware large language models what they do not hear through synthesized negative samples.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments show that LISTEN effectively mitigates hallucinations while maintaining impressive performance on existing audio question and reasoning benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports reduced hallucination behavior for the tested audio-aware models and synthesized negative-sample strategy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports reduced hallucination behavior for the tested audio-aware models and synthesized negative-sample strategy.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Negative-sample construction, audio quality, prompts, model family, and evaluation rubric limit the claim; abstention quality is not the same as factual clinical reliability.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Bridging Audio and Vision: Zero-Shot Audiovisual Segmentation by Connecting Pretrained Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Connect pretrained audio and vision models so shared representations can guide zero-shot audiovisual segmentation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies zero-shot audiovisual segmentation by bridging pretrained audio and vision models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Audiovisual segmentation (AVS) aims to identify visual regions corresponding to sound sources, playing a vital role in video understanding, surveillance, and human-computer interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports zero-shot audiovisual segmentation results for the connected pretrained models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports zero-shot audiovisual segmentation results for the connected pretrained models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, categories, synchronization, pretrained models, and segmentation labels bound the result; co-occurrence does not establish physical source identity.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speech-IFEval: Evaluating Instruction-Following and Quantifying Catastrophic Forgetting in Speech-Aware Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use Speech-IFEval to test instruction-following behavior and quantify catastrophic forgetting across speech-aware tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper introduces Speech-IFEval and evaluates instruction-following and forgetting in speech-aware language models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We introduce Speech-IFEval, an evaluation framework designed to assess instruction-following capabilities and quantify catastrophic forgetting in speech-aware language models (SLMs).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports benchmark results for spoken instruction following and catastrophic forgetting.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports benchmark results for spoken instruction following and catastrophic forgetting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Task suite, speech recognition quality, prompts, model families, and training order bound the conclusions; benchmark retention is not proof of reliable deployment behavior.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unified Audio-Visual Modeling for Recognizing Which Face Spoke When and What in Multi-Talker Overlapped Speech and Video
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train one encoder-decoder to emit a serialized sequence containing speaker tags, timing structure, and words from overlapped audio plus all visible faces.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model combines speech and video encoders with Transformer decoding; evaluation compares it with single-talker, multi-talker, and modular audio-visual baselines on LRS3-derived mixtures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The unified audio-visual multi-talker model is evaluated on speaker-disjoint LRS3 splits with noisy overlapped speech and visual speaker tags. WER measures transcription, while visual WER (VWER) measures whether the correct face is associated with the words and visual time error rate (VTER) measures temporal speaker attribution; tag/no-tag, single-/multi-talker, and model-component conditions are compared. Validation-based early stopping and the longer held-out test utterances define the reported boundary.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposed model reports lower or competitive WER/VWER and strong VTER as the number of overlapping speakers rises, with tags placed before or after each transcription tested explicitly.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposed model reports lower or competitive WER/VWER and strong VTER as the number of overlapping speakers rises, with tags placed before or after each transcription tested explicitly.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evidence is bounded to constructed LRS3 mixtures, visible faces, tested overlap counts, and author-reported metrics; natural meetings, missed faces, and long-range turn structure remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Beat gestures made by human-like avatars affect speech perception
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Manipulate beat gestures made by human-like avatars and measure their effect on speech perception under controlled conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies how beat gestures made by human-like avatars affect speech perception.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: While beat gestures have been traditionally investigated in human-to-human communications, nowadays individuals increasingly interact with computer-controlled avatars (e.g., virtual assistants).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports speech-perception effects of avatar beat gestures in the tested stimuli and listener tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports speech-perception effects of avatar beat gestures in the tested stimuli and listener tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Avatar design, gesture timing, speech material, participants, and task bound generalization; a laboratory effect is not proof of conversational benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: The mutual exclusivity bias of bilingual visually grounded speech models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Test mutual-exclusivity behavior in bilingual visually grounded speech models using controlled novel-object and label situations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies mutual exclusivity bias in bilingual visually grounded speech models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Bilingual visually grounded speech models are evaluated with familiar and mutual-exclusivity (ME) two-image discrimination tests on speaker-disjoint test samples. Each class contributes 50 episodes per test, experiments repeat across five training seeds, and monolingual/bilingual English, French, and Dutch models are compared. Familiar accuracy validates learning, while ME accuracy above 50% quantifies the bias: monolingual models are about 67–68%, with bilingual English/French or English/Dutch training reducing English ME accuracy to 65.7% or 63.5%.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports mutual-exclusivity behavior and cross-language differences for the tested bilingual grounded models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports mutual-exclusivity behavior and cross-language differences for the tested bilingual grounded models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, training data, object stimuli, model architecture, prompt/task design, and bias measure bound the claim; model behavior is not a direct account of child learning.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards High-Quality LLM-Based Data for French Spontaneous Speech Simplification: an Exo-Refinement Approach
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use separate external judges for task-specific dimensions and iterate only when their feedback improves simplicity without losing semantic content.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: LLM-generated French speech simplifications are refined by distinct evaluator models and compared with expert simplifications using SARI and COMET.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We introduce the exo-refinement approach, which builds on the self-reflect workflow but differs by using separate models for generation and evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Mistral-large outperforms tested baselines, Mistral-small becomes competitive after few refinements, SARI improves, and COMET indicates semantic preservation in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Mistral-large outperforms tested baselines, Mistral-small becomes competitive after few refinements, SARI improves, and COMET indicates semantic preservation in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The languages, prompts, judges, reference simplifications, and automatic metrics bound the result; COMET and SARI are proxies, not a guarantee of accessible or faithful speech.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: GenECA: A General-Purpose Framework for Real-Time Adaptive Multimodal Embodied Conversational Agents
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a general-purpose real-time multimodal embodied-agent framework that updates perception, dialogue, action, and speech together.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: GenECA is a framework for real-time adaptive multimodal embodied conversational agents.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: GenECA provides the first ECA system able to deliver context-aware speech and well-timed animations in real-time without reliance on human operators.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports real-time adaptive-agent behavior across its tested multimodal interaction settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports real-time adaptive-agent behavior across its tested multimodal interaction settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Sensors, embodiment, latency, dialogue tasks, user studies, and policy constraints bound the claim; a framework demonstration is not human-level social understanding.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SNIFR : Boosting Fine-Grained Child Harmful Content Detection Through Audio-Visual Alignment with Cascaded Cross-Transformer
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align audio and visual evidence with cascaded cross-transformers and predict fine-grained child-harm categories in real time.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SNIFR boosts fine-grained child harmful-content detection through audio-visual alignment with cascaded cross-transformers.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: As video-sharing platforms have grown over the past decade, child viewership has surged, increasing the need for precise detection of harmful content like violence or explicit scenes.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports fine-grained audiovisual detection and real-time behavior for the tested harmful-content data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports fine-grained audiovisual detection and real-time behavior for the tested harmful-content data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Labels, age policy, modalities, cultures, false-positive costs, and latency bound the result; an automated detector is not a safeguarding decision-maker.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Who Gets the Mic? Investigating Gender Bias in the Speaker Assignment of a Speech-LLM
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Probe default speaker assignment with controlled profession and gender-colored-word prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Bark is prompted with two constructed datasets and assignments are counted for gender alignment and inclinations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate Bark, a Text-to-Speech (TTS) model, analyzing its default speaker assignments for textual prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Bark shows gender awareness and some inclinations but no strong systematic bias under the tested prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Bark shows gender awareness and some inclinations but no strong systematic bias under the tested prompts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Two datasets, one model, prompt wording, and supported voices bound the conclusion; this is not a fairness guarantee.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Enhancing Speech Instruction Understanding and Disambiguation in Robotics via Speech Prosody
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Predict token-level goal/detail referents from prosody, then inject those intent cues into an LLM that selects the robot task plan.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Prosodic and raw-audio features feed Transformer or BiLSTM sequence models trained with cross-entropy; predicted referents are placed in prompts for GPT-4o, o1-mini, or o3-mini to choose among plans.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Enabling robots to accurately interpret and execute spoken language instructions is essential for effective human-robot collaboration.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On 1,540 recordings from 22 participants, the best BiLSTM reaches 95.79% overall referent accuracy, and Prosody-Transformer plus GPT-4o reaches 71.96% task-plan accuracy versus 50% for the ASR-only prompt.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On 1,540 recordings from 22 participants, the best BiLSTM reaches 95.79% overall referent accuracy, and Prosody-Transformer plus GPT-4o reaches 71.96% task-plan accuracy versus 50% for the ASR-only prompt.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The dataset is small and participants are 18–22; recorded ambiguity and candidate plans are controlled rather than open-world robot interaction. Prosody helps the tested task but does not establish safe execution in physical environments.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Spoken Question Answering for Visual Queries
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align speech and image encoders directly into a VQA language model so spoken queries and visual evidence can jointly condition the answer.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Whisper encodes speech and CLIP encodes images; modality-specific projectors align both representations with LLaVA's language space, with speech-only pretraining followed by joint spoken-VQA fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Question answering (QA) systems are designed to answer natural language questions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Synthetic speech training approaches the text-trained VQA upper bound on several benchmarks; the paper reports 62% SEED-Bench accuracy for its strongest spoken variants, with TTS choice having a small effect.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Synthetic speech training approaches the text-trained VQA upper bound on several benchmarks; the paper reports 62% SEED-Bench accuracy for its strongest spoken variants, with TTS choice having a small effect.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Most training speech is synthesized, the spoken models remain below the text model, prompt format changes performance sharply, and transcription failures can be confused with visual-reasoning failures. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Discrete Audio Representations for Automated Audio Captioning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare discrete audio representations for caption generation and test whether tokenization retains semantic evidence.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Encode audio into learned discrete tokens, condition a text decoder on those tokens, and compare tokenizers and decoder choices on caption metrics.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Discrete audio representations are compared for automated captioning on Clotho using BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, SPICE, and SPIDEr, with tokenizer and decoder ablations. These reference-caption metrics evaluate agreement with available descriptions and do not directly measure listener grounding.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that selected audio tokenizers improve automated captioning quality, showing that representation design affects semantic generation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that selected audio tokenizers improve automated captioning quality, showing that representation design affects semantic generation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Reference-caption incompleteness, metric proxy limits, dataset scope, and no broad human grounding study limit conclusions about listener usefulness.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Co-Speech Motion for Virtual Agents in Dialogue Using LLM-Driven Primitive Action Selection: A virtual agent must turn dialogue context into a timed body action; primitive selection makes the response an explicit interactional choice.; Using and comprehending language in face-to-face conversation: Face-to-face meaning is jointly carried by speech, gesture, face, and head movement, with timing affecting comprehension and response.; Towards Human-like Multimodal Conversational Agent by Generating Engaging Speech: The title and preserved abstract identify a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate interactional-feedback under dialogue-and-turn-taking; this resolves taxonomy membership only. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: Feedback can be sparse, ambiguous, or shaped by users adapting to the system's mistakes.

records.subtheme_name: Turning language plans into audible speech
records.question: How does a text or linguistic plan become a timed, pronounceable signal?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: A useful synthetic voice must say the requested content, sound like the intended speaker or style, and remain understandable as it changes over time. The subtheme asks: How does a text or linguistic plan become a timed, pronounceable signal?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with text-to-speech planning, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Text does not specify one correct prosody, and a fluent output can still mispronounce names or sound unnatural.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make text-to-speech planning, waveform synthesis, intelligibility versus naturalness explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Transfer pronunciation knowledge from a large multi-accent frontend and measure how much target-accent data is needed as source accents vary in similarity.
subtheme_boundary: Text does not specify one correct prosody, and a fluent output can still mispronounce names or sound unnatural.
Sample-level realism does not guarantee correct words, stable identity, or natural long-range timing.
A single listener score can conflate content accuracy, recording quality, and preference.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Non-Standard Accent TTS Support via Large Multi-Accent Frontend Pronunciation Knowledge Transfer: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate text-to-speech-planning within text-to-speech-and-content.; DS-Codec: Dual-Stage Training with Mirror-to-NonMirror Architecture Switching for Speech Codec: A speech codec must compress a waveform into usable tokens and reconstruct it; mirror/non-mirror training targets reconstruction quality for TTS.; AF-Vocoder: Artifact-Free Neural Vocoder with Global Artifact Filter: An artifact-free vocoder must reconstruct fine waveform detail without introducing audible periodic or transient artifacts that undermine naturalness.; Accelerating Diffusion-based Text-to-Speech Model Trainingwith Dual Modality Alignment: Dual-modality alignment gives diffusion TTS a shared text-and-speech target so linguistic content can guide waveform generation.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Transfer pronunciation knowledge from a large multi-accent frontend and measure how much target-accent data is needed as source accents vary in similarity.
Train in two stages: first use a mirror architecture to stabilize the codebook, then switch to a stronger non-mirror decoder while preserving the learned quantizer.
Add a learnable frequency-domain artifact filter that imposes explicit control over which spectral components pass.
Align hidden states using both text-guided and speech-guided objectives so the diffusion process starts with more useful semantic structure.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Non-Standard Accent TTS Support via Large Multi-Accent Frontend Pronunciation Knowledge Transfer
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Transfer pronunciation knowledge from a large multi-accent frontend and measure how much target-accent data is needed as source accents vary in similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The frontend predicts phones, lexical stress, and prosodic boundaries; target accents are trained with reduced data and compared with full-data and single-accent baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The multi-accent pronunciation frontend is tested on EDI and LDS1 accents against uni-accent baselines using word-boundary, prosodic-boundary, and word accuracy for seen and unseen tokens. The paper reports multi-accent accuracy near the uni-accent baseline, with seen-word scores above 99% and lower unseen-word accuracy as the harder transfer case.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports up to 95% less pronunciation training data for robust performance and examines 14 English accents using LibriTTS and HiFi-TTS-derived data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports up to 95% less pronunciation training data for robust performance and examines 14 English accents using LibriTTS and HiFi-TTS-derived data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Accuracy is reported for the studied accents, frontend labels, and datasets; transfer to other languages, voices, and synthesis backends remains unestablished.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: DS-Codec: Dual-Stage Training with Mirror-to-NonMirror Architecture Switching for Speech Codec
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train in two stages: first use a mirror architecture to stabilize the codebook, then switch to a stronger non-mirror decoder while preserving the learned quantizer.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: DS-Codec uses vector and product quantization with one 8,192-entry codebook, a downsampling encoder, recurrent/transformer decoder components, and time/frequency discriminators; ablations compare mirror and non-mirror stages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We conduct extensive experiments and ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of our training strategy and compare the performance of the two architectures.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that mirror-stage training outperforms APCodec+ and the non-mirror alternatives on its objective measures, with lower reconstruction error and fewer training epochs/cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that mirror-stage training outperforms APCodec+ and the non-mirror alternatives on its objective measures, with lower reconstruction error and fewer training epochs/cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The speech data, bitrate/downsampling setting, discriminators, metrics, and baselines bound the result; reconstruction quality does not by itself prove usefulness for every TTS or speech-language-model task.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: AF-Vocoder: Artifact-Free Neural Vocoder with Global Artifact Filter
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add a learnable frequency-domain artifact filter that imposes explicit control over which spectral components pass.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: AF-Vocoder inserts GAFilter into a GAN vocoder and tests reconstruction quality and artifact suppression across datasets and speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we propose AF-Vocoder, a novel GAN-based vocoder that can synthesize high-fidelity speech with fewer artifacts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better reconstruction quality and artifact suppression than other GAN vocoders.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better reconstruction quality and artifact suppression than other GAN vocoders.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, speaker coverage, artifacts, and listening protocol define the claim; real-time hardware cost and unseen languages remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Accelerating Diffusion-based Text-to-Speech Model Trainingwith Dual Modality Alignment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align hidden states using both text-guided and speech-guided objectives so the diffusion process starts with more useful semantic structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A-DMA aligns contextual text representations and discriminative speech features during diffusion TTS training, then compares convergence and synthesis quality with baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The diffusion TTS model is trained on approximately 585 hours of multi-speaker LibriTTS and evaluated on the 2.2-hour LibriSpeech-PC test-clean set. WER measures intelligibility and speaker similarity is measured against the F5-TTS Small baseline; the paper reports comparisons for the dual-modality alignment configuration.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports doubled convergence speed with better performance than its baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports doubled convergence speed with better performance than its baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The text/speech encoders, datasets, diffusion schedule, and quality measures bound the claim; hardware cost and new languages remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Scheduled Interleaved Speech-Text Training for Speech-to-Speech Translation with LLMs
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Interleave aligned text and speech units during training, then gradually reduce the text proportion so the model moves toward speech output.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: LLaMA3.2-1B is fine-tuned on CVSS with scheduled interleaving and evaluated across translation directions and resource levels.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We conduct experimental evaluations by fine-tuning LLaMA3.2-1B for S2ST on the CVSS dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports consistent translation improvements, especially in limited-data languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports consistent translation improvements, especially in limited-data languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: CVSS, unitizer, schedule, model size, and languages bound the result; naturalness, speaker identity, and unseen domains need separate tests.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Code Mix TTS: An Approach to Infer Human Like Speech for Multi-Lingual Input Texts
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Infer code-mixed speech from multilingual text without requiring additional training data or fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The proposed inference procedure sends multilingual input through an existing TTS system and evaluates generated code-mixed speech with automated MOS-style measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We have come a far way in terms of producing high quality, human like audios for given input texts using TTS or Text to Speech Systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports an approach for code-mix inference without extra data or fine-tuning; the preserved evidence does not establish broad human preference gains.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports an approach for code-mix inference without extra data or fine-tuning; the preserved evidence does not establish broad human preference gains.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The paper's method and evaluation details are bounded by the selected TTS system, languages, and automated metric; human listening, pronunciation accuracy, and unseen language pairs remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Analyzing Mitigation Strategies for Catastrophic Forgetting in End-to-End Training of Spoken Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare mitigation strategies for catastrophic forgetting during end-to-end spoken-language-model training, including how data and parameter updates are controlled.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates forgetting-mitigation strategies for end-to-end training of spoken language models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: End-to-end training of Spoken Language Models (SLMs) commonly involves adapting pre-trained text-based Large Language Models (LLMs) to the speech modality through multi-stage training on diverse tasks such as ASR, TTS and spoken question answering (SQA).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports comparative forgetting and adaptation results across the tested strategies.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports comparative forgetting and adaptation results across the tested strategies.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Tasks, training order, model size, data mixture, and retention metrics bound the conclusions; results do not establish lifelong learning in open deployment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Vocoder-Projected Feature Discriminator
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Project generated acoustic features through a vocoder and discriminate in a vocoder-feature space, retaining waveform-relevant feedback with lower time-domain overhead.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The vocoder-projected feature discriminator compares feature representations after synthesis; diffusion-based voice-conversion distillation tests whether the adversarial target improves the generated waveform.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Vocoder-Projected Feature Discriminator is evaluated on VCTK and LibriTTS using UTMOS, DNSMOS, Whisper-large-v3 CER, Resemblyzer SECS, training time, and peak memory. Ablations vary discriminator upsampling depth, pretraining/freezing, and alternative acceleration strategies; the main subjective comparison uses 90 speaker/sentence pairs, ground-truth and DiffVC-30 anchors, and more than 1,000 responses from 11 participants for five-point quality MOS and four-point similarity MOS.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved diffusion-based VC distillation quality from the projected-feature discriminator under the evaluated settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved diffusion-based VC distillation quality from the projected-feature discriminator under the evaluated settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Vocoder choice, feature projection, training compute, VC data, and perceptual evaluation determine the result; a reported quality gain does not establish universal TTS or VC superiority.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: BitTTS: Highly Compact Text-to-Speech Using 1.58-bit Quantization and Weight Indexing
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train with quantization present and pack groups of ternary-like weights into compact integer indices so the model learns to tolerate the reduced precision and storage format.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: BitTTS uses quantization-aware training down to 1.58-bit, with most weights represented as -1, 0, or 1, and weight indexing that stores groups as int8 indices for on-device use.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this case, most of 32-bit model parameters are quantized to ternary values {-1, 0, 1}.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports an 83% reduction in model size and better synthesis quality than a similar-size unquantized baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports an 83% reduction in model size and better synthesis quality than a similar-size unquantized baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Hardware, model architecture, bitrate/precision, speech data, and quality metrics bound the result; smaller storage does not automatically mean lower latency or energy on every device.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Revival with Voice: Multi-modal Controllable Text-to-Speech Synthesis
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Augment face-driven training with high-quality audio-only speech, stylize face inputs to cover artistic portraits, and condition synthesis on natural-language control descriptions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The face encoder supplies speaker or voice information, while text conditioning specifies controllable attributes; multi-modal training aligns these conditions with waveform generation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: 2) To generate voices not only from real human faces but also from artistic portraits, we propose augmenting the input face image with stylization.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Revival with Voice reports controllable synthesis from real and artistic face inputs and improved use of high-quality audio-only data in the tested settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Revival with Voice reports controllable synthesis from real and artistic face inputs and improved use of high-quality audio-only data in the tested settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Face distribution, language, control wording, subjective protocol, and disentanglement assumptions limit the claim; controllability is not proof of identity fidelity or safe use of a person's likeness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Efficient Streaming TTS Acoustic Model with Depthwise RVQ Decoding Strategies in a Mamba Framework
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a Mamba acoustic model with depthwise residual-codec decoding: masked refinement preserves dependencies, while implicit neural representation predicts levels in parallel.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SMAM is tested with MLM, INR, and no-MLM decoding in a zero-shot speaker-conditioned setup; CER, similarity, quality, real-time factor, latency, and listening scores separate tradeoffs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The streaming TTS acoustic model is evaluated on 500 test utterances from seen speakers, with objective metrics computed over all 500 and subjective listening on the selected test material. CER, SECS, UTMOS, real-time factor, latency, MOS, and similarity MOS compare the proposed Mamba/RVQ variants with streaming baselines; MOS/SMOS use five-point ratings and 95% confidence intervals, while ablations remove masked-language-model and INR components.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposed models are smaller and faster than listed non-streaming baselines while remaining competitive; removing MLM degrades quality measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposed models are smaller and faster than listed non-streaming baselines while remaining competitive; removing MLM degrades quality measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Codec, datasets, hardware, and zero-shot speaker conditions bound the conclusion; other languages and devices are not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Long-Context Speech Synthesis with Context-Aware Memory
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Maintain long-term and local context in a dynamic memory and use a prefix mask to provide bidirectional context to sentence-level synthesis while keeping generation causal.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The context-aware memory retrieves and updates paragraph information; local details and long-term style guide each sentence, while prefix tokens supply in-context information without unrestricted future leakage.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Long-context speech synthesis is evaluated on 20 sentence-level samples and 10 roughly 60-second long-form samples, rated by 10 native Mandarin listeners on MOS and CoMOS scales from 1 to 5 with 95% intervals. Objective measures are speaker-vector similarity, CER from Paraformer-zh, and SpeechBERTScore; experiments compare MMCE-Qformer, CLAP-RAG, the proposed memory/prefix-mask model, and module ablations while reporting context-token cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The model outperforms the reported baselines on paragraph-level prosody expressiveness, coherence, and context-inference cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The model outperforms the reported baselines on paragraph-level prosody expressiveness, coherence, and context-inference cost.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Text genre, speaker/style conditioning, subjective measures, memory capacity, and paragraph length bound transfer; coherence scores do not prove human preference in broad long-form use.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SpeechSEC: A Unified Multi-Task Framework for Speech Synthesis, Editing, and Continuation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a unified non-autoregressive framework whose input conditions select synthesis, editing, or continuation, while shared training captures common acoustic structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model dynamically changes conditioning for each task and remains compatible with multiple speech discretizers such as HuBERT, DAC, and SpeechTokenizer.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: SpeechSEC is evaluated on LibriTTS-R train-clean subsets with test-clean held out, across speech synthesis, editing, and continuation using SpeechTokenizer, SpeechTokenizer/DAC, and HuBERT/DAC token configurations. WER/CER measure intelligibility, MOS-style audio quality and cosine similarity measure quality/voice preservation, and RTX 3090 acoustic-token generation time measures efficiency; continuation omits WER/CER because generated content is variable. Baselines and edit/continuation ablations isolate the multi-task benefit.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: SpeechSEC reports MOS-like audio quality of 4.20 versus 4.00 and voice preservation of 0.72 versus 0.58 for synthesis, with usable editing and continuation results.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: SpeechSEC reports MOS-like audio quality of 4.20 versus 4.00 and voice preservation of 0.72 versus 0.58 for synthesis, with usable editing and continuation results.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Reported scores, codec choice, task mixture, prompts, speakers, and sample protocol bound the comparison; multi-task compatibility is not proof of editing safety or continuity in arbitrary audio.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Noise Robustness of LLM-based Zero-shot TTS via Discrete Acoustic Token Denoising
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Denoise the first acoustic-token groups with a neural codec token predictor, refine the embedding, and use the cleaned prompt in LauraTTS.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The token denoiser predicts clean coarse tokens; an embedding refiner and codec decoder reconstruct usable acoustic evidence before the zero-shot TTS model conditions generation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: NR-LauraTTS is evaluated first as a speech-enhancement codec denoiser against CMGAN and MP-SENet using DNSMOS P.835 SIG, BAK, and OVRL plus FLOPs, then as noise-robust zero-shot TTS on 3–10-second test samples with same-speaker noisy prompts. SECS, Whisper-large-v3 WER/CER, MOS, and SMOS are reported; more than 30 Mechanical Turk raters each score 20 samples on 1–5 scales with 95% MOS/SMOS intervals. Clean-prompt, noisy-prompt, MP-SENet, and NR-LauraTTS conditions bound the comparison.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that its codec denoiser outperforms speech-enhancement baselines and that noise-robust LauraTTS improves over adding an external enhancer.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that its codec denoiser outperforms speech-enhancement baselines and that noise-robust LauraTTS improves over adding an external enhancer.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Noise types, prompt duration, speaker overlap, codec/model version, and zero-shot evaluation bound transfer; clean synthesis from a prompt is not speaker-authenticated identity preservation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: RapFlow-TTS: Rapid and High-Fidelity Text-to-Speech with Improved Consistency Flow Matching
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train RapFlow-TTS with velocity consistency along a straightened flow-matching trajectory, plus time scheduling and adversarial refinement.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model learns that velocity predictions at different time points agree along the transport path; consistency allows few-step integration while adversarial and acoustic losses protect waveform quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To address this challenge, RapFlow-TTS enforces consistency in the velocity field along the FM-straightened ODE trajectory, enabling consistent synthetic quality with fewer generation steps.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports high-fidelity synthesis with fewer generation steps than compared flow/diffusion systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports high-fidelity synthesis with fewer generation steps than compared flow/diffusion systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Text/speaker data, subjective protocol, step counts, vocoder and hardware, and adversarial stability bound the speed-quality claim; fewer steps do not guarantee lower end-to-end latency.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Intelligibility of Text-to-Speech Systems for Mathematical Expressions
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Evaluate the full chain—LLM pronunciation generation, TTS rendering, listener comprehension, expert comparison, and expression category—using both perceptual and transcription-based measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study samples 120 expressions across eight categories, uses Qwen or GPT-4 to create spoken text, synthesizes audio with five TTS models, and asks 49 technically trained listeners to rate and transcribe it. A second test compares 35 expressions with hidden expert renditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: There has been limited evaluation of advanced Text-to-Speech (TTS) models with Mathematical eXpressions (MX) as inputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: No TTS model is consistently strong across categories; intelligibility varies by expression type and model, and the outputs are generally worse than expert renditions. Pronunciation correctness is reported at 87.5% overall, with category-dependent listener success.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: No TTS model is consistently strong across categories; intelligibility varies by expression type and model, and the outputs are generally worse than expert renditions. Pronunciation correctness is reported at 87.5% overall, with category-dependent listener success.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The expressions, listeners, languages, LLMs, and five TTS systems define the scope; technical listeners and repeated playback may not represent ordinary users. Transcription and MOS remain proxies for mathematical comprehension, and no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Tungnaá In Live Performance: An Implementation Of Interactive Artistic Text-To-Voice
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Define interactive artistic text-to-voice around a reduced-phonetic-alphabet dataset, streaming vocoder, bounded look-ahead, and a GUI that exposes live controls.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The system separates alignment/generation into streaming components, buffers a small number of frames to trade latency for stability, and keeps the interface in a separate process.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Tungnaá is evaluated as an interactive artistic text-to-voice performance system using its IATV dataset, reduced phonetic alphabet representation, and live performance workflow. Evidence concerns the implementation's real-time worker/GUI architecture, customizability on small bespoke datasets, latent feedback control, and performance deployment; the paper does not provide a held-out recognition score, listener study, latency table, or conventional quantitative denominator.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The demonstration reports real-time inference with worst-case latency below 100 ms and a bespoke performance dataset/application.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The demonstration reports real-time inference with worst-case latency below 100 ms and a bespoke performance dataset/application.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Demonstration scope, artist-specific data, reduced phonetic alphabet, hardware, subjective quality, and no controlled comparison bound generalization; live usability is not a standard TTS benchmark.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Bridging the Training–Inference Gap in TTS: Training Strategies for Robust Generative Postprocessing for Low-Resource Speakers
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate training examples from high-resource speakers and train GAN or consistency-flow postprocessors selected for low-resource targets.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Forward Tacotron features are refined by GAN and CFM postprocessors, then compared with listening and ranking tests.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate it through listening tests, demonstrating consistent improvements in the naturalness of the synthetic speech across different postprocessing models and low-resource target speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Both proposed postprocessors improve reported naturalness; the CFM gain over its standard version is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Both proposed postprocessors improve reported naturalness; the CFM gain over its standard version is not significant.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Two speakers, ground-truth prosody in part of evaluation, selected data, and reported tests limit arbitrary-voice claims.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Non-Standard Accent TTS Support via Large Multi-Accent Frontend Pronunciation Knowledge Transfer: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate text-to-speech-planning within text-to-speech-and-content.; Accelerating Diffusion-based Text-to-Speech Model Trainingwith Dual Modality Alignment: Dual-modality alignment gives diffusion TTS a shared text-and-speech target so linguistic content can guide waveform generation.; Scheduled Interleaved Speech-Text Training for Speech-to-Speech Translation with LLMs: Interleaving speech and text training for speech-to-speech translation couples linguistic planning with generated vocal output. concept_families.boundary: Sample-level realism does not guarantee correct words, stable identity, or natural long-range timing.

records.subtheme_name: Changing who sounds like they are speaking
records.question: How can voice identity change while the spoken message remains the same?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: A useful synthetic voice must say the requested content, sound like the intended speaker or style, and remain understandable as it changes over time. The subtheme asks: How can voice identity change while the spoken message remains the same?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with speaker identity representation, but that shortcut misses the boundary: A short recording can encode noise, emotion, or demographic stereotypes rather than stable identity.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make speaker identity representation, voice conversion, unseen-speaker synthesis explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Use voice conversion as augmentation to reduce speaker bias, then evaluate on a newly collected real-world cross-domain set.
subtheme_boundary: A short recording can encode noise, emotion, or demographic stereotypes rather than stable identity.
Conversion may leak source identity, distort pronunciation, or require target-speaker data unavailable in practice.
Similarity on a benchmark does not establish consent, identity security, or robustness to unusual voices.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Voice Conversion Improves Cross-Domain Robustness  for Spoken Arabic Dialect Identification: Voice conversion is used as augmentation to reduce speaker bias, and the real-world cross-domain test asks whether identity variation is being mistaken for task evidence.; VoxAging: Continuously Tracking Speaker Aging with a Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset in English and Mandarin: The longitudinal recordings ask how speaker verification changes as a person ages; time-varying identity is the phenomenon being measured.; Towards Better Disentanglement in Non-Autoregressive Zero-Shot Expressive Voice Conversion: The model separates multilingual content units from expressive voice controls so a new speaker/style can be produced without changing the requested content.; REWIND: Speech Time Reversal for Enhancing Speaker Representations in Diffusion-based Voice Conversion: The method uses time reversal to destroy much linguistic order while retaining speaker-related cues, then uses those representations for voice conversion.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Use voice conversion as augmentation to reduce speaker bias, then evaluate on a newly collected real-world cross-domain set.
Build a longitudinal English/Mandarin resource and measure how aging changes verification evidence.
