records.subtheme_name: Identity, age, gender, and speaking style
records.question: Which voice differences should be preserved, normalized, or treated as evidence?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Voice depends on anatomy, age, health, emotion, language history, social setting, and equipment; these differences affect both communication and measurement. The subtheme asks: Which voice differences should be preserved, normalized, or treated as evidence?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with speaker verification, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Similarity scores are not identity proof and depend on enrollment quality, population, and decision threshold.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make speaker verification, age and developmental speech, within-speaker state variation explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Initialize an interactive phonetic agent model with real speech from two Southern Italian varieties and simulate metaphony, then compare diphthongization and categorical contrasts.
subtheme_boundary: Similarity scores are not identity proof and depend on enrollment quality, population, and decision threshold.
Age prediction or age normalization can encode stereotypes and may not address the actual recognition failure.
There is no universal stable identity vector independent of context.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Agent-based modelling, sound change, and metaphony in Southern Italian varieties of Italo-Romance.: Agent-based sound-change modeling treats speakers and communities as sources of variation rather than nuisance deviations from one pronunciation.; Pitch Target Realization in Putonghua Tone Production of Children from Dialect-Speaking Regions: Children from dialect-speaking regions realize tone targets through both development and language background, so age cannot be treated as a nuisance independent of variety.; Towards Robust Speaker Recognition against Intrinsic Variation with Foundation Model Few-shot Tuning and Effective Speech Synthesis: Robust speaker recognition tests whether identity survives intrinsic changes in a person's voice instead of being confused with a fixed acoustic profile.; Pushing the Frontiers of Self-Distillation Prototypes Network with Dimension Regularization and Score Normalization: The paper addresses collapse and score calibration in speaker representations without speaker labels.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Initialize an interactive phonetic agent model with real speech from two Southern Italian varieties and simulate metaphony, then compare diphthongization and categorical contrasts.
Analyze on-target and off-target realization as interacting targets shaped by physiology and dialect experience.
Use few-shot foundation-model tuning at enrollment and generate style-rich synthetic speech to expose time-varying and emotional conditions, with losses focused on unknown outliers.
Add dimension regularization to a self-distillation prototype network and use score normalization to close the gap toward supervised verification.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Agent-based modelling, sound change, and metaphony in Southern Italian varieties of Italo-Romance.
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Initialize an interactive phonetic agent model with real speech from two Southern Italian varieties and simulate metaphony, then compare diphthongization and categorical contrasts.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper tests an agent-based model of dialect contact and morpho-phonological sound change.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The study uses an agent-based computational model to test the hypothesis that contact between two dialects that are conservative and innovative as far as a sound change is concerned produces an asymmetric shift of the conservative speakers towards the innovative ones.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The reported results provide support for an asymmetric shift toward the innovative dialect and are consistent with feedback models of sound change.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The reported results provide support for an asymmetric shift toward the innovative dialect and are consistent with feedback models of sound change.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The two dialects, 54 speakers collapsed to 13 agents, selected words, F1 trajectory representation, and model assumptions limit generalization to other communities or changes.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pitch Target Realization in Putonghua Tone Production of Children from Dialect-Speaking Regions
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Analyze on-target and off-target realization as interacting targets shaped by physiology and dialect experience.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Pitch production from 139 Changli-exposed children aged 35–71 months is analyzed in the CL-CHILD corpus.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study examines the production of Putonghua tones from both on- and off-target perspectives, using data from 139 children (aged 35–71 months) with Changli dialect exposure, drawn from the CL-CHILD corpus.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports universal physiological constraints, persistent dialect interference, and off-target forms arising from phonetic similarity and target interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports universal physiological constraints, persistent dialect interference, and off-target forms arising from phonetic similarity and target interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The age range, dialect exposure, corpus, and tone inventory bound the developmental claim; longitudinal and other language environments remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards Robust Speaker Recognition against Intrinsic Variation with Foundation Model Few-shot Tuning and Effective Speech Synthesis
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use few-shot foundation-model tuning at enrollment and generate style-rich synthetic speech to expose time-varying and emotional conditions, with losses focused on unknown outliers.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The framework selects synthetic speech, tunes the foundation model with few enrollment examples, and evaluates open-set identification across time-varying and emotional benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments demonstrate strong generalization across multiple time-varying and emotionally rich benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports stronger generalization to aging and emotional variation while maintaining resistance to unknown outliers.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports stronger generalization to aging and emotional variation while maintaining resistance to unknown outliers.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The claim is bounded to the synthetic-data choices, foundation model, enrollment protocol, and benchmarks; real aging trajectories, spoofing attacks, and fairness across groups remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pushing the Frontiers of Self-Distillation Prototypes Network with Dimension Regularization and Score Normalization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add dimension regularization to a self-distillation prototype network and use score normalization to close the gap toward supervised verification.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper improves self-supervised speaker verification with dimension regularization and score normalization.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: SDPN with dimension regularization and score normalization sets a new state-of-the-art on the VoxCeleb1 speaker verification evaluation benchmark, achieving Equal Error Rate 1.29%, 1.60%, and 2.80% for trial VoxCeleb1-{O,E,H} respectively.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On VoxCeleb1, the paper reports EERs of 1.29%, 1.60%, and 2.80% on the O/E/H trials and relative improvements over prior self-supervised methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On VoxCeleb1, the paper reports EERs of 1.29%, 1.60%, and 2.80% on the O/E/H trials and relative improvements over prior self-supervised methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: VoxCeleb1, trial conditions, unlabeled-training setup, score normalization, and EER bound the claim; benchmark gains do not establish fairness or robustness in deployment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speech Unlearning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Define sample-level and class-level unlearning and test whether a model forgets the target while preserving performance on remaining speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Keyword-spotting and speaker-identification experiments compare removing one recording with removing an entire speaker category and examine the difficulty relative to image and text unlearning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In addition, we propose to use subset performances and membership inference attack as evaluation metrics.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that speech unlearning is substantially harder than image or text unlearning and identifies structured training, evaluation, feature-level removal, and adversarial robustness as open directions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that speech unlearning is substantially harder than image or text unlearning and identifies structured training, evaluation, feature-level removal, and adversarial robustness as open directions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Tasks, speakers, unlearning definitions, attack tests, and evaluation criteria bound the result; a proposed forgetting score is not proof of privacy against every adversary.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Analysis of the ABC Classification Backends for NIST SRE24
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Analyze the ABC classification backends used for NIST SRE24 and separate representation quality from backend scoring behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies backend choices for speaker classification/verification in the NIST SRE24 setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present an analysis of the classification backends of the ABC submission for the audio tracks of the NIST 2024 Speaker Recognition Evaluation (SRE24).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports how the analyzed backends behave on the NIST SRE24 evaluation conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports how the analyzed backends behave on the NIST SRE24 evaluation conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Benchmark protocol, language/channel conditions, calibration, and chosen operating points limit claims beyond SRE24.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Copula-Based Generative Score-Level Fusion Model for Speaker Verification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Model the joint score distribution with flexible marginals and a copula that captures dependency, then fuse and calibrate scores.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Variance-Gamma marginals describe each recognizer's score distribution and a Gaussian copula describes dependence for target and non-target trials.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our results on NIST SRE 2019 and SITW datasets show that our approach is competitive with respect to state-of-the-art discriminative score fusion techniques, providing both accurate and well-calibrated scores, with a measured Cllr reduction of up to 7% relative with respect to discriminative linear fusion methods.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On NIST SRE 2019 and SITW, the method reports up to 7% relative Cllr reduction versus discriminative linear fusion.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On NIST SRE 2019 and SITW, the method reports up to 7% relative Cllr reduction versus discriminative linear fusion.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, recognizer diversity, score distributions, and calibration protocol bound the result; new speakers, channels, and attacks need separate evaluation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Inter-Speaker Relative Cues for Text-Guided Target Speech Extraction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Describe the target relative to the interfering speaker, then combine relative cues and pretrained speech representations in a text-conditioned extractor.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Two-speaker mixtures are built across five languages with cues for language, gender, emotion, order, age, rate, duration, pitch, loudness, and distance; prompts identify the target by those relations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Relative cues offers greater flexibility than fixed speech attribute classification, facilitating much easier expansion of text-guided target speech extraction datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that all relative cues beat random subsets, with gender and temporal order especially robust across languages and reverberation; WavLM/CNN initialization improves the baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that all relative cues beat random subsets, with gender and temporal order especially robust across languages and reverberation; WavLM/CNN initialization improves the baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The claim is bounded to the constructed mixtures, cue templates, languages, and author-reported tests; real conversational mixtures and privacy effects remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: An Investigative Study on Recent Sharpness- and Flatness-Based Optimizers for Enhanced Self-Supervised Speaker Verification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Treat the optimization geometry itself as part of the identity-learning problem: compare ordinary, mixture-based, and sharpness-aware optimizers and regularizers instead of changing only the network architecture.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study trains supervised and self-supervised speaker-verification systems with ADOPT, AdEMAMix, SAM, ASAM, GAM, and GSAM, then tests weight decay, exponential moving averages, and SWITCH EMA. The comparison asks whether flatter or better-conditioned solutions improve verification generalization without adding an inference-time identity module.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: While Adam and Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) remain the most popular optimizers in deep learning, other optimizers such as Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), simultaneously minimizing loss value and minimizing loss sharpness and/or improving flatness, have proven to be more effective across a variety of tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that optimizer choice materially changes generalization and that the tested sharpness-aware and general-purpose optimizers can reach state-of-the-art self-supervised speaker-verification results in its experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that optimizer choice materially changes generalization and that the tested sharpness-aware and general-purpose optimizers can reach state-of-the-art self-supervised speaker-verification results in its experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The conclusions are bounded by the selected speaker-verification corpora, architectures, optimizer settings, and author-reported comparisons; a better optimizer score does not establish robustness to every language, channel, attack, or demographic group. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Egocentric Speaker Classification in Child-Adult Dyadic Interactions: From Sensing to Computational Modeling
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Treat the egocentric sensor as part of the task, model the child/adult dyad under that perspective, and evaluate how sensing choices affect automatic speaker classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies wearable sensing in BOSCC child–clinician interactions, uses egocentric speech sampling, and evaluates computational speaker classification for behavioral analysis related to autism treatment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: One important research area in ASD is evaluating children's behavioral changes over time during treatment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that egocentric sensing provides useful information for child/adult speaker classification and highlights the promise and constraints of wearable speech modeling.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that egocentric sensing provides useful information for child/adult speaker classification and highlights the promise and constraints of wearable speech modeling.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: BOSCC activities, children/clinicians, sensor placement, privacy, and speaker labels bound the result; classification is not a direct measure of social communication or treatment outcome.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: How sibilant spectra shape gender perception in prepubertal children: A voice morphing study
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use natural and voice-morphed stimuli to separate the acoustic contribution of /z/ sibilant spectral shape from the broader voice and social context.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The longitudinal study measures center of gravity and skewness of /z/ in German-speaking children aged 6–9 and runs gender-perception experiments with natural and morphed voices.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Center of Gravity (CoG) and skewness were measured in the sibilant /z/.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: No overall gender differences in the measured sibilant features were found; sibilants did not affect gender perception in natural stimuli but did affect it in morphed stimuli, suggesting stereotypical associations in isolation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: No overall gender differences in the measured sibilant features were found; sibilants did not affect gender perception in natural stimuli but did affect it in morphed stimuli, suggesting stereotypical associations in isolation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Age, language, stimulus construction, listener beliefs, longitudinal sample, and morphing artifacts bound the claim; a perceptual association is not a biological marker or justification for gender classification.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: You Are What You Say: Exploiting Linguistic Content for VoicePrivacy Attacks
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt BERT to attack speaker identity from transcript content, inspect explainable keywords, and compare the resulting EER and dataset construction.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The attacker maps linguistic content to speaker labels; semantically similar utterances become a non-acoustic identity channel in the evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To evaluate their privacy benefits, attacks in the form of automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are employed.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports mean EER around 35%, with some speakers as low as 2%, using text alone on VoicePrivacy data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports mean EER around 35%, with some speakers as low as 2%, using text alone on VoicePrivacy data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dataset curation, speaker/content overlap, BERT training, split design, and EER interpretation bound the claim; text leakage does not prove an anonymizer fails acoustically.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: EmoSpeechAuth: Emotion-Aware Speaker Verification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build emotion-aware speaker verification and test identity evidence across affective states.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The verifier separates speaker-consistent structure from emotion-dependent variation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Prior approaches were more computationally expensive and did not focus on the state-of-the-art speaker representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper presents EmoSpeechAuth and evaluates emotion-aware speaker verification.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper presents EmoSpeechAuth and evaluates emotion-aware speaker verification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Emotion labels, speakers, channel, enrollment, thresholds, and demographics bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unified Text and Speaker Verification using SSL model for Text-Dependent Speaker Verification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a unified self-supervised student for text validation and speaker verification, then evaluate tandem decisions across multilingual trials.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The student preserves lexical information for text validation while a speaker backend supplies identity evidence; DeepMine and VoxCeleb1 test both modes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluation on different datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The student improves reported text-dependent and DeepMine results but degrades VoxCeleb1 text-independent results relative to ReDimNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The student improves reported text-dependent and DeepMine results but degrades VoxCeleb1 text-independent results relative to ReDimNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, languages, content, thresholds, and reported EERs bound the conclusion; open-set deployment is unestablished.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: PAEFF: Precise Alignment and Enhanced Gated Feature Fusion for Face-Voice Association
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align the modalities with orthogonality constraints and gated feature fusion in a joint hyperbolic space, where hierarchy-like distances can represent identity similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The two branches extract pretrained face and voice features, fuse them, and optimize a combination of association, orthogonality, and hyperbolic objectives on VoxCeleb1.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Extensive experiments on the VoxCeleb dataset reveals the merits of the proposed approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On the reported VoxCeleb1 splits, PAEFF improves the best listed baseline on unseen-unheard EER and reaches the highest or near-highest AUC in the table.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On the reported VoxCeleb1 splits, PAEFF improves the best listed baseline on unseen-unheard EER and reaches the highest or near-highest AUC in the table.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is author-reported and tied to VoxCeleb1, its split protocol, pretrained encoders, and hyperparameters; it does not establish robustness to dubbing, adversarial pairing, or other cultures.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Variability in performance across four generations of automatic speaker recognition systems
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Evaluate four generations on the same forensic test/calibration data at both system and individual-speaker levels.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Matched evaluation separates model-generation effects from test-set changes and decomposes variation by file and speaker factors.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Adoption of new approaches has mainly been driven by improvements observed in overall system-level performance metrics on common datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Performance improves from GMM-UBM through i-vector and x-vector but not ECAPA-TDNN in the reported comparison; some individuals remain difficult across systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Performance improves from GMM-UBM through i-vector and x-vector but not ECAPA-TDNN in the reported comparison; some individuals remain difficult across systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Forensic data, calibration, system implementations, speaker sampling, and metric choice bound transfer; persistent difficulty is not automatically a biological property.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Challenges in Automated Processing of Speech from Child Wearables:  The Case of Voice Type Classifier
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Treat data relevance, quantity, label quality, and permission to share as first-class parts of the recognition problem.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Three years of voice-type classification experiments on child-worn recordings compare representation features, architectures, and parameter search against data changes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Child-wearable voice-type classification is evaluated with F-score, identification error rate, and percentage correct using a held-out set under the DARCLE annotation scheme. PyanNet-VTC and Whisper-VTC with frozen Whisper tiny/base/small representations are compared across child, other-child, male-adult, and female-adult classes, with a second human annotator as a performance ceiling. The best Whisper-small mean F-score is 53.6% versus 69.8% for human 2, with OCH remaining the hardest class.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Model and tuning improvements produce marginal gains, while more relevant and larger shareable data produce more progress.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Model and tuning improvements produce marginal gains, while more relevant and larger shareable data produce more progress.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The child-wearable setting, label scheme, permissions, and task definition bound the result; conclusions do not automatically transfer to adult or laboratory speech.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Examining Test-Time Adaptation for Personalized Child Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Apply unsupervised SUTA and SGEM test-time adaptation to off-the-shelf and child-fine-tuned ASR models and compare per-child results.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The adaptation updates model behavior from incoming child speech at inference time, without target transcripts, and is evaluated against unadapted baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) models often experience performance degradation due to data domain shifts introduced at test time, a challenge that is further amplified for child speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports average and per-child gains for both model types, with remaining limitations on non-linguistic child speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports average and per-child gains for both model types, with remaining limitations on non-linguistic child speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Child corpus, adaptation methods, update stability, model family, and evaluation conditions bound transfer; average WER gains are not proof of safe continual deployment.

concept_families.unresolved: Whether this concept remains useful outside the reviewed speakers, languages, devices, rooms, and tasks is unresolved; 5 D3 paper(s) provide full-paper evidence.

concept_families.definition: The same person's voice shifts with fatigue, emotion, health, audience, and speaking effort; robust systems must not confuse state with identity.
concept_families.boundary: There is no universal stable identity vector independent of context.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is The same person's voice shifts with fatigue, emotion, health, audience, and speaking effort; robust systems must not confuse state with identity. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Towards Robust Speaker Recognition against Intrinsic Variation with Foundation Model Few-shot Tuning and Effective Speech Synthesis: Robust speaker recognition tests whether identity survives intrinsic changes in a person's voice instead of being confused with a fixed acoustic profile.; Inter-Speaker Relative Cues for Text-Guided Target Speech Extraction: The official abstract and captured PDF identify a speech object and mechanism that instantiate style-and-state-variation under speaker-characteristics; the PDF now supports full-paper mechanism/evaluation notes, while this remains taxonomy membership rather than independent reproduction.; Robust Vocal Intensity Prediction: Overcoming Dataset Bias with Pretrained Deep Models: The preserved abstract identifies a speech object and bounded intervention that instantiate style-and-state-variation under speaker-characteristics; this upgrades a provisional candidate to analyst-reviewed taxonomy membership only. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: There is no universal stable identity vector independent of context.

records.subtheme_name: Speech as a health or access signal
records.question: How can speech technology help when speaking or hearing itself is impaired or changing?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Voice depends on anatomy, age, health, emotion, language history, social setting, and equipment; these differences affect both communication and measurement. The subtheme asks: How can speech technology help when speaking or hearing itself is impaired or changing?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with clinical speech marker, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Association with a diagnosis is not clinical validity, causation, or permission to make a medical decision.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make clinical speech marker, atypical articulation and dysarthria, augmentative communication explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Continue self-supervised pre-training on pathological speech, use etiology-specific codebooks, and select external examples by semantic similarity.
subtheme_boundary: Association with a diagnosis is not clinical validity, causation, or permission to make a medical decision.
Small datasets and speaker-specific patterns make broad claims especially fragile.
A system should preserve the person's authorship and offer correction, not silently decide what they meant.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Pathology-Aware Speech Encoding and Data Augmentation for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Pathology-aware representations and targeted data address systematic production differences rather than generic noise.; Subtyping Speech Errors in Childhood Speech Sound Disorders with Acoustic-to-Articulatory Speech Inversion: The paper uses acoustic-to-articulatory inversion to distinguish clinically meaningful speech-sound error subtypes.; Acoustic and Linguistic Biomarkers for Cognitive Impairment Detection from Speech: Class-aware acoustic and linguistic ensembles test cognitive-decline signals while exposing clinical data imbalance.; Pitfalls and Limits in Automatic Dementia Assessment: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate clinical-speech-marker within clinical-and-assistive-speech.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Continue self-supervised pre-training on pathological speech, use etiology-specific codebooks, and select external examples by semantic similarity.
Use acoustic-to-articulatory inversion to obtain interpretable movement variables, then test subtype differences with a mixed-effects statistical model across children and target sounds.
Combine acoustic, linguistic, knowledge-based, and neural representations, selecting complementary class-aware systems.
Inspect the automated Syndrom-Kurz-Test pipeline by subgroup, transcription quality, item type, and fallback behavior rather than relying on one aggregate number.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pathology-Aware Speech Encoding and Data Augmentation for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Continue self-supervised pre-training on pathological speech, use etiology-specific codebooks, and select external examples by semantic similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A BEST-RQ Conformer is continued on pathological speech; fine-tuning compares synthetic, out-of-domain, and transcript-embedding-selected data, with similarity losses.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We achieve a 13.2% relative word error rate (WER) improvement using the pathology-aware speech encoder with etiology-specific continued pre-training.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The authors report 13.2% relative WER improvement from pathology-aware pre-training, up to 8.7% from synthetic data, 12.2% from OOD data, and 9.7% from semantic selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The authors report 13.2% relative WER improvement from pathology-aware pre-training, up to 8.7% from synthetic data, 12.2% from OOD data, and 9.7% from semantic selection.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Etiologies, corpora, similarity model, and ratios bound the claim; improvements differ by condition and synthetic speech may not preserve clinical variation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Subtyping Speech Errors in Childhood Speech Sound Disorders with Acoustic-to-Articulatory Speech Inversion
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use acoustic-to-articulatory inversion to obtain interpretable movement variables, then test subtype differences with a mixed-effects statistical model across children and target sounds.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study compares inverted articulatory trajectories for correct and erroneous /r/ and /s/ productions in children with speech sound disorders, models repeated observations with linear mixed effects, and asks which tract variables differ between perceptually defined subtypes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speech inversion holds much potential to describe speech errors in childhood speech sound disorders.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports statistically significant articulatory differences among several perceptually salient /r/ and /s/ error subtypes and correct targets in American English.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports statistically significant articulatory differences among several perceptually salient /r/ and /s/ error subtypes and correct targets in American English.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The study is limited to selected American-English child error types and an inversion model; clinical interpretability is demonstrated for these comparisons, not established for all disorders or speakers. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Acoustic and Linguistic Biomarkers for Cognitive Impairment Detection from Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine acoustic, linguistic, knowledge-based, and neural representations, selecting complementary class-aware systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: PROCESS Challenge systems combine acoustic features, text features, LLM descriptors, Longformer, ECAPA-TDNN, and TRILLsson embeddings across three tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Based on our previous experience on the use of speech and text-derived biomarkers for disease detection, we evaluate here the use of knowledge-based acoustic and text-based feature sets, as well as LLM-based macro-descriptors, and multiple neural representations (e.g., Longformer, ECAPA-TDNN, and Trillsson embeddings).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Selected ensembles provide the strongest reported balance across train/development data and individual classes.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Selected ensembles provide the strongest reported balance across train/development data and individual classes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge data, demographic overlap, and missing metadata limit the claim; this is not clinical validation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pitfalls and Limits in Automatic Dementia Assessment
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Inspect the automated Syndrom-Kurz-Test pipeline by subgroup, transcription quality, item type, and fallback behavior rather than relying on one aggregate number.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The analysis links scoring artifacts to speech production decline, ASR errors, and fallback handling; apparent agreement can therefore arise from the test design.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Current work on speech-based dementia assessment focuses on either feature extraction to predict assessment scales, or on the automation of existing test procedures.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports high overall correlation but weaker behavior for healthy and mildly impaired groups and identifies overoptimistic correlations for severely impaired speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports high overall correlation but weaker behavior for healthy and mildly impaired groups and identifies overoptimistic correlations for severely impaired speakers.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: This is an analysis of one standardized assessment and its data; it warns against clinical claims, not a universal ranking of dementia-screening systems.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Perception of Emotional Speech by Individuals with High Borderline Personality Features
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Present Mandarin emotional speech at controlled intensities and compare emotion-identification accuracy and confusions for participants with high and low borderline-personality features.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies emotional-speech perception in listeners with high borderline personality features.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: High-BPF participants showed lower accuracy in identifying neutral speech, more frequently misidentifying it as other emotions, and were less accurate in identifying high-intensity happy speech, tending to misclassify it as neutral.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: High-feature participants were less accurate for neutral speech and high-intensity happy speech, with distinct confusion patterns and marginally higher confidence for angry speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: High-feature participants were less accurate for neutral speech and high-intensity happy speech, with distinct confusion patterns and marginally higher confidence for angry speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Mandarin synthetic stimuli, university participants, self-report grouping, F0 manipulation, and perceptual task bound generalization; the findings do not diagnose BPD or explain all underlying causes.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Predicting Adolescent Suicidal Risk from Multi-task-based Speech: An Ensemble Learning Approach
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine acoustic and semantic features across several task models, then use a nested voting ensemble to stabilize the prediction.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: OpenSmile and Emotion2Vec supply acoustic representations, a fine-tuned Chinese BERT supplies semantic features, and XGBoost/SVM-style base models are combined after Bayesian hyperparameter search.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper aims to address these limitations by detecting suicide risk from multi-task-based speech, utilizing a dataset of 600 Chinese adolescents (age: 10-18 yr) provided by the 1st SpeechWellness Challenge.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On 600 Chinese adolescents, the paper reports test accuracy .63, recall .74, and F1 about .67.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On 600 Chinese adolescents, the paper reports test accuracy .63, recall .74, and F1 about .67.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: This is a screening model on one challenge dataset, not a diagnosis or safety-tested intervention; age, language, labels, privacy, calibration, and external validation constrain the claim.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Comparative Evaluation of Acoustic Feature Extraction Tools for Clinical Speech Analysis
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Standardize extraction settings, compare tools directly, and test whether disagreements change group classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Three toolkits are applied to 77 schizophrenia-spectrum and 87 control speakers; correlations and classification performance are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The toolkit comparison uses speech from 77 participants with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and 87 healthy controls performing picture-description tasks. OpenSMILE/eGeMAPS, Praat, and Librosa are run with standardized 16-kHz, 60-ms frame settings; feature agreement and extraction robustness are compared across clinical groups and acoustic feature types.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: F0 percentile agreement is high, but F0 variation and formants can disagree or even correlate negatively; F0 mean, HNR, and MFCC1 exceed AUC .70 in the reported classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: F0 percentile agreement is high, but F0 variation and formants can disagree or even correlate negatively; F0 mean, HNR, and MFCC1 exceed AUC .70 in the reported classification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The clinical groups, recordings, parameter choices, and tool versions define the boundary; no clinical diagnosis or deployment safety follows from these correlations.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Test-Time Training for Speech-based Depression Detection
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt the model at test time using the incoming unlabeled speech so its internal features respond to the new distribution.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study applies test-time training to a speech-based depression detector and tests shifts from noise, gender, and dataset/curation differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Previous works on speech-based depression detection typically use datasets collected in similar environments for both training and testing the models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports substantial performance improvement under the tested shifts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports substantial performance improvement under the tested shifts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The task is a clinical screening proxy, not a diagnosis; adaptation stability, labels in deployment, privacy, and external clinical validation remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: ADCeleb: A Longitudinal Speech Dataset from Public Figures for Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a longitudinal celebrity speech corpus, balance AD and control groups across relevant demographics, extract frozen acoustic and linguistic representations, and evaluate them with speaker-disjoint nested cross-validation and fusion.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ADCeleb contains public spontaneous recordings from 40 people with AD and 40 controls, with intervals two and one years before diagnosis. Acoustic embeddings include x-vectors, TRILLsson, Wav2Vec2, HuBERT, and Whisper; linguistic embeddings include multilingual encoders. PCA and PLDA classify speakers, and selected acoustic/linguistic predictions are averaged.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To address these gaps, we introduce ADCeleb, a longitudinal speech dataset comprising publicly available recordings from individuals who later disclosed an AD diagnosis.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The authors report that linguistic representations are stronger earlier, while acoustic information contributes more near the year of diagnosis; fusion improves the nearer interval to 0.80 accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The authors report that linguistic representations are stronger earlier, while acoustic information contributes more near the year of diagnosis; fusion improves the nearer interval to 0.80 accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpus uses public figures, YouTube recordings, 40 AD and 40 control speakers, and imperfect observational labels. It is a dataset and baseline study, not a clinical diagnostic validation; author-reported results were not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: EEG-based Voice Conversion : Hearing the Voice of Your Brain
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align EEG features with speaker voice features and use a speech-trained zero-shot voice-conversion model.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A three-stage training strategy maps EEG to speaker-specific features and conditions a pretrained speech-only converter; Dutch single-word production tests the system.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The connection between Electroencephalography (EEG) signals and human voice has gained significant attention, with studies demonstrating the feasibility of speech synthesis from EEG data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports reliable target-voice conversion on the Single-Word-Production Dutch-iBIDS dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports reliable target-voice conversion on the Single-Word-Production Dutch-iBIDS dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Single words, EEG setup, target voices, and small dataset define the claim; intelligibility, privacy, consent, and real assistive communication remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Silent Speech Decoding System from EEG and EMG with Heterogenous Electrode Configurations
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Handle heterogeneous electrodes and use multitask training for cross-subject and cross-language calibration.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A shared model learns from varying EEG/EMG layouts while multitask objectives stabilize word classification across speakers and languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Silent speech decoding, which performs unvocalized human speech recognition from electroencephalography/electromyography (EEG/EMG), increases accessibility for speech-impaired humans.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Accuracy is 95.3% for healthy participants and 54.5% for a patient, versus 70.1% and 13.2% for single-subject baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Accuracy is 95.3% for healthy participants and 54.5% for a patient, versus 70.1% and 13.2% for single-subject baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Patient count, setup, calibration, and author-reported results limit clinical deployment claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Optimizing Pause Context in Fine-Tuning Pre-trained Large Language Models for Dementia Detection
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Insert between-segment pause context into automatic transcripts and tune the pause-duration representation for each classification task.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Cantonese elderly speech from CU-Marvel is transcribed, pause context is fused into transformer input, and binary dementia tasks are compared under alternative pause groupings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We performed the experiments on our Cantonese elderly corpus called CU-Marvel.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that optimized between-segment pause patterns improve detection and that different tasks prefer different pause representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that optimized between-segment pause patterns improve detection and that different tasks prefer different pause representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The corpus, language, age group, transcription quality, diagnostic labels, and pause definitions bound the result; this is not a validated clinical biomarker or a causal account of dementia.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: EEG-based Speech Decoding Based on Multi-mode Joint Modeling
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train one model across modes with dynamic masking, then use its learned channel relevance to make a smaller single-mode decoder.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A joint EEG decoder covers imagined, intended, and spoken speech and is evaluated on four-vowel classification, including a channel-selection transfer step.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The accuracy improvements and channel selection capability demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed joint modeling framework.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Imagined-speech accuracy rises to 34.95% from a 29.18% baseline, and channel-selected single-mode models outperform models using all channels.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Imagined-speech accuracy rises to 34.95% from a 29.18% baseline, and channel-selected single-mode models outperform models using all channels.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The four-vowel task, participants, EEG hardware, mode definitions, and accuracy metric bound the result; it does not demonstrate unrestricted communication or clinical readiness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Synthetic Dysarthric Speech: A Supplement, Not a Substitute for Authentic Data in Dysarthric Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train speaker-specific TTS systems, generate synthetic dysarthric utterances at several scales, combine them with authentic data for dysarthric speech recognition, and compare feature distributions and recognition results.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study varies whether training uses authentic Set A/Set B data, synthetic data derived from Set A, or much larger synthetic additions. It measures ASR performance and compares acoustic feature distributions between authentic and synthetic samples.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Synthetic dysarthric speech is tested for ASR augmentation using speaker-partitioned authentic and synthetic data in an 8:1:1 train/validation/test split, with two synthetic sets generated per speaker and seven training-set combinations. CER measures dysarthric-speech recognition; acoustic similarity uses F0/duration statistics, RM-C, MFCC cosine similarity, PESQ, and average speaker similarity, with means and t-tests comparing synthetic with authentic speech. The paper explicitly treats synthetic data as supplementary rather than a substitute.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Across the tested Chinese dysarthric speech setup, synthetic speech alone does not replace authentic data and large synthetic additions yield only marginal gains over authentic training.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Across the tested Chinese dysarthric speech setup, synthetic speech alone does not replace authentic data and large synthetic additions yield only marginal gains over authentic training.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The language, seven-speaker usable subset, TTS model, data scale, ASR architecture, and speaker-independent split bound generalization; a synthetic-data result is not clinical validation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Addressing Task Conflicts in Stuttering Detection via MMoE-Based Multi-Task Learning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Analyze task conflicts explicitly, use rules to separate incompatible signals, and let a mixture of experts route examples to task-relevant submodels.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Rule-based multi-task learning and a multi-mixture-of-experts model are evaluated on stuttering-symptom detection and the 2024 SLT challenge.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In the 2024 SLT Stuttering Speech Challenge, the rule-based MTL strategy achieved a 19.9% increase in average F1 score over the baseline, securing first place.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The rule-based strategy reports a 19.9% average-F1 gain over baseline and the MMoE strategy a further 7.55% improvement.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The rule-based strategy reports a 19.9% average-F1 gain over baseline and the MMoE strategy a further 7.55% improvement.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The challenge data, symptom definitions, labels, class balance, and F1 aggregation bound the claim; benchmark gains do not establish clinical reliability or fairness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Fairness in Dysarthric Speech Synthesis: Understanding Intrinsic Bias in Dysarthric Speech Cloning using F5-TTS
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate speech from TORGO prompts with F5-TTS, measure intelligibility, speaker similarity, and prosody similarity, then compare severity groups using parity difference and disparate impact.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study defines metrics over group means: WER/CER for intelligibility, SIM-o cosine similarity for speaker traits, and AutoPCP for prosody. Fairness is assessed by deviations from healthy-speaker reference behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of state-of-the-art F5-TTS in cloning dysarthric speech using TORGO dataset, focusing on intelligibility, speaker similarity, and prosody preservation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports severity-dependent differences in the objective measures and uses those differences to characterize intrinsic bias in F5-TTS cloning.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports severity-dependent differences in the objective measures and uses those differences to characterize intrinsic bias in F5-TTS cloning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: TORGO, reference-prompt choice, automatic metrics, severity grouping, and zero-shot model behavior bound the result; parity in proxies does not establish respectful control, consent, or listener benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Personalized Fine-Tuning with Controllable Synthetic Speech from LLM-Generated Transcripts for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use LLM-generated transcripts to create controllable synthetic speech and personalize fine-tuning for the target speaker, then measure recognition under speaker-specific conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper studies personalized fine-tuning with controllable synthetic speech for dysarthric speech recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Synthetic training data is generated by fine-tuning Parler-TTS to mimic dysarthric speech, using LLM-generated prompts for corpus-consistent target transcripts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports recognition results for personalized adaptation using controllable synthetic data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports recognition results for personalized adaptation using controllable synthetic data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Speaker cohort, dysarthria type, transcript generation, synthesis quality, and adaptation budget limit generalization or clinical claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Semantic Processing During Spoken Word Production by Children with Cochlear Implants
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a picture-word interference task to test whether semantically related distractors slow naming differently for children with implants and hearing peers.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Children with cochlear implants and normal-hearing peers name pictured objects while distractor words vary in semantic relatedness.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Research that investigates the speech production of children with cochlear implants (CIs) mostly focuses on the characteristics of their speech sounds.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Normal-hearing children show the typical semantic interference effect, while the implant group does not, consistent with different semantic organization or greater top-down control.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Normal-hearing children show the typical semantic interference effect, while the implant group does not, consistent with different semantic organization or greater top-down control.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The group, age, implant history, language, task, and interpretation of interference bound the result; absence of an effect is not a direct measurement of neural organization.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Leveraging Ordinal Information for Speech-based Depression Classification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Create ordered thresholds so the model learns several nested decisions and a latent representation that respects severity order.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Speech-based depression scores are converted into K threshold tasks; an ordinal loss trains the model across these linked boundaries.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Ordinal-Dep is evaluated on the DAIC-WOZ depression corpus of 189 interview participants, using the development subset as validation and the held-out test subset for reporting. Utterances are segmented into 3.84-second chunks, subject decisions use majority votes over segments, and macro-F1, positive-class F1, and negative-class F1 compare the proposed ordinal model with state-of-the-art and regression/classification ablations. Each experiment is repeated five times and averaged; PHQ-8 score >=10 defines depression.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The ordinal method outperforms reported state-of-the-art depression-detection methods in the paper's experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The ordinal method outperforms reported state-of-the-art depression-detection methods in the paper's experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The clinical scale, speakers, labels, dataset, threshold choices, and evaluation metrics bound the result; better ordinal prediction is not diagnosis or clinical validation.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

concept_families.boundary: Association with a diagnosis is not clinical validity, causation, or permission to make a medical decision.

It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: Association with a diagnosis is not clinical validity, causation, or permission to make a medical decision.

concept_families.boundary: Small datasets and speaker-specific patterns make broad claims especially fragile.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Pathology-Aware Speech Encoding and Data Augmentation for Dysarthric Speech Recognition: Pathology-aware representations and targeted data address systematic production differences rather than generic noise.; Dysfluent WFST: A Framework for Zero-Shot Speech Dysfluency Transcription and Detection: Zero-shot dysfluency transcription treats repetitions and disruptions as communication events to detect and preserve, not ordinary recognition noise.; Revisiting WFST-based Hybrid Japanese Speech Recognition System for Individuals with Organic Speech Disorders: Organic speech disorders require adaptation that uses scarce patient speech without discarding pronunciation and language structure. records.subtheme_name: Whether the system helps a real person
records.question: What does success mean for the person using or affected by the speech system?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Voice depends on anatomy, age, health, emotion, language history, social setting, and equipment; these differences affect both communication and measurement. The subtheme asks: What does success mean for the person using or affected by the speech system?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with listener effort, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Effort measures depend on task, listener experience, and presentation conditions.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make listener effort, user control and consent, accessibility fit explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Fuse STFT audio features with visual embeddings in a dual-branch CNN-BLSTM attention model and jointly predict PESQ and STOI.
subtheme_boundary: Effort measures depend on task, listener experience, and presentation conditions.
A consent checkbox does not solve power imbalance, downstream copying, or inability to withdraw a trained model.
A lab improvement can be irrelevant or harmful if setup, latency, or interaction burden is omitted.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: A Study on Speech Assessment with Visual Cues: Visual cues are added to non-intrusive speech-quality assessment because a no-reference score must predict what listeners understand without a clean signal.; Can We Trust Machine Learning? The Reliability of Features from Open-Source Speech Analysis Tools for Speech Modeling: Reliability of open-source speech features matters because downstream users may treat a convenient tool as a trustworthy measurement instrument.; EAA: Emotion-Aware Audio Large Language Models with Dual Cross-Attention and Context-Aware Instruction Tuning: The captured official PDF and abstract identify a speech object and mechanism instantiating listener-effort under human-centered-evaluation; this upgrades evidence depth for the structured note and does not establish independent reproduction.; Speech stimulus design to study the neural coding of speech and the impact of cochlear synaptopathy: Controlled speech stimuli test how hearing-related neural limitations affect access to fine temporal speech information.
