d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Study on Speech Assessment with Visual Cues
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Fuse STFT audio features with visual embeddings in a dual-branch CNN-BLSTM attention model and jointly predict PESQ and STOI.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model aligns spectral and visual information before multi-task regression; LCC compares predicted and reference proxy scores under noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluations on the LRS3-TED dataset, augmented with noise from the DEMAND corpus, show that our model outperforms the audio-only baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On LRS3-TED with DEMAND noise, the paper reports higher LCC than audio-only baselines for PESQ and STOI under seen noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On LRS3-TED with DEMAND noise, the paper reports higher LCC than audio-only baselines for PESQ and STOI under seen noise.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Seen-noise conditions, proxy targets, visual availability, dataset, and correlation metric limit transfer; proxy prediction is not a listener study.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Can We Trust Machine Learning? The Reliability of Features from Open-Source Speech Analysis Tools for Speech Modeling
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare tools directly in the target population and test how feature differences alter models and group behavior.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: OpenSMILE and Praat features are evaluated on adolescents with autism from audio-visual recordings, with model performance compared across contexts and demographics.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We evaluate speech features extracted from two widely used speech analysis tools, OpenSMILE and Praat, to assess their reliability when considering adolescents with autism.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports considerable tool variation that influences model performance across context and demographic groups.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports considerable tool variation that influences model performance across context and demographic groups.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The population, features, tools, and behavioral tasks define the boundary; the study does not identify one universally correct toolkit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: EAA: Emotion-Aware Audio Large Language Models with Dual Cross-Attention and Context-Aware Instruction Tuning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use dual cross-attention and context-aware instruction tuning for emotion-aware audio-language modeling.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Cross-attention aligns acoustic and conversational representations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Understanding speech emotion through artificial intelligence (AI) is crucial for human-computer interaction and mental health monitoring.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports EAA results for emotion-aware audio large language modeling.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports EAA results for emotion-aware audio large language modeling.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Labels, prompts, audio quality, model, and human agreement bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speech stimulus design to study the neural coding of speech and the impact of cochlear synaptopathy
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Analyze and resynthesize speech so temporal fine structure and other dimensions can be parametrically varied while preserving naturalistic speech cues.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper designs analysis-resynthesis speech stimuli to test phase-locking/temporal-fine-structure coding and accommodates multi-center studies across species, methods, and languages, including cochlear synaptopathy conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Here, speech stimuli were designed to assess the involvement of a specific coding mechanism: the coding of temporal fine structure through phase-locking.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a design framework for controlled naturalistic stimuli suitable for studying the target coding mechanism and its impairment in cochlear synaptopathy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a design framework for controlled naturalistic stimuli suitable for studying the target coding mechanism and its impairment in cochlear synaptopathy.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Stimulus fidelity, resynthesis artifacts, listener population, language, and study protocol bound the inference; a designed cue isolates a mechanism only insofar as unedited cues remain controlled.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Evaluating Speech Enhancement Performance Across Demographics and Language
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Evaluate enhancement systems on multilingual crowdsourced CommonPhone data with age, gender, language, content-retention, and information-loss analyses.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Quality, intelligibility, word error, and phoneme error measures are compared across demographic and language conditions; samples with high WER are examined for information loss.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speech enhancement models have traditionally relied on VoiceBank-DEMAND for training and evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports performance variation across demographics/languages and warns that model rankings on VoiceBank-DEMAND do not transfer directly.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports performance variation across demographics/languages and warns that model rankings on VoiceBank-DEMAND do not transfer directly.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The authors still note benchmark simplification and possible metric overfitting; dataset diversity does not by itself prove universal fairness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards Inclusive and Fair ASR: Insights from the SAPC Challenge for Optimizing Disordered Speech Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Evaluate strong contextual ASR architectures on a dedicated impaired-speech corpus and inspect whether their different context mechanisms help.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ContextNet and Parakeet are tested on Speech Accessibility Project challenge subsets; WER is compared across the challenge conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our system ranked fourth in terms of Word Error Rate, recording values of 10.06% and 11.8% WER for Test1 and Test2 subsets, respectively, on the challenge leaderboard.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports WER 10.06% and 11.8% on the two test subsets, with Parakeet slightly ahead of ContextNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports WER 10.06% and 11.8% on the two test subsets, with Parakeet slightly ahead of ContextNet.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge data, speaker impairment profiles, transcripts, and WER define the boundary; fairness across disorders, user control, and clinical usefulness remain unestablished.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Can ASR generate valid measures of child reading fluency?
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Extract fifteen measures from ASR transcripts and timings, then compare them with the same measures from human transcripts.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates 244 recordings from 131 Dutch children aged 6–13, compares four ASR systems, and correlates automatic and human-derived fluency measures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We investigate the validity of these measures by comparing them to the same measures computed on human transcripts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The best reported system has WER 12.3% and timing F1 0.82; twelve measures meet r ≥ 0.7.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The best reported system has WER 12.3% and timing F1 0.82; twelve measures meet r ≥ 0.7.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Dutch child reading, fixed texts, age distribution, ASR choice, and transcript comparison limit generalization; intervention or diagnosis validity is not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Hearing deficits of transformer-based ASR for anechoic and spatial signals
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Estimate speech-reception thresholds from controlled sentences in noise for ASR models and humans.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Whisper models are tested on anechoic and spatial signals; thresholds come from WER curves at 50% error.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We compare automatic speech recognition (ASR) with human speech recognition (HSR) based on speech material that is traditionally used for diagnosing hearing deficits.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Model size improves ASR thresholds, but the gap changes with language, room, and spatial signals.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Model size improves ASR thresholds, but the gap changes with language, room, and spatial signals.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Whisper versions, German/English material, steady noise, and laboratory setup limit claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unifying Listener Scoring Scales: Comparison Learning Framework for Speech Quality Assessment and Continuous Speech Emotion Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a unified listener scale from pairwise comparisons so the ordering of utterances is preserved without assuming numeric distances.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The method is evaluated on speech quality assessment and continuous emotion recognition, comparing a unified comparison-based scale with mean-listener and multi-scale approaches.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: UTP is evaluated on BVCC speech-quality assessment and IEMOCAP continuous speech-emotion recognition. BVCC contains 4,973 train, 1,066 development, and 1,066 test utterances with listener scores; IEMOCAP contains 10,039 utterances and 5-fold session-held-out validation. SRCC and LCC measure system-level SQA and utterance-level CSER, with 20 SQA runs and averaged cross-validation results comparing UTMOS/UTP, mean-listener scales, listener embeddings, and comparison scores.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved prediction performance and robustness on both tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved prediction performance and robustness on both tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Listener panels, rating prompts, comparison construction, and datasets bound the result; agreement and usefulness for new listener populations remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Does effortful speech production indicate communication difficulty caused by noise and hearing aid support?
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Record paired conversations across quiet/noise and hearing-aid conditions, collect participants' difficulty judgments, and test which speech and interaction measures predict those judgments.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study pairs 44 normal-hearing and hearing-impaired participants in task-based conversations in quiet and 70 dB noise, with the hearing-impaired group tested with and without hearing aids; F1, vocal level, and turn-taking variability are modeled against questionnaires.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We then analyze how F1, vocal level, and turn taking variability predict communication difficulty.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that higher vocal level and interaction measures predict communication difficulty for hearing-impaired participants under relevant conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that higher vocal level and interaction measures predict communication difficulty for hearing-impaired participants under relevant conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Small dyadic sample, task design, questionnaire, hearing-aid settings, and acoustic noise bound the result; a predictor of reported difficulty is not a universal clinical measure or causal explanation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Crowdsourcing MUSHRA Tests in the Age of Generative Speech Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Subjective and Objective Testing Methods
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Adapt MUSHRA for non-experts online, compare platforms with expert data, and test whether objective metrics agree with people.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper compares MTurk, Prolific, and expert ratings, measures test-retest reliability, and evaluates six objective metrics on generative speech codecs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: As a result, objective metrics are often used during development, with expert evaluations conducted later.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports platform-specific bias, reasonable crowdsourced comparisons under its protocol, and that traditional metrics undervalue generative models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports platform-specific bias, reasonable crowdsourced comparisons under its protocol, and that traditional metrics undervalue generative models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is bounded to the codecs, platforms, listener recruitment, and six metrics tested; other populations and model families remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Web-Based Application for Real-Time Biofeedback of Vocal Resonance in Gender-Affirming Voice Training: Design and Usability Evaluation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a browser tool that gives real-time vocal-resonance biofeedback and evaluate whether intended users can complete tasks and understand the feedback.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study combines real-time acoustic analysis, visual feedback, and a usability evaluation for gender-affirming voice training.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper describes the development and testing of software to address one of the most challenging aspects of GAVT: modifying vocal tract resonance.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a working web application and usability findings supporting its use as a training aid.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a working web application and usability findings supporting its use as a training aid.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Small usability sample, task design, browser/audio conditions, and self-report limit claims about long-term learning or clinical outcomes.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Accessible Delivery of Visual-Acoustic Biofeedback for Speech Sound Disorder
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Make the source-filter structure visible: display a real-time LPC spectrum alongside a target resonance, with adaptive practice and clinician-mediated feedback.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: JavaScript computes LPC coefficients with Levinson-Durbin recursion, renders the spectral envelope and peaks, and supports randomized word/syllable routines, clinician scoring, gamification, and local-device WebRTC processing.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: staRt is evaluated as an accessible visual-acoustic biofeedback application for /r/ speech training rather than through a held-out recognition benchmark. The reported evidence is the real-time LPC-spectrum implementation, target-formant slider, clinician scoring/adaptive exercises, iOS/web deployment, and WebRTC telepractice workflow. Peak-picking and formant tracking are explicitly not yet stable enough for automated correctness feedback, so clinical efficacy and generalization remain open evaluation questions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The staRt iOS/web system provides real-time visual-acoustic biofeedback for /r/ training and reports broad uptake; local processing avoids telepractice loss of frequency resolution and latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The staRt iOS/web system provides real-time visual-acoustic biofeedback for /r/ training and reports broad uptake; local processing avoids telepractice loss of frequency resolution and latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The current target is mainly English /r/, peak-picking and formant tracking are not yet stable enough for automated feedback across vocal-tract sizes, and clinical efficacy is not established by this technical description.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Concurrent Speech and Auditory Tag Clouds for Non-Visual Web Interaction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent document semantics as an interactive auditory tag cloud, using concurrent speech and spatial/continuous auditory guidance to let the listener scan and select structure.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: TagThunder extracts morpho-dispositional semantics and maps tags to concurrent speech streams and guiding stimuli; discrete and continuous interaction conditions test structured information scanning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: TagThunder is presented as an experimental framework and browser add-on for concurrent spatialized speech tag clouds and skimming/scanning strategies. Evaluation evidence is the implemented processing pipeline—web-zone segmentation, YAKE keyword extraction, Kokoro synthesis, Web Audio 3D spatialization, and four navigation strategies—plus the downloadable add-on. The paper explicitly states that the framework lacks full accessibility features for end users and reports no participant study, task accuracy, latency benchmark, or listener denominator.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper presents the experimental framework and reports feasibility for non-visual web skimming through auditory tag-cloud interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper presents the experimental framework and reports feasibility for non-visual web skimming through auditory tag-cloud interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The evaluation is interaction-specific, auditory clutter and learning effects matter, and accessibility promise is not equivalent to demonstrated performance across blind users, browsers, languages, or real browsing tasks.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: What Do Humans Hear When Interacting? Experiments on Selective Listening for Evaluating ASR of Spoken Dialogue Systems
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Observe selective listening in 297 human participants, estimate part-of-speech importance, and use those weights to form Human-WWER/H-WCER for dialogue-oriented ASR evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Participants generate a response and then recall/transcribe the speech; multiple regression estimates POS weights, which are inserted into the edit-distance costs used by weighted WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Examining selective listening of humans, which refers to the ability to focus on and listen to important parts of a conversation during the speech, will enable us to identify the ASR capabilities required for SDSs and evaluate them.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Humans attend more to content words than function words; the proposed H-WWER gives lower scores to human than Whisper transcriptions in the reported comparison and is offered as a dialogue-relevant complement to WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Humans attend more to content words than function words; the proposed H-WWER gives lower scores to human than Whisper transcriptions in the reported comparison and is offered as a dialogue-relevant complement to WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Transcription follows response generation rather than occurring simultaneously, and the displayed weight comparison is partly optimized on test data. The metric is a proposal, not validated against downstream response success or diverse dialogue settings.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Processing of grammatical information in cochlear implant simulated speech by German adult listeners
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare normal and CI-simulated speech with eye-tracking, accuracy, and working-memory measures so evaluation reflects both the answer and the listener's processing path.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: German adults answer subject, object, and passive which-questions. Eye movements and response accuracy expose whether case and subject-verb agreement cues survive the simulation; mixed-effects analyses relate performance to working memory.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Using eye-tracking, accuracy and gaze patterns for subject, object and passive questions were studied.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Only object-question accuracy was affected by the simulation, with weaker interpretation preferences in gaze patterns; higher working memory was associated with better accuracy and faster reorientation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Only object-question accuracy was affected by the simulation, with weaker interpretation preferences in gaze patterns; higher working memory was associated with better accuracy and faster reorientation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The simulation is not an actual implant, the German grammatical system and question types are narrow, and listener behavior does not establish clinical device benefit or general speech recognition performance.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Individualize enhancement around the listener's hearing profile and evaluate the resulting speech access.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Listener-specific constraints become the target of enhancement rather than the average waveform.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Individualized speech enhancement is evaluated using simulated hearing profiles and a one-hour DNS-Challenge-derived test set at 0-dB SNR and 70-dB SPL. HASPI and HASQI assess intelligibility and quality for hearing-aided listeners; NRMSE and SRMR assess cochlear-synaptopathy-related enhancement behavior. Noise training uses AudioSet and Freesound test noise, while the paper reports no listener validation yet and identifies a future listening test.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Hearing profiles, listener numbers, fitting procedure, materials, and subjective protocol bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Bayesian Approach to L2 Fluency Ratings by Native and Nonnative Listeners
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a Bayesian hierarchical model to separate listener variability from utterance-level fluency cues and compare syllable- versus segment-based articulation rate.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Posterior distributions represent listener-specific leniency and cue weights; speed, breakdown, and repair features explain ratings while uncertainty remains explicit.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This study investigates how native and nonnative listeners evaluate the fluency of Japanese speakers' English using a Bayesian modeling framework.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Using 16 listeners and 180 Japanese speakers in J-AESOP, the paper reports greater leniency among some nonnative listeners and stronger fit for segment-based articulation rate.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Using 16 listeners and 180 Japanese speakers in J-AESOP, the paper reports greater leniency among some nonnative listeners and stronger fit for segment-based articulation rate.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Listener sample, language backgrounds, trained-rating task, corpus, feature definitions, and Bayesian priors bound transfer; fluency ratings are not a complete measure of communicative success.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Feature Importance across Domains for Improving Non-Intrusive Speech Intelligibility Prediction in Hearing Aids
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Estimate frame-level importance across spectral, temporal, and Whisper latent features, project each domain through those weights, and fuse them in an assessment model.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: FiDo produces domain-specific weighted representations before concatenation and regression; RMSE on intelligibility targets evaluates whether the weighting preserves listener-relevant evidence.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experimental results show that when FiDo is incorporated into the improved multi-branched speech intelligibility model MBI-Net+, RMSE can be reduced by 7.62% (from 26.10 to 24.11).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that FiDo reduces MBI-Net+ RMSE from 26.10 to 24.11 and improves over the best 2023 Clarity Prediction Challenge system.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that FiDo reduces MBI-Net+ RMSE from 26.10 to 24.11 and improves over the best 2023 Clarity Prediction Challenge system.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Weakly supervised targets, hearing-aid/noise conditions, challenge split, proxy RMSE, and absence of a new listener study bound the claim; prediction is not equivalent to real-world access improvement.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The Reliability of Features from Open-Source Speech Analysis Tools for Speech Modeling addresses it by OpenSMILE and Praat features are evaluated on adolescents with autism from audio-visual recordings, with model performance compared across contexts and demographics.. The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.

records.subtheme_name: Sharing structure across languages
records.question: What can be shared, and what must remain language-specific?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Languages differ in sounds, writing systems, grammar, prosody, code-switching, and social meaning; data and tools are distributed unevenly. The subtheme asks: What can be shared, and what must remain language-specific?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with cross-lingual transfer, but that shortcut misses the boundary: Transfer may favor high-resource languages and erase distinctions absent from the source language.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make cross-lingual transfer, language and variety identification, code-switching explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Build a culturally aligned multilingual spoken QA dataset and evaluate the ASR-plus-LLM chain on naturally spoken questions and answers.
subtheme_boundary: Transfer may favor high-resource languages and erase distinctions absent from the source language.
Closely related varieties and code-switching make a single label inadequate or politically loaded.
A monolingual metric can count appropriate switching as error and fail to define the intended transcript.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: SpokenNativQA: Multilingual Everyday Spoken Queries for LLMs: Everyday multilingual spoken queries test whether a language model handles language choice and meaning together instead of translating an artificial sentence list.; TalTech Systems for the Interspeech 2025 ML-SUPERB 2.0 Challenge: Language identification and specialized multilingual decoding allocate recognition capacity across languages.; A Study of Speech Embedding Similarities Between Australian Aboriginal and High-Resource Languages: The paper studies whether learned speech geometry relates Australian Aboriginal languages to high-resource languages, while testing the limits of interpreting similarity as transfer.; From Context to Code-switching: Examining the Interplay of Language Proficiency and Multilingualism in Speech: The study connects code-switching behavior to language background and proficiency, showing why multilingual speech cannot be interpreted without speaker and language context.

Use hybrid language identification, multilingual and language-specific models, and targeted decoding resources.
Compare speech embeddings across Aboriginal and high-resource languages and inspect what kinds of similarity and transfer the representation actually supports.
Model code-switching quantity, dominant language, and switching strategy together with speaker background variables such as parental language, schooling language, and self-reported ability.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SpokenNativQA: Multilingual Everyday Spoken Queries for LLMs
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a culturally aligned multilingual spoken QA dataset and evaluate the ASR-plus-LLM chain on naturally spoken questions and answers.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SpokenNativQA contains about 33,000 spoken questions and answers across multilingual, low-resource, and dialect-rich settings; ASR systems and LLMs are benchmarked on the resulting task.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: However, benchmarking their capabilities with multilingual spoken queries remains largely unexplored.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper introduces the dataset, releases data and scripts, and reports comparative ASR and LLM results for spoken QA.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper introduces the dataset, releases data and scripts, and reports comparative ASR and LLM results for spoken QA.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Language coverage, annotation, question domains, ASR errors, and answer scoring bound the result; a benchmark does not establish equal usefulness across all represented communities.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: TalTech Systems for the Interspeech 2025 ML-SUPERB 2.0 Challenge
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use hybrid language identification, multilingual and language-specific models, and targeted decoding resources.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The system combines language identification with multilingual ASR and customized models, then evaluates language ID and CER.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The ML-SUPERB 2.0 development and dialect-development sets evaluate language-identification accuracy and character error rate across the challenge languages, dialects, and accents. Uniform interpolation of the embedding and generative LID models is compared with each component; the reported reductions are 31% on the regular development set and 23% on the dialectal set.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The system is competitive with challenge baselines and identifies languages needing targeted work.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The system is competitive with challenge baselines and identifies languages needing targeted work.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge data, language mix, averaging, and tuning limit all-multilingual claims.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: A Study of Speech Embedding Similarities Between Australian Aboriginal and High-Resource Languages
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare speech embeddings across Aboriginal and high-resource languages and inspect what kinds of similarity and transfer the representation actually supports.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Audio from multiple languages is passed through a speech encoder; distances or similarity distributions are compared across language pairs and conditions, with downstream implications analyzed.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our results reveal that aboriginal languages are most frequently identified as Māori, suggesting phonetic or structural similarities, while showing significant differences from globally dominant languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports comparative embedding similarities involving Australian Aboriginal and high-resource languages and discusses implications for underrepresented-language technology.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports comparative embedding similarities involving Australian Aboriginal and high-resource languages and discusses implications for underrepresented-language technology.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Similarity is not a language description or a guarantee of recognition transfer; data quantity, speaker coverage, and community context limit interpretation. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: From Context to Code-switching: Examining the Interplay of Language Proficiency and Multilingualism in Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Model code-switching quantity, dominant language, and switching strategy together with speaker background variables such as parental language, schooling language, and self-reported ability.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study analyzes spontaneous Spanish-English speech in the Bangor Miami corpus, defines insertional and alternational switching outcomes, compares speaker language profiles, and fits regression models to quantity, language distribution, and strategy. It separates associations that are statistically reliable from those that only approach significance.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To answer this question, we examine the Bangor Miami corpus of spontaneous Spanish-English speech and analyze the linguistic and demographic profiles of its speakers alongside features of their conversational language production.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that parents’ primary language, secondary-school language, and self-reported higher-ability language are associated with code-switching quantity and dominant-language use, while several direct proficiency relationships are weak or inconclusive.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that parents’ primary language, secondary-school language, and self-reported higher-ability language are associated with code-switching quantity and dominant-language use, while several direct proficiency relationships are weak or inconclusive.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The analysis is observational, focused on Spanish-English Bangor Miami speakers and available self-reports; background variables may be correlated and do not establish why a speaker switched. Findings do not generalize automatically to other language pairs, communities, or tasks; no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Adapting Whisper for low-resource Hindi-English Code-Mix speech with on-the-fly Augmentation & LLM-Synthesised Data
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine language-specific prompts, on-the-fly code-mixed augmentation, and LLM-generated text followed by audio synthesis.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Synthetic switches and language prompts expose the recognizer to transition patterns; MER and code-switch bigram accuracy evaluate transcription.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on a Hindi-English CS dataset show promising results, demonstrating the techniques effectiveness.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 31% relative improvement over pretrained Whisper without real in-domain data for fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 31% relative improvement over pretrained Whisper without real in-domain data for fine-tuning.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The experiments focus on Hindi-English tutorial speech and Whisper large-v2; transfer to other language pairs is proposed, not established.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Teacher-Free Knowledge Distillation for Improving Short-Utterance Spoken Language Identification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use online soft labels from correctly classified training segments, with dynamic weighting, conditional updates, and entropy-based uncertainty, without a separate teacher.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes teacher-free knowledge distillation for short-utterance spoken language identification.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Spoken language identification (LID) systems exhibit performance degradations as the test input duration reduces.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports consistent Cavg improvements in same-corpus and cross-corpus short-utterance evaluations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports consistent Cavg improvements in same-corpus and cross-corpus short-utterance evaluations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, out-of-scope composition, duration, label updates, and corpora bound the result; better short-segment ID does not solve open-set detection generally.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: ADI-20: Arabic Dialect Identification dataset and models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Release broad data and compare pretrained encoders, data-size reduction, and model capacity directly.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ADI-20 contains 3,556 hours across 19 dialects plus MSA; ECAPA-TDNN and Whisper encoder systems are evaluated.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present ADI-20, an extension of the previously published ADI-17 Arabic Dialect Identification (ADI) dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Using 30% of the original data causes only a small F1 decrease in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Using 30% of the original data causes only a small F1 decrease in the reported experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The country/dialect inventory, labels, and data collection define the boundary; conversational code-switching and unrepresented varieties remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Speech-to-Text Translation with Phoneme-Augmented CoT: Enhancing Cross-Lingual Transfer in Low-Resource Scenarios
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Insert phoneme recognition and phoneme-aware chain-of-thought steps, then gradually shift training from text support toward speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: A multilingual LLM processes speech and phonemes under a curriculum; multilingual benchmarks compare low-, zero-, and high-resource settings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on multilingual S2TT benchmarks show that phoneme-augmented CoT improves translation quality in low-resource conditions and enables zero-resource translation, while slightly impacting high-resource performance.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved low-resource translation and zero-resource operation, with a small high-resource tradeoff.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved low-resource translation and zero-resource operation, with a small high-resource tradeoff.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, phoneme recognizer, curriculum, and benchmark define the boundary; zero-resource claims depend on what other language information is available.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Self-Supervised Models of Speech Processing for Haitian Creole
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Pretrain monolingual self-supervised models for Haitian Creole, compare them with multilingual and French-based models, and fine-tune all for ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper develops self-supervised speech-processing models for Haitian Creole and compares monolingual, multilingual, and French-derived initialization.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We compare the performance of these models with models finetuned from larger multilingual (XLSR-53, XLSR2-300m, MMS-1B) and monolingual French-based models (LeBenchmark 1 to 7K).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports monolingual models that are competitive with or surpass larger multilingual alternatives on the tested ASR tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports monolingual models that are competitive with or surpass larger multilingual alternatives on the tested ASR tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Data volume, speakers, orthography, model size, pretraining compute, and evaluation domain limit generalization to the broader Creole speech community.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: NIRANTAR: Continual Learning with New Languages and Domains on Real-world Speech Data
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Measure language-incremental, domain-incremental, and joint language-plus-domain learning on naturally arriving speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: NIRANTAR contains 3,250 hours from 22 languages and 208 Indian districts, with non-uniform episodes and human transcripts; existing continual-learning methods are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We introduce Nirantar, a comprehensive framework for evaluating continual learning (CL) in multilingual and multi-domain ASR.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper finds that no single evaluated method performs consistently across the three scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper finds that no single evaluated method performs consistently across the three scenarios.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: This is a benchmark and comparative study, not proof that one method is universally best; the geography, languages, episode order, and ASR models define the boundary.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Extending the Fongbe to French Speech Translation Corpus:  resources, models and benchmark
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Extend the Fongbe-French speech-translation corpus, document resources and splits, and establish models and baselines for the direction.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper extends the Fongbe-to-French speech translation corpus and presents resources, models, and a benchmark.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper introduces FFSTC 2, an expanded version of the existing Fongbe-to-French speech translation corpus, addressing the critical need for resources in African dialects for speech recognition and translation tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports corpus additions, baseline models, and benchmark results for Fongbe-to-French speech translation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports corpus additions, baseline models, and benchmark results for Fongbe-to-French speech translation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Corpus size, speakers, alignment, transcription, translation references, and split design bound generalization to Fongbe communities and other low-resource pairs.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: ArticulateX: End-to-End Monolingual Speech Translation in Articulator Space
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build an end-to-end monolingual speech-translation system that represents speech in articulator space and tests whether the intermediate structure helps.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: ArticulateX is an end-to-end monolingual speech translation system operating in articulator space.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model in fr-en and de-en speech-to-speech translation on the CVSS dataset, achieving BLEU scores better or comparable to existing models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports speech-translation results for the articulator-space system in its tested monolingual setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports speech-translation results for the articulator-space system in its tested monolingual setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Language, corpus, articulatory estimation, model, references, and evaluation bound generalization; an intermediate representation is not proof of human-like translation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Novel Parasitic Dual-Scale Modeling for Efficient and Accurate Multilingual Speech Translation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a parasitic dual-scale design that shares efficient global structure while preserving language-specific detail for multilingual speech translation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes novel parasitic dual-scale modeling for efficient and accurate multilingual speech translation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: WhisperM2M is evaluated for many-to-many speech translation across six languages using CoVoST2 and Fleurs test sets. Case-sensitive sacreBLEU is averaged over specified X-EN, EN-X, and X-X language directions, comparing Whisper small/medium, SeamlessM4T medium, and SeamlessM4T large v2; decoder efficiency uses average latency per token on 1,000 CoVoST2 utterances over 10 runs on one H800. Training uses approximately 100k hours with cloud-generated pseudo-translation labels.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports multilingual translation accuracy and efficiency improvements for the tested language set.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports multilingual translation accuracy and efficiency improvements for the tested language set.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, directions, data imbalance, parameter budget, decoding, and metrics bound the result; efficiency on a benchmark is not equal quality for every language.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Efficient Multilingual ASR Finetuning via LoRA Language Experts
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use language-specific LoRA experts so a shared base retains common speech structure while small expert updates handle language-specific differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes efficient multilingual ASR fine-tuning via LoRA language experts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly enhanced multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) due to the development of advanced model architectures and available large-scale multilingual datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports multilingual ASR accuracy and efficiency results for LoRA language experts.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports multilingual ASR accuracy and efficiency results for LoRA language experts.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, data balance, rank, routing, base model, and evaluation domains bound the claim; parameter efficiency does not guarantee fairness across languages.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: LIST: Language-Independent Speech Token for Multilingual Speech Synthesis with Language Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a language-independent speech token and use it with language-model synthesis across multiple languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: LIST is a language-independent speech token for multilingual speech synthesis with language models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Recently, language model (LM)-based speech synthesis models have shown remarkable naturalness and powerful zero-shot capabilities.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports multilingual synthesis quality and cross-language token behavior for LIST.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports multilingual synthesis quality and cross-language token behavior for LIST.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, token rate, codebook, speakers, conditioning, and evaluation metrics bound the claim; shared tokens do not guarantee equal quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SawtArabi: A Benchmark Corpus for Arabic TTS.  Standard, Dialectal and Code-Switching
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build a benchmark corpus covering standard, dialectal, and code-switched Arabic TTS with documented speakers, text, and evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SawtArabi is a benchmark corpus for Arabic TTS spanning standard, dialectal, and code-switching speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Curating Text-to-Speech (TTS) datasets is a strenuous task given the quality considerations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports corpus resources and baseline TTS evaluations across the covered Arabic conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports corpus resources and baseline TTS evaluations across the covered Arabic conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Variety coverage, speaker balance, text design, switching labels, and listening tests bound generalization across Arabic communities.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Can we train ASR systems on Code-switch without real code-switch data? Case study for Singapore's languages
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate phrase-level synthetic code-switching data from monolingual augmented speech, then use it to adapt large pretrained ASR models and evaluate several Southeast Asian language pairs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper creates phrase-mixed speech for Malay-English, Mandarin-Malay, and Tamil-English, fine-tunes Whisper, MMS, and SeamlessM4T, and compares monolingual and code-switched test performance against training without real code-switch recordings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper focuses on three under-resourced Southeast Asian language pairs: Malay-English (BM-EN), Mandarin-Malay (ZH-BM), and Tamil-English (TA-EN), establishing a new comprehensive benchmark for CS-ASR to evaluate the performance of leading ASR models.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The authors report improved ASR on monolingual and code-switched tests, with the largest gains for BM-EN followed by TA-EN and ZH-BM.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The authors report improved ASR on monolingual and code-switched tests, with the largest gains for BM-EN followed by TA-EN and ZH-BM.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Synthetic phrase mixing is an approximation to spontaneous switching, and the three language pairs do not represent all multilingual communities. WER does not measure whether switches are socially or linguistically natural, and no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Simultaneous Speech Translation Integrated Compact Multiple Sound Spot Synthesis System On A Laptop Carried Out With A Backpack
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Integrate simultaneous speech translation with compact multiple-sound-spot synthesis in a portable system and evaluate the complete interaction loop.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper presents a simultaneous speech-translation system integrated with compact multiple sound-spot synthesis on a laptop carried in a backpack.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The portable multiple-sound-spot system is evaluated as a Show & Tell demonstration rather than a held-out acoustic or translation benchmark. The demonstrated configurations are eight-language synthesis, eight simultaneous English-content zones, and four-language synthesis combined with Japanese-to-English/Chinese/Korean simultaneous speech-to-speech translation, running on a backpack-carried 16-loudspeaker array, on-premise laptop, wireless microphone, and compact amplifier. The paper reports implementation dimensions and portability but no participant, localization-error, latency, intelligibility, or translation-accuracy denominator.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports an integrated portable-system demonstration and evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports an integrated portable-system demonstration and evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Language pair, overlap conditions, hardware, latency measurement, and user setting limit generalization to broad simultaneous conversation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: CS-FLEURS: A Massively Multilingual and Code-Switched Speech Dataset
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build CS-FLEURS across 52 languages and 113 pairs, compare real and synthetic controls, and add synthetic code-switched training data.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The corpus controls pair and switching conditions; experiments compare CER, direct translation, script pairs, and augmented training.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We present CS-FLEURS, a new dataset for developing and evaluating code-switched speech recognition and translation systems beyond high-resourced languages.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Code-switched ASR is over twice as errorful as monolingual speech, while synthetic training improves seen and unseen pairs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Code-switched ASR is over twice as errorful as monolingual speech, while synthetic training improves seen and unseen pairs.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Language pairs, synthetic voices, Whisper, CER, and controlled read speech limit natural-conversation claims.
