d3_comparison_matrix.title: Optimizing CLAP Reward with LLM Feedback for Semantically Aligned and Diverse Automated Audio Captioning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine CLAP similarity with repetition penalties, clipping, and LLM feedback during reward optimization.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: CRRP trains an automated audio-captioning system with a stabilized CLAP reward and an LLM evaluator; semantic, human, and AI assessments are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: To address this, reinforcement learning (RL) techniques have been adopted to directly optimize evaluation metrics, but these methods often suffer from word repetition and contextual distortion.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports strong semantic and human/AI evaluation results for the proposed reward system.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports strong semantic and human/AI evaluation results for the proposed reward system.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result depends on caption datasets, evaluator prompts, and reward weighting; human agreement and out-of-domain audio remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SMARTMOS: Modeling Subjective Audio Quality Evaluation for Real-Time Applications
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a model of subjective quality from listening-test ratings and design it for fast prediction in the intended real-time setting.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Audio examples and human scores are used to train a predictor; its estimates are compared with held-out subjective ratings across conditions and computational constraints.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluating audio quality is a crucial task, with subjective listening tests being the gold standard.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a real-time subjective-quality model intended to approximate listening-test judgments more cheaply and quickly.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a real-time subjective-quality model intended to approximate listening-test judgments more cheaply and quickly.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Human ratings, test conditions, and audio distortions define the target; a predictor can reproduce annotator bias and fail on unseen codecs or populations. No independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Intelligibility Prediction for Time-Modified Speech Signals Using Spectro-Temporal Modulation Features
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Align clean and time-modified speech with selected spectro-temporal modulation features, then feed the alignment into existing reference-based intelligibility predictors.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The system uses DTW over modulation features and compares two ways of incorporating the alignment into RB-SIPAs across noise and time-modification conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Using these methods, we compare the output scores of the RB-SIPA with listening test scores and show better correlation results using the STM features as compared to MFCCs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports better alignment behavior and better correlation with listening scores than MFCC-based alternatives under its tested conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports better alignment behavior and better correlation with listening scores than MFCC-based alternatives under its tested conditions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The listening datasets, degradation types, chosen modulation channels, and reference availability bound the claim; correlation is not a complete model of listener experience.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Benchmarking and Confidence Evaluation of LALMs For Temporal Reasoning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Build the TREA temporal-reasoning dataset, benchmark audio language models against people, and measure uncertainty through invariance to semantically identical perturbations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper introduces Temporal Reasoning Evaluation of Audio and an uncertainty metric for large audio language models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this quest, large audio language models (LALMs) have to be evaluated on reasoning related tasks which are different from traditional classification or generation tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that tested open-source models lagged human performance and that accuracy and perturbation-based uncertainty were not necessarily correlated.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that tested open-source models lagged human performance and that accuracy and perturbation-based uncertainty were not necessarily correlated.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The dataset, perturbations, models, human comparison, and temporal tasks bound conclusions; invariance is one operational uncertainty test, not a complete account of confidence.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Benchmarking Time-localized Explanations for Audio Classification Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Create time annotations for target events as a proxy reference and benchmark model-agnostic post-hoc explanations against them.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The benchmark compares temporal explanation methods for audio classifiers and uses the annotations to expose spurious correlations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Most modern approaches for audio processing are opaque, in the sense that they do not provide an explanation for their decisions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports near-perfect explanations for some methods and shows their use in finding spurious correlations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports near-perfect explanations for some methods and shows their use in finding spurious correlations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Event annotations, task type, explanation method, and proxy definition bound the claim; faithfulness under distribution shift remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Exploring Linear Variant Transformers and k-NN Memory Inference for Long-Form ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Compare linear-time sequence architectures and add a non-trained nearest-neighbor memory that retrieves useful earlier representations during inference.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Fastformer, SummaryMixing, BiMamba, and E-Branchformer variants are evaluated on a new LibriHeavy long-form benchmark; KNN-MAN is added to encoder-decoder models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Additionally, we propose a new challenging LF benchmark derived from the LibriHeavy corpus, featuring development and test sets with varying average durations to enable comprehensive evaluation across different temporal scales.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a reduction from 18.8% to 17.5% WER on its LibriSpeech long-form test-clean example with BiMamba and KNN-MAN.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a reduction from 18.8% to 17.5% WER on its LibriSpeech long-form test-clean example with BiMamba and KNN-MAN.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Benchmark construction, duration distribution, memory retrieval, architectures, and WER bound the result; a single long-form corpus does not establish general conversation robustness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Spectrotemporal Modulation: Efficient and Interpretable Feature Representation for Classifying Speech, Music, and Environmental Sounds
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Represent sound with spectrotemporal modulation patterns motivated by auditory processing, then compare a compact unpretrained classifier with pretrained audio networks.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: STM features are used for naturalistic speech, music, and environmental sound classification without pretraining.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Audio DNNs have demonstrated impressive performance on various machine listening tasks; however, most of their representations are computationally costly and uninterpretable, leaving room for optimization.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The STM-based model reaches performance comparable to pretrained audio DNNs across the tested categories while remaining interpretable and efficient.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The STM-based model reaches performance comparable to pretrained audio DNNs across the tested categories while remaining interpretable and efficient.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Tasks, datasets, modulation parameters, baselines, and definition of interpretability bound the claim; comparable accuracy does not prove a match to human auditory cortex.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Towards LLM-Empowered Fine-Grained Speech Descriptors for Explainable Emotion Recognition
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Disentangle speech-emotion descriptors from HuBERT features with alternating LLM fine-tuning, ASR and descriptor tasks, and an information-bottleneck VAE.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes LLM-empowered fine-grained descriptors for explainable speech emotion recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper presents a novel end-to-end LLM-empowered explainable speech emotion recognition (SER) approach.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On IEMOCAP and MELD, the paper reports up to 4.0 and 3.7 absolute UAR gains over the relevant baselines and presents descriptors as explanations.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On IEMOCAP and MELD, the paper reports up to 4.0 and 3.7 absolute UAR gains over the relevant baselines and presents descriptors as explanations.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, descriptor definitions, LLM/SSL choices, bottleneck size, and benchmark labels bound the interpretation; a predicted descriptor is not automatically a human-valid cause.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Temp4Cap: Temporally-aligned Automated Audio Captioning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train temporal alignment directly with contrastive learning, using language-model temporal captions and event/order shuffling plus substitutions as negatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Temp4Cap is a temporally aligned automated audio-captioning framework.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Temp4Cap is trained and evaluated on Clotho (5k 15–30-second clips) and AudioCaps (about 50k clips); validation/test clips have five reference captions. BLEU4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, METEOR, SPIDEr, temporal accuracy, and temporal F1 are compared with CNN-encoder baselines, with MOS reported with 95% confidence intervals.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On Clotho and AudioCaps, the paper reports gains in captioning metrics and temporal metrics over the compared systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On Clotho and AudioCaps, the paper reports gains in captioning metrics and temporal metrics over the compared systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, generated temporal captions, negative-sampling design, caption metrics, and temporal scoring bound the claim; metric gains do not ensure every relation is correctly grounded.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Audio Captioning with Generation-Assisted Multimodal Querying and Progressive Learning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate a caption for the query audio, retrieve with a weighted combination of audio-to-audio and text-to-text similarity, and progressively train the model with interleaved audio-text examples.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MQ-Cap trains a connector and LoRA parameters with a cross-entropy loss over interleaved pairs. It first retrieves 25 candidates by audio similarity, then combines normalized Laion-CLAP audio and text similarities with alpha 0.5. WavCaps, AudioCaps, and Clotho provide training and knowledge-base data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our experiments on AudioCaps, Clotho, and Auto-ACD demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art results across these benchmarks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Progressive learning plus generation-assisted querying improves the reported captioning scores and gives up to 3.1 percentage points of retrieval improvement; the method adds about 1.07 seconds of generation overhead to retrieval.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Progressive learning plus generation-assisted querying improves the reported captioning scores and gives up to 3.1 percentage points of retrieval improvement; the method adds about 1.07 seconds of generation overhead to retrieval.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The benchmarks are AudioCaps, Clotho, and Auto-ACD with overlapping-source controls and missing test audio; retrieval quality depends on the generated caption and CLAP encoders. Results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multivariate Probabilistic Assessment of Speech Quality
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Model MOS and four diagnostic quality dimensions jointly as a multivariate probability distribution.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The model predicts a multivariate Gaussian through Cholesky factors and extends probabilistic affine transformations on NISQA ratings.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The mean opinion score (MOS) is a standard metric for assessing speech quality, but its singular focus fails to identify specific distortions when low scores are observed.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports state-of-the-art-level point estimation while uniquely providing uncertainty and cross-dimension correlation estimates.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports state-of-the-art-level point estimation while uniquely providing uncertainty and cross-dimension correlation estimates.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is bounded to NISQA's labels and distributional assumptions; whether listeners and engineers benefit in new codecs or languages remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Non-intrusive Speech Quality Assessment with Diffusion Models Trained on Clean Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train an unconditional diffusion model only on clean speech and use the likelihood of a deterministically noised input as an unsupervised quality score.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper uses diffusion-model density estimation for non-intrusive speech-quality assessment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Our proposed log-likelihoods show promising results, correlating well with intrusive speech quality metrics and showing the best correlation with human scores in a listening experiment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The proposed log-likelihood correlates with intrusive metrics and showed the strongest correlation with human scores in the reported listening experiment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The proposed log-likelihood correlates with intrusive metrics and showed the strongest correlation with human scores in the reported listening experiment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Clean-speech corpus, diffusion schedule, likelihood proxy, reference metrics, listeners, and distortion types bound the claim; low likelihood can mean unfamiliarity rather than poor quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Beyond Similarity Scoring: Detecting Entailment and Contradiction in Multilingual and Multimodal Contexts
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Classify the logical relation between speech and text or between two speech segments as entailment, contradiction, or neutral across languages and modalities.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Speech-text, text-speech, and speech-speech pairs are added to a multilingual inference framework and compared with similarity-based BLASER evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The framework complements evaluation methods and helps identify inconsistencies by detecting entailment and contradiction alongside semantic similarity.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports F1 gains of 0.19 for speech-speech and 0.13 for speech-text over BLASER in distinguishing entailment from non-entailment.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports F1 gains of 0.19 for speech-speech and 0.13 for speech-text over BLASER in distinguishing entailment from non-entailment.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Languages, pair construction, translations, labels, and evaluation sets bound the result; logical classification does not guarantee complete translation assessment or human usefulness.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: AttentiveMOS: A Lightweight Attention-Only Model forSpeech Quality Prediction
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use attention for local and global context in a small model, then sequentially teach it from refined targets to reduce noisy-rating effects.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: AttentiveMOS uses Swin and transformer attention with 86K parameters and is evaluated across in-domain, out-of-domain, and cross-domain MOS datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Research in modeling subjective metrics for quality assessment has led to the development of no-reference speech models that directly operate on utterance waveforms to predict the Mean Opinion Score (MOS).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: It beats listed lightweight baselines in the reported SOMOS-clean comparison, but PCC falls to 0.359 on out-of-domain LIVETALK.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: It beats listed lightweight baselines in the reported SOMOS-clean comparison, but PCC falls to 0.359 on out-of-domain LIVETALK.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: MOS labels, listener composition, dataset domains, and the sharp shift drop limit claims of general quality assessment.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Enabling the replicability of speech synthesis perceptual evaluations
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Decompose evaluation into a structured report and a recipe containing materials and decisions needed to repeat it.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Audit the goal, dataset and bias, participant cohort, protocol, analysis, conclusions, and limitations, then package evaluation assets and procedures.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: This paper evaluates subjective speech-synthesis research methodology rather than a new synthesizer: its evidence is a checklist and reproducibility-report recipe covering hypothesis, dataset bias, participant cohort, stimuli, protocol, analysis, conclusions, and limitations. The proposed evaluation object is whether another researcher can reconstruct the listening experiment; no new MOS denominator or model benchmark is claimed.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a structured template intended to make subjective speech-synthesis studies more reproducible and limitations more visible.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a structured template intended to make subjective speech-synthesis studies more reproducible and limitations more visible.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: A checklist cannot guarantee participant representativeness, perceptual validity, or exact replication when access differs.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Voice Quality Dimensions as Interpretable Primitives for Speaking Style for Atypical Speech and Affect
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train separate probes for seven voice-quality dimensions on frozen speech representations, then test cross-category and zero-shot transfer.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The frozen representation supplies a common acoustic space while lightweight probes map it to interpretable dimensions; held-out speakers and out-of-domain datasets test transfer.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Here we develop and evaluate voice quality models for seven voice and speech dimensions (intelligibility, imprecise consonants, harsh voice, naturalness, monoloudness, monopitch, and breathiness).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports strong probe performance and generalization on SAP categories, with zero-shot tests on additional languages, tasks, and affect data.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports strong probe performance and generalization on SAP categories, with zero-shot tests on additional languages, tasks, and affect data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Proxy labels, speaker/sample overlap, limited out-of-domain sets, frozen-encoder choice, and correlation metrics bound transfer; dimensional prediction is not a clinical or listener-outcome validation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multimodal and Multitask Learning for Predicting Multiple Scores in L2 English Speech
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use cross-modal attention to exchange information between speech and text and a joint loss that treats the five proficiency traits as related but distinct targets.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: MFCC, wav2vec 2.0, GloVe, and BERT embeddings are compared on five L2 English scores with a trait-aware loss and mean Pearson correlation as the main measure.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Multimodal L2-English scoring is evaluated on 29,857 Korean-learner speech samples split into 20,965 train, 4,501 validation, and 4,391 test samples. Two expert raters provide 1–5 scores for task completion, delivery, accuracy, and appropriateness; models are compared with unimodal, integrated multimodal, and independent multimodal baselines using Pearson correlation coefficient for each score and the final level. The best wav2vec2+BERT model reports average PCC 0.734 with SD 0.0129, using an in-house ASR transcript stream with 14.2% WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The wav2vec 2.0 plus BERT configuration reports the best mean PCC, 0.734 with standard deviation 0.0129 across the five criteria, above unimodal and baseline multimodal systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The wav2vec 2.0 plus BERT configuration reports the best mean PCC, 0.734 with standard deviation 0.0129 across the five criteria, above unimodal and baseline multimodal systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The learner dataset, rubric, rater scores, split, and correlation metric bound the result; correlation is not agreement or evidence that the model understands proficiency.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Aligning ASR Evaluation with Human and LLM Judgments: Intelligibility Metrics Using Phonetic, Semantic, and NLI Approaches
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Fit a metric combining natural-language inference, semantic similarity, and phonetic similarity to human ratings of ASR outputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Five-fold regression learns weights from 100 transcript pairs rated by six annotators, then tests the combined score against held-out judgments.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Traditional ASR metrics like WER and CER fail to capture intelligibility, especially for dysarthric and dysphonic speech, where semantic alignment matters more than exact word matches.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The integrated measure outperforms individual and traditional error measures in the reported SAP evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The integrated measure outperforms individual and traditional error measures in the reported SAP evaluation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: One dataset, six annotators, regression assumptions, and reported correlation limit other listeners, languages, and clinical decisions.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: On the reliability of feature attribution methods for speech classification
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Vary input type, aggregation, and perturbation timespan, then compare attribution stability, faithfulness, and agreement across speech classification tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Experiments use TIMIT and Common Voice with gradient-based saliency and integrated gradients; word-aligned and fixed-timespan perturbations are compared.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Feature attribution aims to reveal which parts of the input elements contribute the most to model outputs.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Standard approaches are generally unreliable in speech, except that word-aligned perturbations are more reliable for word-based classification tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Standard approaches are generally unreliable in speech, except that word-aligned perturbations are more reliable for word-based classification tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The models, tasks, datasets, attribution methods, and reliability definitions bound the result; no explanation method becomes a causal proof from these tests alone.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

No independent reproduction was performed.. Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Intelligibility Prediction for Time-Modified Speech Signals Using Spectro-Temporal Modulation Features: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate word-error-versus-understanding within metrics-and-targets.; Exploring Linear Variant Transformers and k-NN Memory Inference for Long-Form ASR: Long-form ASR evaluation asks whether memory and efficient inference preserve the words that matter over extended speech, not only short-utterance accuracy.; Temp4Cap: Temporally-aligned Automated Audio Captioning: Temporally aligned audio captioning needs evaluation of whether captions identify the right events at the right time, not only fluent text. concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is Listening ratings, preference tests, and signal measures estimate different aspects of whether generated or enhanced speech is acceptable. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Optimizing CLAP Reward with LLM Feedback for Semantically Aligned and Diverse Automated Audio Captioning: Optimizing an automated audio-captioning reward raises the question of whether a metric rewards semantic coverage or merely reference style.; SMARTMOS: Modeling Subjective Audio Quality Evaluation for Real-Time Applications: The paper predicts subjective audio-quality judgments for real-time use, directly addressing the gap between a cheap proxy and what listeners actually report.; Benchmarking Time-localized Explanations for Audio Classification Models: Time-localized explanations are evaluated as evidence about why an audio classifier decided, so explanation quality must be measured separately from classification accuracy. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A score without listeners, conditions, and target definition cannot support a general quality claim.

In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Benchmarking and Confidence Evaluation of LALMs For Temporal Reasoning: Confidence evaluation tests whether a spoken temporal-reasoning system knows when its answer is uncertain, not only whether its average score is high.; Towards LLM-Empowered Fine-Grained Speech Descriptors for Explainable Emotion Recognition: Fine-grained speech descriptors make an emotion claim inspectable, testing whether explanations correspond to meaningful acoustic evidence.; Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Audio Captioning with Generation-Assisted Multimodal Querying and Progressive Learning: Generation-assisted multimodal retrieval tests whether audio and text evidence agree on what should be retrieved, rather than rewarding fluent captions alone. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: Calibration on a held-out sample does not guarantee safety under a new population or distribution.

records.subtheme_name: From model score to deployed behavior
records.question: What changes when the model is placed in a real device and interaction loop?

family_synthesis.ordinary_pressure: Speech systems are used through microphones, networks, interfaces, policies, and people; a benchmark number is only one observation of that whole chain. The subtheme asks: What changes when the model is placed in a real device and interaction loop?
family_synthesis.naive_shortcut: A first attempt would answer the question only with distribution shift, but that shortcut misses the boundary: A named shift is not evidence of coverage; the shift must be measured and tied to the failure.
family_synthesis.recurring_move: Across this subtheme, papers make distribution shift, latency and resource budget, end-to-end recovery explicit rather than treating the speech evidence as one undifferentiated variable. The reviewed full-paper mechanisms instantiate that move in different ways; for example: Use annotated SFUSED speech errors to stratify WhisperX performance by error type and word position.
subtheme_boundary: A named shift is not evidence of coverage; the shift must be measured and tied to the failure.
A faster model may emit less context, reduce quality, or move cost into an unreported service.
A robust component is not an end-to-end safe system if downstream policy ignores its uncertainty.
family_synthesis.tradeoff: The recurring move must preserve the evidence relevant to the named concept without importing a neighboring concept's assumptions; the boundaries below state where that interpretation stops.
family_synthesis.reviewed_variation: Evaluating ASR Robustness to Spontaneous Speech Errors: A Study of WhisperX Using a Speech Error Database: Annotated spontaneous speech errors map where ASR crosses failure boundaries by error type and position.; Defending Speech-enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats: Speech-enabled language systems must be evaluated as an end-to-end interaction because an acoustic request can become a harmful action through later reasoning and tool use.; Pushing the Limits of End-to-End Diarization: End-to-end diarization removes hand-built intermediate labels, making the evaluation sensitive to how speaker boundaries and identities fail together.; NanoCodec: Towards High-Quality Ultra Fast Speech LLM Inference: Ultra-fast speech language model inference makes latency a first-class system constraint, with quality claims meaningful only alongside the compute and timing budget.
d3_mechanism_evidence: Use annotated SFUSED speech errors to stratify WhisperX performance by error type and word position.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Evaluating ASR Robustness to Spontaneous Speech Errors: A Study of WhisperX Using a Speech Error Database
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use annotated SFUSED speech errors to stratify WhisperX performance by error type and word position.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study evaluates sound and word errors with controlled classification variables and compares initial, medial, and final positions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The Simon Fraser University Speech Error Database (SFUSED) is a public data collection developed for linguistic and psycholinguistic research.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Sound errors have higher transcription accuracy than word errors, with position-dependent differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Sound errors have higher transcription accuracy than word errors, with position-dependent differences.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Database, annotations, WhisperX, language, and task design limit generalization.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Defending Speech-enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train with synthesized harmful and benign speech queries and test against strong white-box attacks across two model sizes and data configurations.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper develops adversarial-training methods tailored to speech-enabled language models.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We experiment with different training data configurations, and evaluate the methods on strong white-box adversarial attacks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports relative safety gains of 45%–300% in its tested settings using four hours of harmful speech with 150 hours of benign speech.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Four hours of harmful plus 150 hours of benign speech yields reported relative safety gains of 45–300% over baseline.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The two models, synthesized data, attack family, safety measure, and training recipe bound the result; robustness to unseen speakers, attacks, languages, and real-world misuse remains open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Pushing the Limits of End-to-End Diarization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use one end-to-end non-autoregressive model and scale pretraining across systematically represented eight-speaker mixtures.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: EEND-TA is evaluated on AliMeeting, AMI, DIHARD III, and MagicData RAMC with speed and diarization error comparisons.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we present state-of-the-art diarization error rates (DERs) on multiple publicly available datasets, including AliMeeting-far, AliMeeting-near, AMI-Mix, AMI-SDM, DIHARD III, and MagicData RAMC.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 14.49% DER on DIHARD III and state-of-the-art results on the listed datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 14.49% DER on DIHARD III and state-of-the-art results on the listed datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The simulations, corpora, speaker counts, and model speed define the boundary; spontaneous conditions beyond these meetings remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: NanoCodec: Towards High-Quality Ultra Fast Speech LLM Inference
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Ablate frame rate, bitrate, and causality, then design NanoCodec around a low-rate operating point and compare reconstruction quality.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The codec maps audio to discrete tokens and back; token rate controls autoregressive steps while bitrate and causal context control information and latency.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: NanoCodec outperforms related works across various bitrate ranges, establishing a new benchmark for low-latency and efficient Speech LLM training and inference.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: NanoCodec reports high-quality compression at 12.5 FPS and competitive results across bitrate ranges.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: NanoCodec reports high-quality compression at 12.5 FPS and competitive results across bitrate ranges.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Audio domain, codec training data, perceptual metric, hardware, and causality setting bound transfer; codec quality is not end-to-end speech generation quality.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Breaking Resource Barriers in Speech Emotion Recognition via Data Distillation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Distill the original emotional speech into a smaller synthesized dataset and test whether models trained on it retain emotion-recognition performance.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper proposes data distillation for resource-efficient speech emotion recognition.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Speech emotion recognition (SER) plays a crucial role in human-computer interaction.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports comparable performance to the full dataset under its fixed-initialization experiments.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports comparable SER performance between models trained on distilled and original emotional-speech data.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The distillation procedure, emotion labels, source corpora, privacy threat model, model initialization, and UAR evaluation bound the claim; smaller data is not automatically private or representative.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Multi-Channel Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Diarization: Experimental Results for The MISP 2025 Challenge
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Generate initial predictions with sequence-to-sequence neural diarization, then refine them with multi-channel audio in MC-S2SND for the MISP challenge.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The paper presents a multi-channel sequence-to-sequence neural diarization system.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The final system achieves a diarization error rate (DER) of 8.09% on the evaluation set of the competition database, ranking first place in the speaker diarization task of the MISP 2025 Challenge.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The system reports 8.09% diarization error rate on the challenge evaluation set and first place in the MISP 2025 diarization task.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The system reports 8.09% diarization error rate on the challenge evaluation set and first place in the MISP 2025 diarization task.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Challenge data, channel layout, scoring convention, enrollment assumptions, and test conditions bound generalization; rank and DER do not guarantee usable transcripts in every meeting.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unmasking real-world audio deepfakes: A data-centric approach
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Treat curation, pruning, and augmentation of real-world examples as the primary intervention, then test generalization on both an in-the-wild set and a newly collected real-world set.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The study introduces the AI4T real-world deepfake dataset, analyzes data quality and coverage, applies data-centric filtering and augmentation, and evaluates detector systems on five public datasets plus the new set.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: The growing prevalence of real-world deepfakes presents a critical challenge for existing detection systems, which are often evaluated on datasets collected just for scientific purposes.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports a 55% relative EER reduction on In-the-Wild to 1.7% absolute EER and a 63% reduction on AI4T after the data-centric interventions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports a 55% relative EER reduction on In-the-Wild to 1.7% absolute EER and a 63% reduction on AI4T after the data-centric interventions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The new dataset and curation choices define the tested notion of real-world variation; future generators and channels may differ. EER is not a guarantee of safe moderation or authentication, and no independent reproduction was performed.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: PruneSLU: Efficient On-device Spoken Language Understanding through Vocabulary and Structural Pruning
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Prune task-irrelevant vocabulary first, prune layers structurally, then refine with distillation and contrastive losses.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: PruneSLU starts from Whisper-tiny, selects a base vocabulary, chooses layers by loss, and trains with language-model, distillation, and contrastive components on STOP and SLURP.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments on the STOP and SLURP datasets demonstrate that PruneSLU compresses a 39M model to 15M while retaining 98\% of its original performance, outperforming previous compression techniques.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The 15M model retains 98% of original STOP performance, reaches STOP EM 72.31 and SLURP slot F1 71.42, and improves on listed compression baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The 15M model retains 98% of original STOP performance, reaches STOP EM 72.31 and SLURP slot F1 71.42, and improves on listed compression baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: STOP/SLURP domains, Whisper initialization, five seeds, and author-reported comparisons bound the result; energy and open-world commands are not tested.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: GTA: Towards Generative Text-To-Audio Retrieval via Multi-Scale Tokenizer
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Use a multi-scale tokenizer and generative retrieval architecture with explicit resource tradeoffs.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Coarse and fine audio tokens represent different temporal resolutions for retrieval.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Currently, mainstream approaches primarily employ a dual-tower architecture, independently encoding text and audio while performing similarity score matching.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports GTA results for generative text-to-audio retrieval.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports GTA results for generative text-to-audio retrieval.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Audio, prompts, token rates, metrics, hardware, and generation budget bound transfer.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Ultra-Low Bit Post-Training Quantization of Large Speech Models via K-Means Clustering and Mixed Precision Allocation
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Cluster weights nonlinearly, allocate more bits to columns with many outliers, and retain only critical outliers in sparse FP32 form.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The method quantizes Whisper-Large-V3 after training and compares mixed precision and outlier retention across speech datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Evaluated on Whisper-Large-V3 (1.5B parameters), our method achieves 2.12-bit quantization with only 0.17% absolute WER increase on LibriSpeech test-clean.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports 2.12-bit quantization with a 0.17 percentage-point WER increase on LibriSpeech test-clean and under 1% degradation across additional datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports 2.12-bit quantization with a 0.17 percentage-point WER increase on LibriSpeech test-clean and under 1% degradation across additional datasets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: The result is author-reported for Whisper-Large-V3 and tested corpora; latency, energy, hardware kernels, and other model families remain open.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Improving Generalization of End-to-End ASR through Diversity and Independence Regularization
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Add diversity loss to separate feature representations and independence loss to reduce covariance, then test across three ASR architectures.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: The losses operate on learned feature vectors: one discourages collapse toward similar patterns, the other discourages redundant correlated dimensions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Diversity/independence regularization is evaluated primarily with CTC, AED, and RNN-T models on LibriSpeech test-clean/test-other, measuring WER and relative error-rate reduction under Viterbi, beam, and greedy decoding without language models. CTC robustness tests use TEDLIUM2 dev/test, CHiME-3 dt/et, and KsponSpeech eval-clean/eval-other; OOD comparisons and ablations are run on CHiME-3 and TEDLIUM2. Checkpoints are selected by validation WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports improved generalization and robustness for CTC, AED, and RNN-T models in the evaluated tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports improved generalization and robustness for CTC, AED, and RNN-T models in the evaluated tasks.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Training/test shifts, loss weights, architectures, languages, and robustness protocol bound transfer; benchmark generalization is not immunity to arbitrary distribution shift.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Unfolding A Few Structures for The Many: Memory-Efficient Compression of Conformer and Speech Foundation Models
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Train a compact seed and unfold it through shared structures, using KL self-distillation between largest and seed paths.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Logical depth changes through repeated blocks sharing a seed; distillation aligns small and large outputs across paths.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Foldable Conformer and wav2vec2 compression are evaluated on NIST Hub5'00, RT02, RT03, and LibriSpeech test-clean, with WER as the principal accuracy measure and MAPSSWE at alpha 0.05 for significance. Experiments vary executed depth, layer folding, joint training, self-distillation, and comparison compression methods; averaged WER across the three conversational evaluation sets is reported for Conformer systems, while test-clean is reported for wav2vec2 systems.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The models report comparable ASR with 35% Conformer and 30% wav2vec2/HuBERT parameter reductions.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The models report comparable ASR with 35% Conformer and 30% wav2vec2/HuBERT parameter reductions.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Hardware latency, unfolding cost, family, task, and benchmark coverage bound transfer; fewer parameters is not automatically less energy.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Simultaneous Masked and Unmasked Decoding with Speculative Decoding Masking for Fast ASR without Accuracy Loss
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Combine simultaneous masked/unmasked decoding with speculative masking so confidently predictable hypotheses skip unnecessary decoder computation.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Preliminary masked decisions identify positions whose score computation can be omitted; the remaining positions retain the autoregressive search path and its result.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: These methods achieve the same recognition accuracy as Autoregressive (AR) decoding while maintaining higher computational efficiency than AR in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR).
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: On TED-LIUM2, the paper reports WER 7.3% for both the proposed and autoregressive systems, with RTF 0.41 versus 0.59.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: On TED-LIUM2, the paper reports WER 7.3% for both the proposed and autoregressive systems, with RTF 0.41 versus 0.59.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: One corpus/model, beam and hardware settings, confidence thresholds, and real-time measurement protocol bound transfer; equal WER on one test set does not prove universal speed preservation.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: SpecTokenizer: A Lightweight Streaming Codec in the Compressed Spectrum Domain
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Operate in a compressed spectral domain and combine lightweight convolutional and recurrent layers at multiple time scales.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: SpecTokenizer is a streaming single-codebook codec evaluated at 4 kbps against a lightweight codec under matched computation and storage budgets.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: SpecTokenizer is evaluated as a compressed-spectrum neural codec at 6, 4, and 0.5 kbps, with ASR WER, PESQ, STOI, SDR, Mel-spectrum loss, UTMOS, and XLSR-MOS as reported objective measures. Comparisons cover other codec models; ablations vary spectrum design, codebook size, frame rate, bitrate, and model miniaturization, with parameter/compute cost also reported. The evaluation establishes rate-distortion and intelligibility comparisons under the paper's test protocol, not broad perceptual or deployment reliability.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: At 4 kbps it reports comparable or better performance with 20% of the computation and 10% of the parameters of the comparison codec.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: At 4 kbps it reports comparable or better performance with 20% of the computation and 10% of the parameters of the comparison codec.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Bitrate, audio material, hardware, streaming definition, and quality measure bound the claim; benchmark efficiency does not prove end-to-end device power or user benefit.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Calm-Whisper: Reduce Whisper Hallucination On Non-Speech By Calming Crazy Heads Down
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Diagnose decoder self-attention heads with head-wise masking, identify a small set responsible for most non-speech hallucinations, and fine-tune those heads on non-speech data.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Ablation assigns causal responsibility at the head level; targeted fine-tuning changes the decoder’s response to acoustic absence while monitoring speech WER.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Specifically, we benchmark the contribution of each self-attentional head in the Whisper-large-v3 decoder to the hallucination problem by performing a head-wise mask.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports that three of twenty decoder heads account for most hallucinations on UrbanSound and that targeted training reduces them with limited LibriSpeech WER degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports that three of twenty decoder heads account for most hallucinations on UrbanSound and that targeted training reduces them with limited LibriSpeech WER degradation.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Non-speech corpus, head attribution, fine-tuning regime, language/model version, and WER tradeoff bound transfer; reduced hallucination is not perfect abstention or factual reliability.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: WIND: Accelerated RNN-T Decoding with Windowed Inference for Non-blank Detection
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Inspect a window of frames in parallel to locate non-blank predictions, then retain decoder logic around the informative positions for greedy and beam search.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: WIND is evaluated on multiple datasets with greedy, batched greedy, and beam-search RNN-T decoding against sequential baselines.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: We propose Windowed Inference for Non-blank Detection (WIND), a novel strategy that significantly accelerates RNN-T inference without compromising model accuracy.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: Greedy modes reach up to 2.4x speedup with identical WER, while the proposed beam search is faster and slightly more accurate than alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: Greedy modes reach up to 2.4x speedup with identical WER, while the proposed beam search is faster and slightly more accurate than alternatives.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: RNN-T models, datasets, hardware, window size, and decoding modes bound the result; reported speedup is not portable to every implementation or workload.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Effective and Efficient One-pass Compression of Speech Foundation Models Using Sparsity-aware Self-pinching Gates
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Learn a small gate for each layer during training and let the gates pinch off underused neurons while model parameters are updated at the same time.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: Self-pinching gates are trained with wav2vec2.0-base and HuBERT-large and then drive fine-grained neuron pruning on LibriSpeech-100hr.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech-100hr corpus suggest that our approach reduces the number of parameters of wav2vec2.0-base and HuBERT-large models by 65% and 60% respectively, while incurring no statistically significant word error rate (WER) increase on the test-clean dataset.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The method removes 65% of wav2vec2.0-base and 60% of HuBERT-large parameters without a statistically significant test-clean WER increase, with 7.05% WER at 4.26x compression.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The method removes 65% of wav2vec2.0-base and 60% of HuBERT-large parameters without a statistically significant test-clean WER increase, with 7.05% WER at 4.26x compression.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: LibriSpeech, model variants, pruning thresholds, and test-clean evaluation bound the result; no claim follows about noisy conditions, energy, or other languages.

d3_comparison_matrix.title: Dynamic Acoustic Model Architecture Optimization in Training for ASR
d3_comparison_matrix.central_move: Grow useful parts and drop less useful parts during training, reallocating parameters while keeping the total model complexity and training resources fixed.
d3_comparison_matrix.mechanism: DMAO is evaluated with CTC on LibriSpeech, TED-LIUM-v2, and Switchboard across architectures and model sizes.
d3_comparison_matrix.evaluation_object: In this paper, we introduce DMAO, an architecture optimization framework that employs a grow-and-drop strategy to automatically reallocate parameters during training.This reallocation shifts resources from less-utilized areas to those parts of the model where they are most beneficial.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_result: The paper reports up to roughly 6% relative WER improvement across datasets, architectures, and sizes with negligible added training overhead.
d3_comparison_matrix.reported_payoff: The paper reports the following payoff at D3 depth: The paper reports up to roughly 6% relative WER improvement across datasets, architectures, and sizes with negligible added training overhead.
d3_comparison_matrix.evidence_limit: Datasets, CTC setup, compute budget, search rules, and final architecture bound the result; a benchmark gain does not establish optimality or universal resource allocation.

family_synthesis.comparison_conclusion: The papers share the ordinary pressure but intervene at different points in the chain; their reported outcomes are not directly rankable unless the measured object and test condition match.

The shared problem is therefore compatible with more than one intervention point.

These outcomes should not be ranked unless their data, listeners, metric, and test condition are comparable.

Those are evidence boundaries, not proof that either method fails outside the paper.

It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A faster model may emit less context, reduce quality, or move cost into an unreported service.

concept_families.definition: Handle uncertainty through confirmation, correction, fallback, and logging so one recognition error does not become an irreversible action.
concept_families.boundary: A robust component is not an end-to-end safe system if downstream policy ignores its uncertainty.
concept_families.family_claim: The ordinary pressure is Handle uncertainty through confirmation, correction, fallback, and logging so one recognition error does not become an irreversible action. In the reviewed evidence, the family appears as Defending Speech-enabled LLMs Against Adversarial Jailbreak Threats: Speech-enabled language systems must be evaluated as an end-to-end interaction because an acoustic request can become a harmful action through later reasoning and tool use.; Pushing the Limits of End-to-End Diarization: End-to-end diarization removes hand-built intermediate labels, making the evaluation sensitive to how speaker boundaries and identities fail together.; Multi-Channel Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Diarization: Experimental Results for The MISP 2025 Challenge: Multi-channel diarization evaluation must reveal coupled failures in segmentation, speaker identity, and overlap rather than one isolated score. It must not be confused with neighboring problems outside this boundary: A robust component is not an end-to-end safe system if downstream policy ignores its uncertainty.
